News.title: BT delays Starlink satellite launch for Brit users after Musk ‘ordered’ Ukraine blackout leaving it defenceless
News.content:
Next

BT has delayed a huge rollout of Starlink satellites to provide broadband to remote areas of the countryside after tech mogul Elon Musk shut off its services in Ukraine.

In October, Musk blocked access to the critical tech for Volodymyr Zelensky’s forces with a ten-day freeze on its top-speed services, leaving Kyiv defenceless against Russian strikes.



BT chief exec Allison Kirkby told the Financial Times that Britain’s biggest broadband company would not launch its Starlink satellite service until “the noise has died down” about Musk after his blackout of Ukrainian services.

The BT-Starlink service is set to deliver fast Wi-Fi speeds for remote and rural areas of the UK that have long been left with snail-pace services.



Kirkby revealed that the service is “ready to launch” yet said BT was “cautious on how Starlink might be viewed at the moment considering what happened in Ukraine a couple of weeks ago”.

The telecoms boss said: “We will only launch it proactively when we feel the noise has died down a little bit on Elon Musk and Starlink as a result of the Ukraine thing.”



Kyiv’s military depends on the satellite system to guide drone fleets including interceptors used to down deadly Russian attacks.

But Musk suddenly restricted the speeds that Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network in October.

The outage struck without warning overnight as Russian forces unleashed a deadly salvo of ballistic missiles on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.

Zelensky warned the slowdown would cost lives and services were restored ten days later – but the blackout has affected Starlink’s reputation worldwide.



Kirkby added in a statement: “Offering the best products for our customers means working with the best partners.

“Starlink has far more satellites than any other operator and they are launching more each year. The demand is there and we’ll launch satellite broadband in the coming months.”

Starshield, the military arm of Musk’s Starlink, has become critical for frontline operations in Ukraine.



The SpaceX CEO initially blamed Trump for throttling the service, writing on X: “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government.

“Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.”

But the US officials told the Wall Street Journal that Musk pulled the plug on the military-grade Starlink service himself.

The tech mogul ordered the slowdown after expressing anger at recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian diesel hubs and rising fuel prices.

Some US officials claimed that Musk acted unilaterally, although one said that he talked to multiple senior White House officials, including Trump, before introducing the cap.



Sources told The Telegraph that Trump “agreed” the shutdown with Musk.

The paper reported that the billionaire tech CEO approached the president proposing speed limits in the wake of Trump lifting sanctions on Russian oil by announcing a deal with the Kremlin.

As Musk lifted the speed limits which had destroyed drone defences for Ukraine, he accused Ukraine of “violating” Starlink terms of service.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The SpaceX CEO claimed Ukraine had exploited a “loophole” to use the commercial Starlink tech for drone hits instead of the US military-controlled Starshield system.

Ukrainian defence experts said it was impossible for the commercial platforms to be used for strikes.

News.title: Chilling moment boy, 15, cries ‘someone help me as ex-classmate, 16, stabs him’ after lying in wait behind tree
News.content:
Next

THIS is the chilling moment a 15-year-old boy screams for help as he is repeatedly stabbed in a horror broad daylight attack.

His assailant allegedly lay in wait behind a tree before pouncing on the unsuspecting teen outside a school in Sydney, Australia.



Harrowing footage reveals the victim asking “what the f*** is this?” before his confusion breaks into shouts of “hey, hey, someone help me!”.

CCTV shows a boy in a black hoodie lurking near a tree – before determindly strolling across the street.



Moments later, haunting cries can be heard from across the road.

Police raced to Casula High School just before 8.30am on Monday after being told a boy had been stabbed in the stomach “multiple times”.

He was found lying on the pavement and clutching his wounds after the blade narrowly missed piercing his heart.

The boy also suffered a collapsed lung, wounds to his liver and cuts across his arms and legs.

Paramedics administered first aid before rushing him to Liverpool Hospital in serious but stable condition.

A former classmate, 16, has been accused of stabbing him with a kitchen knife before bystanders battled the teen off the alleged victim.



The 16-year-old allegedly fled and hid his knife in a bush 300m down the road.

Just four hours later, at a round 12.30pm, police arrested the teen at a Hinchinbrook home and charged him with wounding a person with intent to cause grievous bodily harm.

NSW Police Superintendent Robert Toynton said: “This is a shocking incident to occur outside a high school.”



He added: “It’s very sad that we’ve had to respond to an incident like this.”

The suspect appeared in court today – where the harrowing CCTV footage of the alleged crime was revealed.

The teenager has been denied bail and will spend Christmas behind bars until his next court appearance in January.

It comes after a knife-wielding pupil allegedly stormed a school in Poland and started knifing members of staff.

The boy, 15, was allegedly armed with three knives when he is accused of launching an attack at around 9am in Leszczydół-Nowiny.



A female caretaker, 37, died from her wounds and a further two teachers – including the head – were injured in the deadly rampage.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The stabbing spree came just one day after a teenager, 19, allegedly knifed pupils and a teacher at another Polish school.

Eight people were injured – inclduing three adults and five children.

HARRY COLE Trump’s so-called ‘Golden Age’ has come to a thundering halt – but midterms bloodbath is only the start of the fallout







Next

What just happened… and crucially what comes next?



One thing is clear, Donald Trump’s promised Golden Age has come to a thundering halt – but was it ever real?

Harry Cole Saves the West’s Midterms post-mortem is here, as the Blue Wave winners arrive in Washington DC…

The company also pledges its support to the West, making it a natural ally of the show.

Yet Trump is far from alone as a second term President getting a kicking in their sixth year of power – just ask Ronald Reagan, George W Bush or Barack Obama.

But the fallout is in full swing in Washington DC, as the White House Chief of Staff moves on, and the impeachment battles – starting with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth – begin.

The darkhorse in the race insists he’s focussing on the day job, but our experts weigh in on what to believe…

GOP Strategist Chris Johnson reckons Rubio will sit this race out.

And suddenly the Democratic bench looks as deep as the Republicans with moderates like Georgian Senator Jon Ossoff on the march.

Meanwhile the socialists insist they can now win in unexpected purple parts of America.

But what do those who know her say about her candidacy?

News.title: US army soldier arrested in UK by counter-terror cops after ‘spying for Russia’
News.content:
SOLDIER ‘SPY’ US army soldier arrested in UK by counter-terror cops after ‘spying for Russia’







Next

A MEMBER of the US army has been arrested in the UK by counter-terror cops after allegedly spying for Russia.

Cops said they arrested a 41-year-old man near Gloucester on Tuesday and he currently remains in custody at a London police station.

The Met Police said the man – who has been called a “senior soldier” of the US Armed Forces – was detained on suspicion of offences under Section 1 and Section 3 of the National Security Act 2023.

The force said that officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire as part of their investigation.





The allegations – which have been branded “serious” – relate to Russia and are not linked to any ongoing Counter Terrorism Policing investigations.

It comes after the US pulled all of its B1 bomber jets out of RAF Fairford – which is based in Gloucestershire – amid fears of “new threats” to the airbase last month.

The decision came just a week after five men were arrested over an alleged plot at the heavily guarded base, used as a launchpad for US strikes on Iran.

An offence under Section 1 of the National Security Act 2023 relates to the unauthorised acquisition and dissemination of sensitive state material.

Meanwhile, a Section 3 offence relates to engaging in conduct that intentionally or recklessly assists a foreign intelligence service.

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said: “This significant arrest and investigation is a result of close collaboration between UK and US authorities.

“The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing.

“This activity demonstrates the strength of our UK and US law enforcement and national security partnerships, and I commend the work of all the teams involved.



“We will work together to take robust action against those we suspect of any criminal activity that could undermine our national security.”

FBI Director Kash Patel said: “This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies.

“While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message – this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners.

“This includes 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests from this FBI over the last 21 months – a 53% increase.”

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, said: “The alleged conduct of a senior solider, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.



“I encourage anyone who thinks they’ve witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office.”

News.title: Brute who confronted ex with kitchen knives as she held their baby daughter jailed after being snared by cat camera
News.content:
CAUGHT OUT Brute who confronted ex with kitchen knives as she held their baby daughter jailed after being snared by cat camera







Next

A VIOLENT brute who confronted his ex with kitchen knives as she held her baby daughter has been locked up after a cat camera helped snare him.

Michael Salmon, 50, of London, was put behind bars for three years and two months at Manchester Crown Court on November 6.



He was convicted of controlling and coercive behaviour against his former partner.

Salmon’s offending escalated over a number of years, which left the victim feeling isolated, intimidated and living in fear, cops said.



His controlling behaviour consisted of monitoring her movements, repeatedly questioning where she was and demanding video calls to verify where she was and who she was with.

After the birth of their daughter, Salmon’s behaviour became increasingly possessive and aggressive.



As the police investigation progressed, the victim disclosed a number of incidents where she had been physically assaulted and subjected to threats and intimidation.

The terrifying situation came to a head on September 28, 2024, when Salmon became aggressive during a family journey and began driving erratically while the victim and their young daughter were in the vehicle.

As tensions rose, he threatened to drive the car into a wall, killing everyone inside.

Later the same say, after an argument at home, Salmon armed himself with two kitchen knives and confronted the victim while she was holding their five-month-old daughter.



He pointed the knives towards her and yelled: “She is the only one saving you now.”

The next day, September 29, the victim reported the abuse to the police which led to Salmon being arrested and later charged.

Throughout his police interview he denied the allegations but detectives were able to unearth compelling evidence that contradicted his claims.

A household cat camera, installed above a cat feeding area and intended to monitor the family’s cat while they were away from the property, captured crucial footage.

DC Grindley that led this investigation said: “This conviction reflects a sustained pattern of controlling, coercive and threatening behaviour that left the victim living in fear.

“What began as monitoring, jealousy and attempts to control everyday aspects of her life escalated into violence, intimidation and serious threats involving weapons.

“Crucially, footage captured on a household pet camera, alongside evidence provided by the victim, enabled investigators to demonstrate the reality of what was happening behind closed doors.

“I would like to commend the victim for the immense courage she has shown throughout both the investigation and court process.

“Her bravery in coming forward has ensured a dangerous offender has been brought to justice.



“I hope this outcome reassures victims of domestic abuse that they will be listened to, believed and supported. No one should have to live in fear in their own home or relationship.

News.title: Twisted woman, 30, who killed her ex’s son, 8, & Googled whether wild boars eat dead bodies is jailed for life
News.content:
BEHIND BARS Twisted woman, 30, who killed her ex’s son, 8, & Googled whether wild boars eat dead bodies is jailed for life







Next

A TWISTED woman who murdered her ex-boyfriend’s eight-year-old son then Googled whether wild boars eat dead bodies has been sentenced to life in prison.

Gina H, 30, lured the child from his mum’s flat to a pond, stabbed him to death and set his body on fire, the court heard.



She was arrested after she claimed to have found the body of Fabian, eight, at the edge of a pond in Gustrow, northern Germany in October 2025.

The child had disappeared from his home four days earlier.



On Tuesday she was found guilty of murder and handed a sentence of life in prison after a 34-day trial in Rostock Regional Court.

Judge Holger Schuett gave the sentence and verdict after hearing evidence from 75 witnesses and nine experts.

She is not likely to be eligible to be released on parole after 15 years because of the seriousness of the crime.

Gina had been in a relationship with the boy’s dad, Matthias R., for around four years, but he had broken up with her in August 2025.



Prosecutors said she felt the child was getting between her and Matthias, and wanted to punish her ex for breaking up with her.

On the day Fabian disappeared, he had stayed home from school because he was ill.

The court heard Gina lured Fabian out of his mum’s home and took him to an isolated pond.



She then murdered the child, with prosecutors saying she stabbed him at least six times before setting his body alight with a flammable liquid.

On the evening of October 10, 2025, when little Fabian was first reported missing, Gina asked the boy’s dad in text messages whether anything had happened at home, the court heard.

She Googled “police” and “police news“, before searching whether wild boars eat dead people the day after her ex-partner’s son disappeared, the court was told.

She allegedly searched “do wild boars eat people” and “do wild boars eat dead people” at 8:01am.

In a terrifying voice message played to the court, after Gina was asked about what had happened to Fabian, she could be heard saying: “Well, you’ll never really know, will you?



“Because bodies found in water don’t leave any DNA traces.

“Neither do bodies from fires; they won’t leave many DNA traces either, unfortunately.”

Gina continues to deny all charges, telling the court in her final statement: “I am innocent. Fabian was like my second child.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She still has the right to appeal before the sentence is finalised and vowed to fight the conviction.

News.title: Final bin collection warning for over 220,000 households in England ahead of winter break
News.content:
Next

OVER 220,000 Brits have been issued a final bin warning in England ahead of winter break.

The last round of collections will start from next Monday for residents in certain councils as the festive season puts a pause to services.

Councils are reminding UK residents that the final brown bin collections will begin from next week – before pausing for 11 weeks.



This year, Leeds City Council said the last round of collections will start from November 16, with the final scheduled collection day being November 28.



Affecting more than 220,000 households in the area, the authority noted that those in the Wetherby area who receive a combined food and garden waste collection will continue to have their brown bins emptied.

Meanwhile, councils including Warrington, Stroud, Bath and North East Somerset and Leicester, will hold their final collections between November 23 and December 4.

Garden waste collections are paused annually during the winter months due to diminished demand, and usually start again the following spring.



However, residents can check through their council’s website to find out when their final collection date will be in their area.

In the meantime, Brits are encouraged to compost any garden waste at home by adding level layers of leaves, garden prunings and grass cuttings to the top layer of their soil.

In the spring, this composted material can be used as a nutrient-rich soil for March blooms.

Alternatively, garden waste can still be taken to any council-run local household waste recycling centres for free.



Those who wish to restart their garden waste collections in the new year are also reminded to visit their council’s 2027 subscription page.

News.title: New footage in search for missing dad-of-3 DoorDash driver shows his car left abandoned as cops piece together timeline
News.content:
Next

NEW surveillance footage has emerged in the mysterious disappearance of a DoorDash driver and dad-of-three, showing someone abandoning his car before walking away into the night.

Zachariah Schuck, 32, vanished on October 22 after completing a food delivery in Pennsylvania, leaving his family desperate for answers more than two weeks later.



The black-and-white footage, captured by a home’s doorbell camera on Croxall Avenue in Hopewell Township, shows a vehicle identified as Zachariah’s black Chevrolet Impala pulling up and parking along the road.

Moments later, a person can be seen getting out of the driver’s seat and walking down the street, leaving the vehicle behind.



The footage was shown by local news station WPXI-TV, also known as Channel 11, on Monday, as police revealed a more detailed timeline of Zachariah’s final known movements.

The footage is not clear enough to positively identify the individual, leaving police and the missing man’s family unable to determine what happened in the moments leading up to the vehicle being abandoned.

The U.S. Sun spoke to Zachariah’s father, Carl, who said his son completed a DoorDash delivery to a home in Beaver County shortly before 7 pm.

Around an hour later, the doorbell camera captured his vehicle being parked in Hopewell Township, leaving a critical gap in his movements that investigators are now attempting to piece together.

Zachariah had been in contact with his wife, Jenn, that evening and reportedly reassured her that he was heading home after finishing his deliveries.

But he never returned, and police said his cellphone lost coverage at approximately 8 pm, around the same time his car was seen being abandoned.



His father told The U.S. Sun that his son’s black Chevrolet Impala was eventually discovered on October 24 after information about the vehicle circulated on social media.

Investigators examined the car and discovered that its keys had been left in the ignition, while the gas tank was completely empty.

Carl said the mystery surrounding the person in the footage had left him struggling to establish where searches should be focused.



“Once we can identify who got out of the vehicle, then we could determine what to do next,” he told The U.S. Sun.

“They have not identified who got out of that vehicle. I can’t verify where to start searching.”

The worried father admitted he fears his son may have either walked away voluntarily or fallen victim to a crime.

“There’s two ways to look at it. Either he had an emotional event and left, or something happened to him that’s criminal,” Carl said.

Carl is urging people living in the area to check their own security cameras for anything that could help establish who was driving the Impala or where the individual went afterward.



Police have since carried out extensive searches around Croxall Avenue and nearby wooded areas, deploying drones and search-and-rescue dogs, but have found no trace of the missing driver.

Another crucial part of the investigation centers on the Vanport Bridge, where Zachariah’s wife told authorities she had last tracked his location using the Life360 app.

Pennsylvania State Police searched the bridge area on the night he disappeared but failed to locate Zachariah or his cellphone, according to North Sewickley Township Police Chief Tyler Kelosky.

Kelosky has confirmed that investigators are examining all possibilities, including whether foul play may have been involved, but stressed that police do not want to jump to conclusions without evidence.

Meanwhile, Carl previously revealed to The U.S. Sun that Zachariah had recently lost his job managing truck-leasing branches and had been experiencing financial difficulties.



Despite those challenges, the father insisted there had been no obvious warning signs that his son was struggling emotionally, describing him as someone who generally remained positive even during difficult times.

Zachariah, whose family includes a newborn baby, is described as six feet tall, weighing around 160 pounds, with brown hair and green eyes.

He was last reported wearing a blue-and-red flannel shirt, blue jeans, and brown boots.

As detectives continue examining the footage and reconstructing his final known movements, his family remains desperate to establish whether he walked away from the vehicle himself or something more sinister happened.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He has all of our support. And all we want is for him to come home. And then we can work everything out,” Carl told The U.S. Sun.



Anyone with information is urged to contact the North Sewickley Township Police Department at 724-843-3421 or 724-843-8118.

News.title: US Army soldier arrested by UK terror cops over alleged espionage linked to Russia
News.content:
US Army soldier arrested by UK terror cops over alleged espionage linked to Russia

The 41-year-old US Army senior soldier was arrested today in Gloucester following a collaboration between authorities in the UK and the US

View Image The arrest took place in Gloucester (Image: ANNA SZILAGYI/EPA/Shutterstock)

A member of the US Army has been arrested in Britain by counter-terror police as part of a major investigation into alleged espionage linked to Russia.

‌



‌



The 41-year-old senior soldier was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday, November 10, on suspicion of offences under the National Security Act 2023. The arrest followed an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing in the UK, in collaboration with the US Military and the FBI.

‌



The suspect was arrested on suspicion of offences under Section 1 and Section 3 of the National Security Act 2023, the Metropolitan Police said. Searches are being carried out at two locations in Gloucestershire as part of the investigation.

‌



Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "This significant arrest and investigation is a result of close collaboration between UK and US authorities. The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing.

"This activity demonstrates the strength of our UK and US law enforcement and national security partnerships, and I commend the work of all the teams involved. We will work together to take robust action against those we suspect of any criminal activity that could undermine our national security."

‌



The Met added that the investigation is not linked to any other ongoing probes by Counter Terrorism Policing. The suspect remains in custody at a London Police station, with the investigation led by officers from Counter Terrorism Policing London.

FBI Director Kash Patel said: "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies. While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message – this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners."

‌



Mr Patel explained that the FBI has carried out 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests in the last 21 months. He said: "This matter shows that partnerships are essential to protect our countries and I want to express my thanks to UK Counter Terrorism Policing, MI5, UK Defence Counter Intelligence, and the US Army Counterintelligence Command for their outstanding work."

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command, said: "This case demonstrates the strength of our partnerships and the resolve of the counterintelligence community. I am grateful to the UK and the FBI for their professionalism and teamwork throughout this investigation.

Article continues below

"The alleged conduct of a senior solider, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent. I encourage anyone who thinks they’ve witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office."

News.title: Met Office warns 10 areas face polar vortex snow this Thursday - see the full list
News.content:
Met Office warns 10 areas face polar vortex snow this Thursday - see the full list

The Met Office has warned of disturbances to the stratospheric polar vortex as snow showers are expected to hit parts of northern Scotland and the Northern Isles in the early hours of Thursday

View 3 Images Snow is forecast in some areas this week (Image: Getty)

Ten regions could experience snowfall on Thursday as chilly conditions start to spread across the UK, according to the Met Office.

‌



‌



The weather service said snow showers may appear in parts of northern Scotland and the Northern Isles during the early hours. This follows the Met Office's warning last week regarding disturbances to the stratospheric polar vortex high above the Arctic. Experts indicated there are signs that a sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) - which can increase the chances of an extended dry, cold period of weather in Britain - is "developing".

‌



In a forecast issued on Monday, Met Office Chief Meteorologist Jason Kelly said: "Snow showers could briefly fall on lower ground in northern Scotland and the Northern Isles, mainly Shetland, overnight on Wednesday and into Thursday."

‌



He noted that snow may only settle on higher ground, adding this is "relatively normal for the time of year".

Urgent toxic air warning issued as air quality map turns red and purple over London READ MORE :

View 3 Images A weather map shows forecast temperatures at 6am on Friday (Image: Netweather)

The mercury reached 14C on the Isles of Scilly on Monday, but a "risk to life" cold weather alert has now been issued for the UK. Netweather forecast maps suggest temperatures at 6am on Friday could be around 0C or below freezing across much of the UK, with some parts of the West Midlands seeing temperatures as low as -4C.

‌



Met Office weather maps appear to support the broader outlook, although they suggest temperatures in some areas, particularly along the coast, could be slightly higher, at around 1C to 2C.

Chillier and progressively frostier conditions are anticipated to move southwards as the week progresses, following a damp and foggy beginning for many areas. The Met Office said colder air is expected to move further south across the UK through Thursday and Friday.

‌



View 3 Images Fog covers Durham Cathedral today (Image: Owen Humphreys/Press Association)

Most locations will turn dry with some clear or sunny intervals, the forecaster said. Showers may still occur in northern and eastern areas, with some wintry showers over elevated ground in Scotland.

‌



Temperatures are set to fall below average widely by Thursday, and "particularly" by Friday, the Met Office has warned, as frost becomes increasingly widespread. The forecaster noted that the north-east is likely to bear the brunt of the chill during "stronger winds".

Come the weekend, temperatures are expected to creep back towards seasonal norms, with the possibility of some rainfall as high pressure shifts towards mainland Europe. The Met Office's forecast for Thursday to Saturday reads: "Feeling markedly colder with frosty nights ahead. Largely dry with plenty of autumnal sunshine, though showers around the coasts and wintry showers in the far north with strong winds."

News.title: Mum, dad and son, 14, killed in M5 crash as car seen going over 100mph, inquest hears
News.content:
Mum, dad and son, 14, killed in M5 crash as car seen going over 100mph, inquest hears

Andrew Moore, 46, Swala Harling, 47, and Sebastian Moore, 14, died in the 100mph crash on the M5 in South Gloucestershire

View Image Swala Harding, Andy Moore (middle) and Sebastian Moore were killed in the crash (Image: Chesterfield Panthers RUFC sports facility)

A teenager and his parents were killed when their car travelling at more than 100mph crashed on a motorway, an inquest has heard.

‌



‌



Andrew Moore, 46, Swala Harling, 47, and Sebastian Moore, 14, were killed when their BMW left the northbound carriageway of the M5 in South Gloucestershire on the evening of May 30 last year.

‌



Eyewitnesses described seeing the estate car undertaking, crossing lanes of the motorway and driving up the hard shoulder at high speed.

‌



Avon Coroner’s Court heard the BMW was seen to swerve across the motorway, collide with a crash barrier and travel down an embankment and crash into trees.

Driver Mr Moore, his partner who was a front-seat passenger, and their son, who was a nearside passenger, were all declared dead at the scene.

Area coroner Dr Peter Harrowing said that although Mr Moore suffered with epilepsy, had undergone an aortic valve replacement and had a pacemaker fitted, there was not enough evidence to support a conclusion he had suffered a medical episode.

‌



The inquest heard evidence from several motorists who had witnessed the manner of Mr Moore’s driving that evening.

Andrew Robiliard said the BMW had passed him at speed in the outside lane of the motorway, and then crossed lanes to drive onto the hard shoulder to undertake lorries.

‌



“I would estimate the speed at over 100mph,” he said.

Lorry driver Adam Norris said he was “shocked” to see the car undertake him on the hard shoulder.

‌



“I would estimate it between 100mph and 120mph. It could even be as much as 130mph,” he said.

Joshua Jack estimated the car was driving at a speed of around 140mph.

‌



“It was travelling very fast and had thrown up debris from the hard shoulder, which covered my car,” he said.

Another motorist, Andrew Harding, said: “Not only was the car driving fast, but I could see it had its hazard lights on.

‌



“I formed the opinion it appeared like someone apart from the driver was trying to steer.

“By this I mean it appeared that whoever was in control of the car was over-compensating, causing the car to swerve from side to side.”

‌



From his rear-view mirror, motorist Ali Shabaz saw the BMW crash.

“I can only describe this collision as like an explosion, with a big cloud of smoke followed by car parts being thrown everywhere,” he said.

‌



Lorry driver Peter Bakowsky also witnessed the crash and told the court: “In a matter of seconds, I saw the vehicle brake lights come on and heard tyres screeching, before watching the vehicle crash into the barriers landing in a field.

“The next thing I remember is a cloud of dust and parts of the vehicle scattered across the motorway.”

‌



Another lorry driver Jurgens Terblanche was on the southbound carriageway when he saw the crash.

“I then saw the white car speed direct into and collide with the barrier with a massive force, and the car pitched upwards and went airborne towards several trees just off the motorway,” he said.

‌



“I would describe it travelling some distance airborne before it collides with the trees and dropped into what looked like a ravine off the motorway.”

The emergency services went to the scene, but the three occupants of the car, from Chesterfield, Derbyshire, were declared dead soon after.

‌



The court heard that collision investigators were unable to say whether there were any faults or defects with the BMW due to the damage sustained.

Post-mortem examinations found that Mr Moore, a mechanic, died from multiple injuries, while Ms Harling, an IT worker, also died from multiple injuries, while Sebastian’s cause of death was given as head injuries.

‌



Toxicology tests for Mr Moore were negative for drugs and alcohol, and his heart and brain were examined by experts but “again nothing of note was found that caused or contributed to the death”, the coroner said.

“It is not for me to answer a question of why,” Dr Harrowing said.

‌



“There is insufficient evidence before me to indicate that this was a deliberate act on the part of Mr Moore in driving the vehicle in the manner in which he had driven.

“It has not been possible to identify whether there were any mechanical defects.

‌



“He may have suffered a medical episode at the time, but there is insufficient evidence for me to make a finding in that respect.

“Therefore, as to why the vehicle was being driven in the manner it was driven, there is insufficient evidence for me to reach a conclusion on the balance of probabilities.”

Article continues below

The coroner recorded conclusions of deaths caused by a road traffic collision.

News.title: Deliveroo 100 celebrates 10th anniversary - as top trending item of 2026 named
News.content:
Deliveroo 100 celebrates 10th anniversary - as top trending item of 2026 named

Deliveroo has revealed the UK’s most in-demand order, and the global number one, as it marks 10 years of its Deliveroo 100 list.

View 3 Images The delivery services celebrates 10 years of its Deliveroo 100 (Image: Deliveroo)

Deliveroo has unveiled its annual Deliveroo 100 – marking ten years of its countdown of the most-trending orders on the app – and this year’s UK winner is officially the coolest yet. From Brexit and royal weddings to Tiger King, Brat summer and the World Cup, the Deliveroo 100 has spent a decade reflecting what Britain has been ordering through some of the country’s biggest cultural moments.

‌



‌



Since it launched in 2016, the list has charted changing tastes, cravings and shopping habits across the UK, and this year’s top pick shows how quickly those habits can shift with the weather.

‌



View 3 Images 2026 is the first year a grocery item has made number one in the UK (Image: Deliveroo)

‌



In a year of soaring temperatures, Premium 2kg Ice Cubes from Iceland in London have been crowned the UK’s number one most-trending order of 2026 – the first time a grocery item has topped the UK Deliveroo 100 in the list’s ten-year history.

Ice also finished second globally, beating protein-packed bowls, pizzas and sandwiches from around the world – missing out on the top spot only to a Build Your Own Signature Plate from Dayz in Paris.

This year’s UK list was anything but ordinary, featuring a gloriously mixed bag of dishes, treats and everyday essentials. And while ice took the crown, traditional takeaway favourites still proved hugely popular, with Monte Forte Neapolitan Pizza’s Diavola taking second place in the UK and seventh globally.

‌



A spokesperson from Monte Forte Neapolitan Pizza said: “We’re incredibly proud that our Diavola from Monte Forte in Horsham has made the Deliveroo 100. Seeing it alongside some of the biggest names in the world is a bit surreal.

“Our team puts so much care into every pizza, and knowing our customers keep coming back for it makes this recognition even sweeter. A huge thank you to everyone who’s ordered, to our brilliant team.”

‌



View 3 Images Elsewhere the list was packed with protein (Image: Deliveroo)

While ice stole the show in the UK, 2026 was the year of “protein-maxxing” globally. Chicken featured in more than 20 of the world’s 100 most-trending items, with protein-heavy dishes including beef bowls, steak sandwiches and fish biryani also making the list – signalling the trend shows no sign of slowing down.

‌



Food analysts at Innova named “powerhouse protein” the number one food trend of 2026. At least 20 dishes feature chicken or other protein, from Dubai’s wings to Milan’s cashew chicken, while a Beef Power Bowl, a steak sandwich and a fish biryani all flex their way onto the list.

Meanwhile, grocery and retail items make up the biggest share of the list to date (10%) – from 2kg bags of ice, flowers and golden kiwis in the UK, to watermelon in Belgium and deodorant and toothpaste in Ireland – as more consumers turn to Deliveroo for much more than a classic Friday-night takeaway.

‌



Jeff Wemyss, VP and General Manager for UK & Ireland, said: “As the Deliveroo 100 turns ten, it’s a big change from 2016, when this was a list of restaurant dishes. Today the same app brings you a post-gym beef bowl, a 2kg bag of ice in a heatwave or tights before a night out, whatever the moment.”

UK’s top 10 trending orders of 2026:

Premium 2kg Ice Cubes, Iceland, London Diavola Pizza, Monte Forte Neapolitan Pizza, Horsham Chilli Broccoli Salad, Dishoom, Manchester Morrisons Mango Sorbet, Morrisons, Glasgow House Cheeseburger, Supernova, London Clarityn Allergy 10mg Tablets (20), Boots Pharmacy, London Quesadilla, La Choza, Brighton Charred Corn, Nando’s, London Chicken Yeeros, Mythos, Leeds Prawn & Pork Spicy Wonton, Din Tai Fung, London

News.title: Three celebs who came out in support of Russell Brand after rape conviction
News.content:
Three celebs who came out in support of Russell Brand after rape conviction

Despite Russell Brand's rape conviction and subsequent 10 year prison sentence, three celebrities have come out in support of the comedian.

View 4 Images Russell Brand has been convicted of rape (Image: Shutterstock)

Three celebrities have spoken in support of Russell Brand after he was convicted of rape and sexual assault.

Though the comedian has now begun a 10 and a half year sentence after being found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, a small group of high-profile figures have continued to say supportive things about him, with one even saying she did not believe he was guilty.

One was Megyn Kelly, who previously spoke out about the sexual harassment and misconduct at Fox News and called the Me Too Movement a "watershed moment in history".

During an episode of The Megyn Kelly Show, on the day the guilty verdicts came through, said: "I had a very difficult time believing that he was capable of rape, as I do right now. I don't believe these charges. I'm going to be honest. I don't.

View 4 Images Megyn Kelly has spoken out in support of Russell Brand (Image: Getty Images)

"I believe he dearly loves his wife Laura, his children, and, as I said, I think he has found God and he's asked for forgiveness from a lifestyle that he completely rejects now."

She added that he was an "utterly charming guy" and said his sentence was an "outrage" that was part of a "political witch hunt", claiming that Brand was targeted for being a "conservative stalwart".

Despite having previously encouraged women to come forward about sexual assault, telling women at a Time Person of the Year panel that "we are all there with you", Kelly dismissed the victims' accounts as: "Grabbing boobs, kissing, sniffing, and having that kind of sex with a woman who consented to vaginal sex with him seconds beforehand, and also had clearly been joking with him.”

View 4 Images Elon Musk tweeted in favour of Brand (Image: AP Photo/Matt Rourke)

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Elon Musk also showed support for Brand by responding to a fan's comment. The fan wrote on X: "So using the Russell Brand case as precedent, any woman can wait 20+ years and then go to police and say the sex she had on a particular night all those years ago wasn't consensual so the guy is then guilty. We're living in the twilight zone."

Musk agreed that it was a "crazy legal standard" and remarked that the 10 years sentence was, compared to another sentence shared by a different user, "unjust".

GB News host Neil Oliver came under fire after he re-shared a tweet from 2025. In the post, he was seen with Brand and wrote that the comedian was his "friend". When resharing it, the day after his verdict was handed down, Oliver wrote: "Still is."

View 4 Images Neil Oliver wrote that he was still friends with Brand (Image: @thecoastguy/X)

Other X users responded with disgust. One said: "Still is. And a jury just found him guilty of rape and sexual assault."

Brand was found guilty of multiple counts of sexual assault and one of rape. He was told he would be on the sex offenders register for life and must serve at least seven years of his sentence before being considered for release.

News.title: Jonathan Ross joked about David Walliams ‘going home with 15 year old’ at 2004 awards
News.content:
Jonathan Ross joked about David Walliams ‘going home with 15 year old’ at 2004 awards

At a 2004 awards show, Jonathan Ross made a joke about David Walliams going home with a 15 year old, in a clip that has resurfaced in a documentary about the author's behaviour towards teenagers and young women

David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct by multiple women

In a documentary on David Walliams' alleged 'predatory' behaviour towards teenage girls and young women, a clip of Jonathan Ross joking about the author and 15 year olds has resurfaced.

‌



The joke was made as part of the 2004 National Comedy Awards but shown in ITV News' documentary David Walliams: Power and Silence, which airs on ITVX and ITV1 tonight.

At the awards, Ross said: "The comedy awards is 15 years old - 15 years old! And like most 15 year olds, it's drunk, it's unpredictable and it's probably going home with David Walliams!"

The camera then cut to Walliams, who was sat with his Little Britain co-star Matt Lucas, and stuck two fingers up at Ross, whilst laughing. Ross has since said, via lawyers, that he did not write the joke and merely read it.

View 4 Images David Walliams was seen laughing while giving two fingers to the host (Image: ITV)

Labour suspends David Walliams as party member over misconduct allegations READ MORE :

The clip was used as part of a documentary put together by ITV News and The Guardian, which investigated Walliams' behaviour towards young women and teenage girls.

In the documentary, several women shared allegations about the author, including one who alleged that he sexually assaulted her when she was 15.

'Jade' said she met him after he privately messaged her on MySpace and subsequently met him in a cafe, where, she alleged, he asked her about whether she had ever had sex. "I said I hadn’t. I didn’t like talking about that kind of stuff," Jade added.

Jade continued to say that after they finished their coffees, Walliams offered to walk her to a tube station and kissed her down a side street. After the kiss, Jade claims Walliams invited her back to his house where he groped her inside and tried to put her hand in his trousers. '

View 4 Images 'Jade' (right) says Walliams first contacted her on social media platform MySpace

"I wasn't ready for sex," Jade said. "I didn't want to do that, with him or with anyone. I didn't want to be touched in that way at all. I mean, I was only a 15-year-old.” Walliams strongly denied this.

Other allegations against Walliams include grooming a girl he met when she was 15, another he met when she was 18 and "vulnerable" and plying a teenager with alcohol in order to have sex with her. The documentary also discussed allegations that he harassed women who worked on Britain's Got Talent and women working for former publisher Harper Collins.

Walliams has denied all wrongdoing. In a letter addressed to the journalists working on the investigation, Walliams wrote: “Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with. I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

View 4 Images Walliams has denied the allegations against him (Image: AP Photo/Scott A Garfitt)

“And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.

“I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

‌



It has also been revealed that Walliams was the unnamed celebrity who took legal action against Independent Television News (ITN) and Guardian News and Media (GNM), publisher of The Guardian, to prevent publication of the allegations. The court heard they intended to report his alleged "abuse of power and status" to contact young women and try to engage in "inappropriate and exploitative sexual activities”.

Walliams, who has always denied the claims, was seeking an injunction to prevent this broadcast and publication because of a risk that he would take his own life, following two previous suicide attempts.

‌



View 4 Images David Walliams is the subject of a ITV documentary (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

Judge Mr Justice Nicklin denied the injunction on November 3, and his legal team decided not to appeal before the deadline ended today, which means Walliams can be named as the man at the centre of the case.

Article continues below

The Metropolitan Police said it has contacted the Guardian and ITV News to “to ensure that any potential victims” are “made aware of how they could report any criminal allegations to police”, after claims of sexual misconduct were made against Walliams.

News.title: Eight injured with seven in hospital after car ploughs into pedestrians in Glasgow
News.content:
Eight injured with seven in hospital after car ploughs into pedestrians in Glasgow

The incident was reported on Hyndland Road in western Glasgow this afternoon, with motorists asked to avoid the area and emergency services still at the scene

View 3 Images Emergency services at the scene on Hyndland Road (Image: David Donaldson/Daily Record)

Eight people have been injured after a car ploughed into pedestrians on a busy road in Glasgow.

‌



‌



The incident was reported on Hyndland Road at around 3.45pm today, which is still closed with a police cordon in place as emergency crews attend the scene. Seven people were taken to hospital for treatment and assessment, with the driver also checked by paramedics at the scene.

‌



A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "Hyndland Road in Glasgow is closed following a crash involving a car and a number of pedestrians which happened around 3.45pm on Tuesday, 10 November. Emergency services are at the scene and drivers are urged to avoid the area."

‌



View 3 Images The scene on Hyndland Road (Image: Andrew Milligan/Press Association)

Emergency crews from Police Scotland, the Scottish Ambulance Service and Scottish Fire and Rescue Service are all in attendance. The extent of injuries sustained in the collision are unknown as of yet, the Daily Record reports. Enquiries into the incident are ongoing and the crash is being treated as a road traffic collision.

‌



Glasgow City Council said Hyndland Road was closed between Clarence Drive and Novar Drive. The council said: "Road users are advised to avoid the area and consider alternative routes."

View 3 Images Emergency crews at the scene (Image: Fraser Boag/Press Association)

Article continues below

One eyewitness spoke about how they were passing by the scene just moments after the crash happened. They said: "[It is a] terrible scene. Several [were] injured. Thankfully it happened in front of two GP surgeries so medics [were] there instantly. Prayers for all the injured and their families, as well as the wonderful people who were assisting the injured."

Unconfirmed reports suggest the vehicle may have hit a bus stop before overturning and colliding with the pedestrians.

News.title: Senior US soldier arrested by UK counter-terror police
News.content:
A senior soldier in the US Army has been arrested by British counter-terrorism police.

The 41-year-old man was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday, on suspicion of offences under the National Security Act, the Metropolitan Police said.

The force said the allegations related to Russia. The FBI said the arrest involves allegations of espionage.

As part of the investigation, officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire.

Counter-terrorism police in the UK is working closely with the US military and the FBI.

FBI director Kash Patel said in a statement: "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies."

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, from Counter Terrorism Policing, described the arrest as "significant".

"The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing," she said.

Brig Gen Sean Stinchon, commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command, said: "The alleged conduct of a senior solider, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.

"I encourage anyone who thinks they've witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office."

News.title: Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up
News.content:
The dangers in Slovyansk are clear from the start.

"If I say run, you run," Tetiana tells us. She and her colleague Yasha are escorting us into a city now under constant bombardment from Russian drones, missiles and glide bombs.

It is raining and cloudy as we enter the city, and our military escorts call this "good" weather, meaning it is bad for drones.

But the threat is still there, and Yasha keeps his eyes peeled on the skies, while 21-year-old Tetiana scours her phone for the latest military intelligence on likely threats from the air.

They are members of a drone unit who call themselves Peaky Blinders and their distinctive emblem is a flat cap of the type made popular by the cult BBC TV series, although theirs are camouflaged.

Slovyansk is one of four cities that make up Ukraine's "fortress belt" - a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the parts of eastern region of Donetsk still under its control.

Russia wants Kyiv to give up the fortress cities and they are central to talks on a possible peace deal that have resumed after nine months between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi.

Ukrainians worry that doing so would make it much easier for Russia to advance further west, including to the capital Kyiv.

News.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
News.content:
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.

One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.

Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.

A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother, Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.

Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.

Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.

In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.

"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."

The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.

"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.

"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."

The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.

"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."

The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line.

News.title: Train attack driver's '10 seconds' to change line
News.content:
The driver of a high-speed train where a mass stabbing took place said he had "probably about 10 seconds" to decide to switch to the slow line before making an unscheduled stop.

Andrew Johnson was driving the London-bound LNER service on 1 November last year when the train stopped at Huntingdon in Cambridgeshire.

Giving evidence, Johnson told jurors at Cambridge Crown Court he heard someone on the intercom "screaming 'there's a knifeman stabbing people'".

Anthony Williams, 33, of Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder on the train.

He is also charged with four other attempted murders following earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

News.title: Watch: Meghan's first public appearance since father arrested
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has made her first public appearance since her father, Thomas Markle, was charged with the possession of child sex abuse material.

Meghan arrived at the European Parliament in Brussels with her husband, Prince Harry, who delivered a speech about online child safety.

During his address, Harry said he and his wife stood alongside parents who had lost children to online harm

The BBC's Jessica Parker has this report.

More on Harry and Meghan's Brussels visit.

News.title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
News.content:
Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.

Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.

The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.

However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.

The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.

Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.

After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.

"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.

"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.

Sales of tinned and jarred goods rose from Â£58.2m in the 10 days to 2 November 2025 to Â£79.5m over the same period in 2026.

Bottled water sales jumped from Â£13.6m to Â£22.8m compared with a year earlier and hand sanitiser sales climbed from Â£497,000 to Â£908,000.

News.title: More than 12 US military aircraft leave second UK base
News.content:
Retired Royal Air Force Air Marshal Greg Bagwell told BBC Verify "we need to keep an open mind" about the reasons behind the US aircraft movements.

He suggested they could be the result of an exercise, or because the weather forecast meant it was safer to move the aircraft to other bases ahead of planned deployments elsewhere.

Bagwell said the decision may also have been taken because of a hoax as part of "nuisance hybrid warfare" by countries like Iran - or it could be a genuine threat.

He said the aircraft being dispersed to several bases could indicate the US was spreading them around to keep them safe and the moves have been "triggered by something".

Bagwell added that the reason "we haven't seen an attack succeed or even happen" could be that "maybe our intelligence and our security is better than people might believe".

Monday's departures from Mildenhall follow a security incident at RAF Fairford, a US-operated airbase in Gloucestershire.

A major incident was declared after three suspicious vans were seen near that base in September. It later emerged that the US had pulled its bombers from there and returned them to America.

Two British nationals appeared in court in October in connection with an alleged Iran-linked plot.

Seven men have been arrested as part of the investigation, Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed to the BBC on Tuesday, while an eighth has been interviewed under caution and since charged under Section 3 of the National Security Act 2023.

Iran has previously said that it considered UK bases used by the US for military strikes to be "legitimate targets".

Additional reporting by Nick Johnson at RAF Mildenhall, and Rob Corp, BBC Verify.

News.title: Analysis: Hegseth fights for his political life with appeal to Trump
News.content:
There was plenty of defiance and rhetorical venom from Pete Hegseth at the Pentagon on Tuesday, as the under-pressure US defence secretary gave his first news conference in six months.

Much of his ire was directed at the Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, who has brought articles of impeachment against him. Hegseth dismissed him as "one disgruntled and defeated congressman" who was leading a "farce and a stunt".

But this was, in many ways, a news conference with an audience of one - President Donald Trump.

Again and again, Hegseth tied his fate to that of the president.

The military operations in Iran and Venezuela that are now at the centre of impeachment proceedings, he said, were "ordered by the commander-in-chief, then ordered by myself". If standing with the president put him in the firing line, he added, "I'll take that company every day of the week".

That positioning matters.

Hegseth has frequently echoed the president's rhetoric and public statements and he did it repeatedly on Tuesday. Attacks on the media, denunciations of political enemies and even reflecting the very words the president uses.

Referring to Trump's 2019 impeachment over a call with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky, Hegseth described it as a "perfect phone call" â the exact formulation the president has used when discussing the issue.

News.title: Met Police investigating more 'potential criminal allegations' about Brand
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police have said several people contacted them during the trial and following the conviction and sentencing of the disgraced comedian Russell Brand, "to provide information or report a potential criminal allegation".

A Met spokesperson said: "Detectives are assessing this information as part of their ongoing enquiries."

Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Det Supt Andy Furphy, who led the Brand investigation, said officers were "looking at exactly what we've got" and "whether they're information that points to behaviour or whether they could constitute a criminal offence".

Brand is already being investigated over rape allegations from two more women. He has been interviewed under caution in connection to those allegations.

News.title: Carrick's Man Utd future to be decided as Berrada and Wilcox retain support
News.content:
Looking back, the 48 hours before United's season-opening match at Hull were pivotal.

With Benjamin Sesko still trying to ease his way back from the shin issue that ended his previous campaign early, Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out for seven weeks. It meant Carrick was deprived of his first-choice striking alternative, with Bryan Mbeumo having to play on the right of the attack.

Carrick instead turned to Matheus Cunha, whose preference for dropping deep took him into the spaces captain Bruno Fernandes likes to occupy.

It neutralised United's attack on a day they seemed ill-prepared to meet the physical challenge of an opponent motivated by their long-awaited Premier League return.

In his role as interviewer for Nordic broadcaster Viaplay, former Norway and Middlesbrough striker Jan Aage Fjortoft later claimed United had lacked passion - something Carrick dismissed as "ridiculous".

"It's one game," Carrick told the media afterwards.

The following week, United were losing to Ipswich - another newly promoted side. Only a slip from Marcelino Nunez inside his own half allowed Cunha to tee up Fernandes for an undeserved equaliser.

The Portugal playmaker, who had just been crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26, went on to complete a hat-trick in a 5-2 win.

He has scored just once - a penalty against Villa on Sunday - in the league since.

After the Ipswich win came a trip to Everton.

Twice United led, the second occasion when Sesko struck two minutes from full-time after coming on as a substitute. Deep into stoppage time, Ainsley Maitland-Niles drove home from long range to deny the visitors.

Asked how confident he was in his side's ability to react to a disappointing start to the season, Carrick snapped back: "It's not been that bad."

What happened next, however, was.

Time and again, United's fitness was called into question. They struggled badly against a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men in the first half before their rivals benefited from an Erling Haaland goal that referees' chief Howard Webb later admitted should not have stood.

Carrick's complaints were justified - but they masked a poor performance from his team.

After taking a 2-0 lead inside 10 minutes against Brighton in the EFL Cup, United were outplayed and beaten, thanks to two goals in four second-half minutes.

The fine margins United benefited from during Carrick's interim spell were now going against them, and his coaching staff - lauded months earlier - could not find an answer.

Carrick called Cunha's injury-time equaliser against a Fulham side who started the game bottom of the table a positive to build on. But immediately after the international break, United were held to another draw - conceding in injury time to an out-of-form and 10-man Tottenham.

The whirlwind was starting to pick up strength.

Lisandro Martinez, who scored an own goal against Fulham, was at fault for Spurs' leveller, which made his post-match outburst after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid more amazing.

The Argentina defender criticised United's summer recruitment and placed the blame at the door of "the technical director" - Wilcox.

By the time of Martinez's outburst, Sesko and left-back Luke Shaw were injured. Marcus Rashford has not played since. The rotation at left-back that eventually led to Carrick starting five different players in that role was in full swing.

After conceding in the opening minute against Atletico, Como scored inside the first two in a 4-1 Champions League defeat for United. Fernandes came out afterwards and criticised Carrick's tactics.

He was dropped for the Bournemouth game, but returned as captain at Chelsea. United were beaten in both matches.

With just three wins in 15 matches in all competitions this season and United stuck in 18th in the Premier League, Carrick is set to pay the price.

News.title: Seven in hospital after car 'mounts pavement' in Glasgow
News.content:
Seven people have been taken to hospital after they were struck by a car in the west end of Glasgow.

Police Scotland said the driver was assessed by paramedics and treated at the scene of the incident, which happened at about 15:45 on Hyndland Road.

Unconfirmed reports suggest the vehicle mounted the pavement, hit a bus stop shelter and then struck scaffolding before coming to a halt.

A force spokesperson said: "Officers remain in attendance and inquiries are ongoing into the incident which is being treated as a road traffic collision."

News.title: Tories pledge to cut benefits for children with 'milder cases' of ADHD
News.content:
The Conservatives have pledged to save Â£2.8bn a year by ending Disability Living Allowance (DLA) payments to families of children with "milder cases" of behavioural disorders, learning difficulties or ADHD.

The policy is one of a series of measures which the party says will save Â£36bn from the welfare budget.

Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said the system risked putting children on a "conveyor belt" towards a "lifetime on benefits".

Labour described the Tories' plan as a "charter for homelessness and human misery that would push people into hardship and end up costing the state more".

DLA for children allows parents to claim between Â£30.30 and Â£194.60 per week to help cover the additional costs that come with raising a disabled child.

The child must either have difficulty getting about or need more looking after than a child of the same age who does not have a disability.

The Conservatives say child DLA is the "fastest growing benefit in the UK's welfare system", citing government statistics showing the number of cases had risen from 521,476 in 2020 to 914,000.

The party is proposing that in cases where a claim is for a behavioural disorder, learning difficulty or ADHD, only those with the highest need will be eligible for cash payments.

Under the party's plans, those with the most severe conditions, representing around 30% of cases, would continue to receive payments.

The remaining 70% would lose the money but instead receive support through mental health services and family hubs, into which the Conservatives have said they will invest Â£1bn.

The changes would apply to new claims and reassessments. Those with physical disabilities would be exempt.

The party's other previously-announced cuts include:

Â£13.7bn from changes to sickness and disability benefits including restricting payments to claimants with "milder mental health issues and neurodiversity conditions such as anxiety, depression and ADHD"

Â£9.5bn by making it harder for foreign nationals to claim benefits

Â£4.5bn by reducing local housing allowance payments

Â£3.1bn by reintroducing the two-child benefit cap

Â£1bn from tackling fraud

Setting out the party's plans, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "The reality is that millions of people can and do contribute to our economy, to their families, to their communities even when they face serious challenges.

"Double amputees run marathons. People who are housebound do wonderful creative work from home. People with autism run some of the biggest tech companies in the world.

"If you tell a young person that their ADHD means they are defective and will never amount to anything, that mindset is likely to be more destructive to their future than the condition itself."

News.title: US pilot arrested at Heathrow admits drugs offence
News.content:
An American pilot has admitted possessing cocaine after being arrested at Heathrow Airport earlier this month.

Wayne Sigler, 64, from Louisiana, was detained by police on Sunday 1 November and appeared at Uxbridge Magistrates Court on Saturday. After pleading guilty to the possession offence he was placed into custody, the Metropolitan Police confirmed.

He has also been charged with being drunk or unfit to fly while flying or working on an aircraft - two offences that fall under the Railway and Transport Act 2003.

He is due appear for his next hearing at Isleworth Crown Court on 7 December.

Police have not specified which company the pilot was working for when he was arrested.

Heathrow Airport has declined to comment.
