News.title: Stevie Wonder leaves cafe staff £1,000 tip after Manchester gig
News.content:
Staff at a Greater Manchester cafe found themselves sharing a Â£1,000 tip after a late-night visit from a musical legend.

Cafe Continental in Stalybridge found itself feeding Stevie Wonder, his band and entourage after the singer's sold-out gig performing his classic album Songs In The Key Of Life at the Co-op Live in Manchester.

Owner Ryan Robinson said Wonder, 76, was "a really nice guy, happy to chat to everybody".

Among those dining was Wonder's daughter and backing singer Aisha, about whom he wrote Isn't She Lovely? for the album.

Robinson said he had been contacted about 18 months ago by members of the band, who called in while playing in soul singer Toni Braxton's backing band.

They stayed in touch, and then on Sunday, Robinson got a call to ask if they could come back after the show.

"The band turned up at 23:00 had some food and then at about 00:30, four blacked out mini buses turned up outside, and Stevie Wonder was in one of them," he said.

The cafe staff had been forewarned that they would need to work late and put on a different menu to the usual Sunday roast.

The singer had a seaside feast with grilled sea bream, bouillabaisse and octopus.

And the staff's efforts were rewarded with the generous tip from Wonder and his band.

"That was first for everyone," Robinson said, adding: "His family, his entourage and his crew are absolutely lovely.

"You wouldn't even think they were famous and they're really enthusiastic about the restaurant."

News.title: York man, 19, shot and injured in Krakow attack
News.content:
A 19-year-old British man is in a stable condition after being shot by a gunman in Krakow, Poland.

Harry Marchant, from York, suffered a gunshot wound in the attack on Saturday, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square.

The 24-year-old attacker, who died in hospital on Monday, fatally shot four Polish citizens, a British national and an Austrian woman, while a further 15 people, including two police officers, were injured.

Marchant's family said he was receiving ongoing hospital treatment for his injuries.

"We can't express how grateful we are to the first responders, medical team, and the people of Poland for their help and care for Harry," they added.

"We ask for our privacy to be respected as we support Harry with his recovery."

News.title: Teens found guilty of murdering boy, 15, in park
News.content:
Two teenage boys have been convicted of murdering a 15-year-old boy in a dispute over Â£40.

The 16-year-old boys lured Luis Guembes to Stoke Park in Guildford in January then stabbed him to death.

A jury at Guildford Crown Court found the teenagers guilty of murder on Tuesday.

Their trial heard the boys, who were aged 15 and 16 at the time of the attack, had agreed to rob Guembes in order to settle "a debt he owed concerning a broken mobile phone".

The older boy had admitted charges of conspiracy to rob and possession of a bladed article. The jury convicted the younger boy of the same additional charges.

Both teenagers, who cannot be named due to their age, are due to be sentenced on 18 December.

"There are no winners, it is invariably sad for everyone involved," said Ms Justice Norton.

She told the court: "The sentence for murder is fixed by law - it is a life sentence.

"I require reports from a number of different bodies."

Norton continued: "Louis' family have a right to tell me what the effect of his death has been on them and they need time to process that and prepare a statement on that."

News.title: Rio Ngumoha explains why he left Chelsea for Liverpool: 'No-brainer'
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Rio Ngumoha has revealed why he chose to leave Chelsea and move to Liverpool, branding the decision a “no-brainer”.

The teenage winger joined Chelsea’s academy - world-renowned for its youth development - at the age of eight and became one of the club’s most-prized starlets, with academy coaches previously stating that they believed Ngumoha could win the Ballon d’Or.

But at 16, Ngumoha left Chelsea and joined Liverpool, who oversaw the last of his development in junior ranks before watching him burst onto the scene at senior level.

Chelsea were disgruntled with the nature of Ngumoha’s exit and Liverpool were told in February to pay an initial £2.8m in compensation by a tribunal, with potential for that sum to rise to £6.8m with various add-ons.

Nevertheless, with Ngumoha now a regular under Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola after a breakout season last term, the 18-year-old has explained the reasoning behind his transfer decision and asserts he has no regrets over the switch.

“I feel like I needed a new challenge,” he said. “I feel like if I stayed at Chelsea... not saying that I wouldn't have got to the first team as quick, because I believe in my ability, but I feel like Liverpool just gave me a new pathway.

“The plan that they set for me was straightforward really. For me, it was a no-brainer going to Liverpool, and they just said if I prove myself, because they know how much ability I had, then they know that I would definitely be a first-team player and definitely a star for them in the making.

“I think going to Liverpool so far has been the right choice.”

open image in gallery Rio Ngumoha made the bold decision to swap Chelsea for Liverpool at 16 ( Getty )

While Ngumoha only crossed paths with the senior Chelsea team a handful of times during his time at Cobham, he reflects on an interaction he had with Raheem Sterling - who was similarly once a teenage prodigy - when training with the seniors.

“I trained with them only a few times but Raheem Sterling pulled me to the side a couple of times and told me he could see I had talent but I should never zone out in the game and I should always be in the game,” he said.

“The best players are always in the game in the last minutes. If you look at him and Mo [Salah], they’re always there until the crucial moments. Learning off them was important.”

Ngumoha has featured 14 times for Liverpool so far this season across all competitions, notching two assists which both came in a standout Champions League performance in the 4-3 win over Villarreal.

open image in gallery Ngumoha shone in Liverpool’s win over Villarreal in October ( PA Wire )

He was hailed by pundits and fans alike after that match, with Liverpool supporters chanting his name as he was substituted.

“Like I always say, Liverpool, we have the best fans in the world, especially Anfield on Champions League nights against big teams,” Ngumoha added.

“The way it roars, I've never heard anything like it. It's special. It's definitely special to play in front of them.”

Ngumoha earned his second call-up to the England squad for the November international break, again entrusted by Thomas Tuchel as the youngest player in his roster.

open image in gallery Ngumoha has been called up by Thomas Tuchel for the second time this season ( Getty )

He could make his first England start in the coming days as the Three Lions see out their Nations League group-stage campaign, first with the visit of Croatia on Thursday before travelling to Madrid to face World Cup winners Spain on Saturday.

The latter will present him the opportunity to share the pitch with another winger sensation in Lamine Yamal, who was pipped to the Ballon d’Or by England captain Harry Kane last month.

Asked about that prospect, Ngumoha said: “I think what he’s doing changed football for young player. He’s phenomenal. He’s one of the best in the world.

“Seeing what he can do so young inspires me and all the other young players in how we can just play freely. The way he plays, it’s like it’s his pitch. It’s a good challenge.”

News.title: Was Kim Kardashian’s $148 Skims advent calendar a genuine blunder – or genius rage-bait marketing?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Since its 2019 launch, Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand Skims has dealt in viral moments. The company has made headlines for selling eyebrow-raising items, like a push-up bra with built-in nipples, a micro thong decorated in faux pubic hair and face-shaping compression gear. Early on, it also faced claims of cultural appropriation.

The brand’s latest internet catnip came over the weekend when influencers were underwhelmed – and angry – while unboxing its $148 luxury 12-day advent calendar, which was filled with inexpensive junk like bobby pins, hair ties and loose bra straps.

The discontent mounted quickly. “Are we serious right now?” Kayla Ryan, a content creator, asked in a video she posted on TikTok over the weekend, as she unboxed the various objects – including a plaid teddy bear key ring, endless amounts of bobby pins and a stress-relieving squishy – from large scrunches of clumsily wrapped tissue paper. The backlash inspired hundreds of parodies, some of them skits imagining Kardashian herself packing the calendar with debris from the bottom of her purse. Onlookers online branded it a “Skam.” By Sunday, Skims issued full refunds to all buyers, admitting the product “didn’t meet expectations.”

Then came another form of content – people arguing that the whole thing was a marketing stunt. And since Skims is known for orchestrating viral moments that manage to rage-bait the masses, some people have bought into the theory.

Melissa Alcruz, a brand strategist and chief marketing officer with 35 years of experience building and marketing major brands, can understand the outrage – especially considering that the advent calendar didn’t contain any clothing or underwear that it’s known for.

“It doesn’t feel like a premium Skims experience. It feels like somebody put together a corporate swag bag and called it an advent calendar,” Alcruz told The Independent.

But experts don’t believe this was a marketing stunt, since the company dished out refunds to every customer who had bought a calendar, even if they hadn’t made a complaint.

Adrianna Moore, a brand expert who advises businesses on creative risk, said that Skims has “mastered the art of making controversy commercially valuable,” but there’s a difference between “making people talk about your brand and making customers regret buying from it.” The Independent has contacted Skims for comment.

“Skims has built a business around making people uncomfortable. The problem is that this time, it made its own customers feel stupid,” Moore told The Independent.

“The nipple bra and faux-hair thong were provocative because they were abnormal, whimsical even, and their customers could laugh, criticize, or embrace the absurdity. They got to choose if they bought into it or not,” Moore said. “The problem with the advent calendar is different because it cost them $148 for what looks like the contents of somebody’s junk drawer.”

open image in gallery Kim Kardashian launched her shapewear brand Skims in 2019 with entrepreneur couple Jens and Emma Grede ( Getty )

Moore does not think it is a marketing stunt, and that the saying “any publicity is good publicity” only goes so far.

“A viral unboxing can rack up tens of millions of views, but that doesn’t mean the brand has earned tens of millions of potential customers,” Moore said.

“This probably won’t seriously damage Skims, but it does reveal where the brand is vulnerable,” she added.

Alcruz doesn’t think it was a stunt, either, and she was surprised by the lack of thought behind it.

open image in gallery Influencers were underwhelmed – and angry – while unboxing the Skims $148 luxury advent calendar, which was filled with bobby pins, hair ties and loose bra straps ( Skims )

“Having worked on major product launches, I know these decisions typically involve multiple people. Somebody selects the merchandise, somebody approves the concept, somebody evaluates the pricing and somebody ultimately signs off,” she said.

“I have to believe this concept originated with a relatively junior marketing team, because I find it very difficult to imagine an experienced brand strategist looking at a box of bobby pins and keychains and saying, ‘This is exactly what our customers love about Skims.’”

“If you can’t fill 12 compartments with merchandise that feels worthy of your brand, don’t make a 12-day calendar. Make a three-day calendar. Make a beautiful gift set,” she said.

“Nobody forced you to put 12 things in a box.”

News.title: David Walliams slashes price of London mansion by £1.45m as he faces allegations of preying on teenage girls
News.content:

Comedian David Walliams slashed the price of his mansion after it failed to sell, while he was battling accusations of sexually inappropriate behaviour.

The former Britain’s Got Talent judge, who allegedly used his fame to prey on teenager girls, last month took £1.45m off the asking price of his period London home to try to attract a buyer, it’s been revealed.

Walliams, who denies any wrongdoing, put the four-bedroom house up for sale in June with a price tag of £11,950,000, according to Rightmove. But five months on, the star dropped the price to £10.5m.

Estate agent Marcus Parfitt, which specialises in properties from £2m upwards, described the home as “an imposing white stucco-fronted residence” in a coveted position in north London.

open image in gallery The star has reduced the £11.95m price tag of house in north London

The details read: “Arranged over multiple levels and extending to approximately 4527sq ft (421sq m), the property, which has been totally refurbished and extended by the current owner over the last five years, offers generous proportions and a graceful sense of period charm.”

The house, behind black gates, was sold in 2013 for £8,450,000, according to the Land Registry.

Photographs show it has large sash windows, period features such as fireplaces and all-white walls, many hung with monochrome photographs of famous people or film posters.

The estate agent highlights that it has “21st-century technology throughout”.

Walliams has been revealed as the famous man who brought legal action against two media organisations to prevent them from publishing allegations against him.

open image in gallery Walliams took legal action against media outlets to prevent them from identifying him over the allegations ( Invision/AP )

He is accused of sexually inappropriate behaviour by women, including two who claim to have been “groomed” by the comedian when they were 15.

One woman, identified in the investigation as Jade, said Walliams was 36 when they met in August 2007 and he invited her back to his house. She claimed what happened to her there was “sexual assault” and “grooming”, adding: “It’s completely wrong in every way.”

Another woman alleged she was having sex with when she was 17. Asked how she felt about him now, she said: “I think I was groomed. 100 per cent.”

The star told journalists during the investigation he was not a sexual predator and denied breaking the law.

He wrote: “Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with. I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

“And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.”

He added: “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

News.title: US soldier arrested by British terror police for alleged espionage relating to Russia
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A member of the US Army has been arrested in the UK on suspicion of offences under the National Security Act 2023 which relate to Russia, Counter Terrorism Policing London said.

The man, aged 41, was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday following an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing, working closely with US authorities, US Military and the FBI. He remains in custody at a London police station as enquiries continue.

Officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire as part of the investigation. The investigation is not linked to any other ongoing Counter Terrorism Policing investigations.

The man has been detained under the sections one and two of the National Security Act 2023, which respectively covers obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

open image in gallery Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel said there had been a 53 per cent increase in counterintelligence and espionage arrests over the past 21 months ( Getty )

Deputy assistant commissioner Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said that UK and US law enforcement and national security services were working together on the “serious” investigation.

“This significant arrest and investigation is a result of close collaboration between UK and US authorities,” she said.

“The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing. This activity demonstrates the strength of our UK and US law enforcement and national security partnerships, and I commend the work of all the teams involved.

“We will work together to take robust action against those we suspect of any criminal activity that could undermine our national security."

FBI director Kash Patel said his agency had no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States.

“This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” he said.

“While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message – this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners.

“This includes 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests from this FBI over the last 21 months – a 53 per cent increase.

“This matter shows that partnerships are essential to protect our countries and I want to express my thanks to UK Counter Terrorism Policing, MI5, UK Defence Counter Intelligence, and the US army counterintelligence command for their outstanding work.”

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of US army counterintelligence command, said: “This case demonstrates the strength of our partnerships and the resolve of the counterintelligence community. I am grateful to the UK and the FBI for their professionalism and teamwork throughout this investigation.

“The alleged conduct of a senior solider, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent. I encourage anyone who thinks they’ve witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office."

More to follow...

News.title: Six Flags theme park announces 2027 will be its final season
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The ride is almost over for one Six Flags theme park which is preparing for a final season in 2027 before closing its doors for good.

After more than 50 years, California’s Great America in Santa Clara will celebrate its final year. The park’s special Farewell Season will run from March until Labor Day on September 6, 2027.

"The Farewell Season is an opportunity for generations of Bay Area guests to return, spend time with family and friends, and revisit the attractions and traditions that have made the park in Santa Clara, California, such a meaningful part of the community,” Six Flags said in its announcement Friday.

California's Great America first opened in 1976 as Marriott's Great America. Over the years, the park has changed ownership several times, eventually becoming part of Cedar Fair's amusement park portfolio before the company merged with Six Flags in 2024.

The decision to close the park comes down to its land lease. Cedar Fair sold the 112-acre property to real estate company Prologis in 2022 for $310 million but secured a lease allowing the amusement park to continue operating on the land.

California's Great America, which initially opened in 1976 as Marriott's Great America, will close after its 2027 season, Six Flags recently announced ( iStock/Getty Images )

That lease is scheduled to expire in June 2028. Six Flags has decided not to renew it, making 2027 the park’s final season.

Group outings, corporate events and student and youth group visits will also continue throughout the 2027 season, park officials said.

Additional details about the final season's operating calendar, including specific days and hours, will be announced at a later date.

Six Flags Entertainment Corporation operates 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resort properties across 13 U.S. states, Canada and Mexico.

News.title: GOP-led Epstein committee clears Trump of wrongdoing - but details government’s failings
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Republican-led House Oversight Committee released a report detailing the findings of its months-long investigation into the government’s mishandling of criminal probes into Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell.

Released Tuesday, the 137-page report cleared President Donald Trump of wrongdoing, while concluding that the federal government had “failed” survivors for decades.

“We conducted 19 witness interviews or depositions, subpoenaed the Department of Justice, Epstein’s estate and two major banks and reviewed financial records from the Department of the Treasury to uncover the truth,” GOP Rep. James Comer, the committee chair, said in a video. “What we found is both heartbreaking and infuriating.”

Rep. Robert Garcia, the leading Democrat on the committee, denounced the report as “based on an incomplete investigation and zero public hearings on Jeffrey Epstein.” The findings were published one week after the midterm elections, when Democrats reclaimed control of both the House and the Senate. The committee is set to be chaired by a Democrat in January, when the new Congress is sworn in.

Here are the report’s key findings:

open image in gallery On Tuesday, the GOP-led House Oversight Committee released a 137-page report documenting its probe into the government's investigations of Jeffrey Epstein. Pictured: Committee Chair James Comer and ranking member Robert Garcia ( Getty )

The federal government ‘failed survivors for decades,’ including by granting Epstein a non-prosecution agreement.

Despite Democrats’ obsession with implicating Trump, no evidence emerged he was involved in Epstein’s crimes.

The Department of Justice must take “further action,” including by interviewing key witnesses.

Major financial institutions failed to respond to “clear indicators of human trafficking and immigration fraud.”

Congress should pass a bill to “prevent the weaponization of nondisclosure agreements to silence survivors.”

open image in gallery Ghislaine Maxwell with Jeffrey Epstein. She is the only person to go to jail in connection to his crimes ( US Department of Justice )

The committee began investigating the government’s handling of probes into Epstein and Maxwell last year, when the Trump administration’s handling of the Epstein files sparked widespread controversy. Maxwell is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence after she was found guilty of sex crimes. Esptein died by suicide in 2019 inside a jail cell while awaiting trial.

A number of high profile figures have been interviewed by lawmakers, including former President Bill Clinton, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, billionaires Les Wexner and Bill Gates, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and former Attorney General Pam Bondi. All have denied wrongdoing, and several who were asked said they had no knowledge of Epstein’s criminal activities during their association with him.

For months, Republicans on the committee have publicly defended Trump, claiming they’ve seen no evidence implicating the president and casting Democratic efforts as a witch hunt. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, a Florida Republican on the committee, said in February that Bill Clinton’s testimony had “exonerated” Trump.

Trump’s name appears repeatedly in the Epstein files, and the disgraced financier once said he was Trump’s “closest friend.” The president has said he cut ties with Epstein years ago and that Democrats are perpetuating a “hoax.” He has not been charged with a crime and denied any involvement.

Democrats, meanwhile, have accused the committee's GOP leadership of failing to conduct a thorough investigation.

“You didn't hold a single public hearing,” Oversight Democrats said Tuesday in response to Comer’s report. “You didn't say anything when the DOJ withheld 2.5 million missing files. You didn't bring in [Attorney General] Todd Blanche after saying you would.”

“We will not allow the President and his allies to dismiss this investigation,” they added. “We're just getting started.”

According to an October YouGov survey, 58 percent of Americans disapprove of the way Trump has handled investigations into Epstein, while just 26 percent approve.

open image in gallery The committee interviewed both Bill and Hillary Clinton in New York earlier this year ( GOP Oversight Committee )

More on the report’s findings

The committee concluded that the crimes committed by Epstein — who was charged with sex trafficking minors before his 2019 death — could have been prevented if not for “failures” by prosecutors in Florida and Washington, D.C., as well as federal investigators.

Committee members specifically called attention to Epstein’s 2007 non-prosecution agreement, which they said enabled crimes after 2005. The committee found the deal allowed him to evade federal prosecution for lesser state charges. Federal prosecutors also failed to inform victims, which impacted their ability to pursue civil cases or tell the public.

Committee members determined that while some failures resulted from “poor judgment” by prosecutors, others appeared to be influenced by Epstein’s far-reaching connections.

The New York prison that housed Epstein after his 2019 arrest had constant understaffing and dysfunction, including guards missing 12 rounds and three inmate counts on the night Epstein died, the committee noted.

“This resulted in nearly eight hours without adequate supervision of Epstein and other inmates,” the committee stated.

Lawmakers also highlighted the Justice Department’s failure to “adequately communicate about document releases” following the enactment of the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

open image in gallery Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified at a closed-door interview with the House Oversight Committee in May ( Getty )

GOP lawmakers accused Democrats of having been “obsessed” with implicating Trump in Epstein and Maxwell’s crimes.

“The consensus of every witness examined before the Committee was that President Trump––to their knowledge––was not involved in any crimes committed by Epstein and Maxwell,” the report states.

The report did make several recommendations to the DOJ moving forward, and called on the Justice Department to interview key witnesses, possible accomplices and victims.

“DOJ should establish an appropriate process for Epstein survivors and their representatives to access their personal files and records in unredacted form,” the committee stated.

Justice officials should also scrutinize non-prosecution agreements to ensure they do not “enable and empower criminals,” the committee stated.

Major financial institutions were also accused of failing to respond to “clear indicators of human trafficking and immigration fraud.” Despite being aware of Epstein’s criminal history and identifying suspicious transactions, institutions allowed him to “use fraudulent decoy flights and refundable or dummy itineraries to transport foreign women across borders directly to his residences.”

“The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) should review whether financial institutions are meeting their reporting obligations designed to detect and prevent suspicious activities, including money laundering and human trafficking,” the committee said in a release about the report.

Finally, GOP lawmakers on the committee said that Congress should pass a bill to “prevent the weaponization of nondisclosure agreements to silence survivors of sexual abuse.”

News.title: David Walliams accused of preying on teenage girls and sexually assaulting 15-year-old
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Comedian and former Britain’s Got Talent judge David Walliams has been unmasked as the star who failed to gag reports accusing him of grooming teenagers as young as 15.

Multiple women have accused the celebrity of sexual misconduct in an investigation published by The Guardian and ITV News, alleging he used his fame to prey on them for sexual purposes.

One claims she was just 15 when the Little Britain star allegedly contacted her out of the blue on MySpace in 2007. The 36-year-old comic later invited her to his £3.2m London townhouse where he sexually assaulted her, she alleges.

The Metropolitan Police says it has not received any reports of sexual assault or other offences, but added that if anyone comes forward, their complaints will be “carefully assessed”.

Walliams denies any wrongdoing and his lawyers took a case to the High Court to try to stop the allegations being published.

In an emphatic denial, Walliams insisted he is “not a sexual predator” and said he is “devastated” that allegations have been brought against him.

“Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with,” the comedian said in a statement to The Guardian and ITV News.

open image in gallery Comedian David Walliams tried to gag press reports alleging sexual misconduct ( Getty )

“I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.”

He added: “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

Walliams, now 55, did not respond to The Independent’s request for comment following the publication of his name on Tuesday.

The prime minister’s spokesperson described the allegations as “deeply troubling” and the Labour Party is understood to have suspended the television personality’s membership after the accusations came to light.

A BBC spokesperson said the broadcaster is in the process of removing some programmes while it carries out a review of “all material featuring and written by David Walliams on our platforms”.

The children’s author was also dropped by his literary agency, Independent Talent Group (ITG), on Tuesday, with a spokesperson saying they were “deeply disturbed” by the allegations.

His publisher HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025 after an investigation into allegations that he had “harassed” young women, which Walliams denied. The eponymous Alton Towers attraction inspired by his bestselling children’s books was permanently closed earlier this month.

The joint investigation includes accounts from several women who shared their allegations using pseudonyms. One, who used the name Jade, claimed her date of birth was displayed on her profile page on MySpace when Walliams sent her a private message in summer 2007.

open image in gallery The former Britain’s Got Talent judge denies any wrongdoing ( PA )

In August that year, when she was 15, they met in person and he took her back to his then-home in Belsize Park, she alleges. She claimed what happened to her there was “sexual assault” and “grooming”, adding: “It’s completely wrong in every way.”

Walliams strongly denied that he had any sexual contact with Jade, adding that he rejects any allegations of criminal activity and he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.

Another woman, named by the news organisations as Alex, alleged she was 15 and studying for her GCSEs when Walliams telephoned her in 2004 after she had shared some of her scripts with him at a fan event a few days earlier. They stayed in contact and she started having sex with Walliams when she was 17, she claims.

Asked how she feels about him now, she said: “I think I was groomed. 100 per cent.”

Walliams told the publications he believed she was 18 at the time they had sex. His lawyers say the suggestion he groomed Alex is false and has caused him significant distress.

Another young woman, Lilly Creightmore, said she met Walliams in July 2003 when she was 18 at a live filming of Little Britain.

Having seen him at a second event, the former teen model claimed she received a card sent to her home asking her out.

She said they became friends and when she fell out with her mother, Walliams invited her to stay with him. Although she slept on the sofa, she claimed he asked her to stay in his bed every night.

open image in gallery The author has been dropped by his publisher and his literary agency ( Getty )

“He would plead with me to share a bed with him and paw at me, trying to make me feel sorry for him,” she told the news organisations.

“He definitely crossed the line physically in moments, when I was young, trying to coerce me into sleeping with him.”

Lawyers for Walliams said he saw her as a close friend and is mortified that she feels he was grooming her, which he denies. He also denies targeting her because she was young and vulnerable and insists he did not say or do anything inappropriate.

A model, named as Ella, was 19 when she met Walliams, then 36, in 2007, and attended a party at his house. She alleges he tried to kiss her when they were alone and she “ducked underneath his arm and ran away”.

Walliams said he made a “clumsy pass” at Ella but made no further approaches.

Justice minister Alex Davies-Jones said the government is “concerned” about the use of injunctions and is “looking at what more” it can do, after Walliams used the courts to try to prevent the allegations from being published.

Walliams had brought legal action against the news outlet’s publishers, Independent Television News (ITN) and Guardian News and Media (GNM). He denied the claims and unsuccessfully sought an injunction to prevent publication because of the risk he would take his own life, after two previous suicide attempts.

The author was granted anonymity during the proceedings, which was lifted after his injunction bid was dismissed and the investigations were published on Tuesday.

open image in gallery Walliams applied for an injunction because of the risk he would take his own life ( PA )

They also included allegations about Walliams’ conduct at BGT, and at his publisher HarperCollins.

A spokesperson for ITV said: “Our thoughts are with those who have spoken out and we are very sorry to hear about their experiences.

“BGT is produced for ITV by Fremantle, an independent production company. Although ITV is the broadcaster of the programme, the producer has day-to-day responsibility for the running of the production, including all aspects of duty of care, and for ensuring compliance with all legal and regulatory obligations as well as ITV’s production and compliance guidelines.

“We expect the highest standards of all production companies who work with us, and to be notified of any duty of care concerns when they come to the producer’s attention. Fremantle have confirmed that no complaint has ever been made to them about David Walliams’ behaviour.”

A spokesperson for HarperCollins said: “HarperCollins UK previously terminated its publishing relationship with David Walliams. We take the safety of our people incredibly seriously and to respect the privacy of individuals we do not comment on employee matters”.

A Met spokesperson said they had contacted the news outlets last week to ensure potential victims were aware of how to report criminal allegations.

“The Met has not received any related reports of sexual assault or any other offences,” the spokesperson added. “Should we receive any reports, they will be carefully assessed. Anyone who contacts the police will be supported by specialist officers.”

Reports can be made by calling 101, providing the reference 4900/10NOV26.

News.title: England must collaborate with clubs for key duo's recovery, says Kevin Sinfield
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry will be carefully managed between now and the World Cup as England look to give two key personnel the best possible chance of being available for the tournament.

Feyi-Waboso will miss the rest of the autumn because of an ankle injury sustained in Sunday’s 44-22 mauling of Australia, robbing England of their most dangerous attacking threat.

And British and Irish Lions flanker Curry will sit out all four Nations Championship matches at Allianz Stadium this month after aggravating a long-standing hip condition in training last week.

Both players will travel to next year’s World Cup in Australia if fit but have concerning injury records that paint an uncertain picture over their involvement.

open image in gallery Tom Curry is managing a persistent hip problem and will miss the autumn campaign (Steven Paston/PA)

Under the current agreement between England and the Prem clubs, head coach Steve Borthwick now has greater control over the 25 members of his elite player squad, including final say on workload and medical matters.

“The best high-performance environments have the right amount of care and the right amount of challenge,” assistant coach Sir Kevin Sinfield said.

“How Tom’s managed, looked after and supported over this next period of time will be really important for him.

“He’s still a young man and we’re a better squad when he’s around. He’s a world-class player.

open image in gallery Will Joseph is a contender to replace Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the wing against Japan (John Walton/PA)

“The agreement that’s in place hopefully will ensure brilliant collaboration between club and country so that Tom plays for a long, long time, and he can be at his very best when he’s in and out of camp.

“Manny’s had a run of injuries now and hopefully that can be the last one for some time. I think it’s because of the nature of how he’s put together – he’s that powerful.

“What you tend to find is players either get a load of injuries at the start of their careers or get them towards the back end.

“Hopefully we can get him fully fit for a long period of time and Exeter get to see the best of him too. Again the collaboration is going to be really important for us.”

Feyi-Waboso’s unique ability to beat defenders was on full display at Twickenham and Sinfield described his performance as “world class”, adding “he’s our Jason Robinson” in reference to the cross-code great.

open image in gallery Former England boss Eddie Jones takes hiss Japan side to Twickenham on Saturday (Andrew Matthews/PA)

His absence creates a vacancy on the wing for Saturday’s Test against Japan and whoever is selected will be instructed to play to their own strengths.

“There aren’t many Mannys kicking around so to go like for like is difficult,” Sinfield said.

“We can’t ask somebody to come in and play like Manny, but we can ask them to come in and bring the best of themselves.”

Gloucester’s in-form outside back Will Joseph is one of the players looking to fill his boots and Sinfield insists he is ready to take his chance if selected.

“What a player he is,” Sinfield said. “He beats people. He’s got great balance. He’s a good defender with unbelievable power and speed off the mark.

“He’s a special player. Some of the bits he’s done in training have been ‘wow’ moments. He can play.”

News.title: Gaza floods are an “immediate humanitarian emergency”, warns Trump’s Board of Peace
News.content:
Donald Trump’s Board of Peace has accused Israel of an “insufficient” response to deadly floods that have hit the Gaza Strip.

In a rare statement, the US-led body, charged with ending war in Gaza and rebuilding the Strip, called on Israel “to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies”.

“The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency,” they said on Monday.

The Board has been pushing Israel for at least a month to speed up its “winterisation” policies so that residents in Gaza are better able to withstand the coldest months of the year.

The statement followed a weekend of torrential rain and winds that battered the decimated territory’s displacement camps, causing widespread flooding, landslides and several deaths.

A mother and her three young children were killed when a sand dune collapsed onto their tent in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. The children, aged four, five and eight died on Sunday. Their mother also suffocated under the sand.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick LIVE: Man Utd chiefs set for crunch Monaco meeting as Mauricio Pochettino tops shortlist
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is set to be relieved of his duties as Manchester United manager after a disastrous start to the season left them in the Premier League relegation zone

Michael Carrick is set to be sacked as Manchester United manager in a crunch meeting held in Monaco tomorrow.

The Old Trafford hierarchy are set to finally wield the axe following a disastrous start to the season. United have won just once in the Premier League, leaving them marooned in the relegation zone.

Carrick was given three games to save his job before the international break, but suffered defeat by Chelsea before a stirring comeback saw United beat Roma 3-2.

The Red Devils then drew 4-4 with Aston Villa on Sunday, twice recovering from a two-goal deficit, but it wasn't enough to save Carrick, with United to relieve him of his duties today.

Club chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are expected to meet with Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday, where they are expected to decide to make a change. He will then be told in person at Carrington on Thursday.

Mauricio Pochettino is the favourite to succeed Carrick and is reportedly open to the job, while Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe are also in the frame.

Stay right here for all the latest updates throughout the day.

Sports.title: Damning total cost of Man Utd sacking Michael Carrick for Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
Damning total cost of Man Utd sacking Michael Carrick for Mauricio Pochettino

Manchester United are seemingly on the verge of sacking Michael Carrick following a poor start to the season, with Mauricio Pochettino

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United may have to shell out more than £10million to sack Michael Carrick and bring in Mauricio Pochettino. The Red Devils have endured a horrid start to the new season, languishing in 18th with just eight points to show from their opening 10 matches.

‌



‌



As a result, many fans expect United to part ways with the 45-year-old during the November international break, leaving them plenty of time to source an apt replacement ahead of their return to Premier League football. That comes on Sunday, November 22, with the Red Devils making the trip to Anfield to face a fierce Liverpool.

‌



While a number of names have been linked with taking up tenure at Old Trafford, from Eddie Howe to Julian Nagelsmann, it is Pochettino who is thought to be the frontrunner in the event that Carrick is handed his marching orders. That would, however, require United to splash the cash on hiring and firing once more - in an era that Sir Jim Ratcliffe has made the club's dedication to cutting costs and making savings clear.

‌



Ineos make Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sack decisions ahead of crunch Man Utd talks READ MORE :

Carrick is currently contracted by the club until 2028, having signed a permanent deal this summer. As a result, United would have to pay the Englishman severance in the event that they choose to terminate that contract prematurely.

As per GiveMeSport, while Carrick has a one-year break clause embedded in his contract, United would still have to cough up the remainder of the year's salary to part ways with him. Thought to be commanding around £5m annually, that is thought to equate to around £3m considering Carrick is months into his contract.

‌



Elsewhere, United would also have to pay compensation to Pochettino's current employers in the United States national team - to whom, the Argentine is under contract with until at least 2030. Reports suggest that Pochettino has a $10m (£7.4m) release clause in that deal.

Add that figure to the £3m that would be due to go Carrick's way, and United may have to shell out more than £10m to swap out Carrick for Pochettino this month - and that could rise higher with support staff. No strangers to sacking underperforming managers, the Red Devils have spent a fortune in hiring and firing head coaches over the past decade while trying to find the next Alex Ferguson.

‌

David Moyes is thought to have received around £5.2m when he was let go just one year into his deal at Old Trafford in 2014, while Lous van Gaal is said to have been paid out £8.4m for his exit in 2016.

‌



Jose Mourinho lived up to his 'Special One' moniker by taking home a £19.6m payday for his sacking in 2018, with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer receiving severance to the tune of a cool £10m three years later.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is feeling the heat (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ralf Rangnick was afforded around £15m for his leave, Erik ten Hag saw £10.4m as per reports and the club are thought to have spent £8.2m to send Ruben Amorim packing in January. It comes as Sky Sports claim that club officials fear a change of face in the dugout may not be enough to reverse fortunes at Old Trafford.

Supporters and pundits have shown discontent with the club hierarchy, with bosses seemingly agreeing that problems within the club run deeper than within the dressing room. Whether the club will afford Carrick more time and address said problems as a result remains to be seen, although it appears as though the head coach has finite time within his current post.

Sports.title: Ineos make Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sack decisions ahead of crunch Man Utd talks
Sports.content:
Ineos make Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sack decisions ahead of crunch Man Utd talks

Manchester United's poor season could cost Michael Carrick his job but Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have come in for particular criticism as fans and pundits take aim at the duo

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe is ready to stick by two of his most senior figures - Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

Manchester United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada retain the backing of Sir Jim Ratcliffe despite their competency coming under severe scrutiny.

‌



‌



The club go into the international break in the relegation zone and reports claim Michael Carrick will be axed this week, with both of the senior figures approving of his exit.

‌



However Carrick and the team's struggles have shone a light on the issues that run far deeper at the club. Among those is whether Berrada and Wilcox are fit for purpose given their previous experience and subsequent decision making on the red side of Manchester.

‌



They will have played their part in United potentially having a third different manager in the dugout inside a calendar year if Carrick is sacked. But despite their decision making clearly setting the club back, the Telegraph reports that Ratcliffe has no plans to remove them from their roles.

‌



Wilcox and Berrada are expected to meet Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday as part of a summit for Ineos’s senior staff. It had long been pencilled in the diary but the situation at Old Trafford means Carrick's future will be front and centre.

The United hierarchy, namely Wilcox and Berrada, have been increasingly singled out by fans and pundits as a result of United's dire season - which has seen them win just one of their 10 Premier League games. Even Lisandro Martinez went as far as to call out Wilcox in the aftermath of their loss to Atletico Madrid, accusing him of not equipping the squad well enough.

‌



Wilcox in his role as the director of football has been hammered for the club's poor recruitment with chief executive Berrada ultimately overseeing the day-to-day football operations at the club.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's time as Man United boss may well come to an end this week (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

‌



Ratcliffe appointed Berrada and Wilcox after taking control of the football department when he bought an influential minority stake from the Glazers in 2024.

Berrada was hired off the back of his work at Manchester City, where he had seen his reputation rise. It was at City that Berrada became aware of Wilcox, who was the club’s academy director before leaving to become director of football at Southampton. He was there 14 months before joining United, initially as technical director.

Among the poor decisions that have seen the pair criticised is the backing, and then the sacking, of Erik ten Hag. Sports.title: Truth about Tom Brady's involvement in Birmingham City after NFL legend's departure
Sports.content:
The departure of Tom Brady from Birmingham City will spark more interest from elsewhere than it will in the corridors of the club’s training ground and stadium.

Brady has always been a bit-part player in the Blues story and was little more than an advisor to Tom Wagner and Co – even if his name was used in the title of the six-part documentary about the club which aired on Amazon Prime last year.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner never made it onto Blues’ official board. He was given some shares in Shelby Companies Limited, the company through which Knighthead controls Blues, but he didn’t have any voting rights.

Back in April 2025, an update on the Companies House of SCL revealed that Brady and some of his business partners had been awarded an insignificant number of shares. Alex Guerrero, who is Brady’s long-time mentor, body coach and ‘best friend’, and filmmaker Gotham Chopra, who co-founded media brand Religion of Sports with Brady, were among those given shares.

‌



There has been no update on Companies House regarding Brady’s shareholding since it was announced on Monday evening that his involvement with Blues has ended.

For Blues, it will be business as usual with Wagner still the figurehead and chairman of the club.

View 3 Images Tom Wagner with Tom Brady at Birmingham City (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

The American hasn’t been so hands-on in 2026 during his recovery from a stroke but he has now watched three Blues matches in person this season and he is in regular communication with manager Chris Davies and the club’s leadership team.

‌



Andrew Shannahan has been Wagner’s right-hand man throughout Knighthead’s Blues tenure, indeed they carried out the League One trophy together before the team were crowned champions at St Andrew’s last year, and he has stepped up in recent months.

Shannahan, who alongside Wagner is the only other listed director on the Companies House of SCL, has frequented St Andrew’s more regularly and mingled with supporters at a recent Open House event.

He even joined chief executive Jeremy Dale in The Big Bulls Head in Digbeth on Saturday night to celebrate the victory that sent Blues top of the Championship table.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 3 Images Tom Brady had very little involvement at Birmingham (Image: Getty Images)

Blues’ four-man board is completed by Matt Alvarez and Kyle Kneisly, although neither are named as directors on SCL.

Alvarez is a well-known film director in the United States and played a key role in the documentary, Built in Birmingham: Brady and the Blues. He has taken a keen interest in the women’s team but has only been seen sparingly at St Andrew’s.

At 38, Kneisly is the youngest board member and has taken an active role in planning for the Sports Quarter and The Powerhouse.

‌



While Brady’s departure has attracted headlines, Blues’ ownership structure hasn’t changed at all.

Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's Man Utd future to be decided in Monaco meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe

Manchester United CEO and technical director Jason Wilcox will recommend to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that Michael Carrick is sacked in a crunch Monaco meeting

View 2 Images Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox will meet in Monaco tomorrow (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

Manchester United bosses will meet in Monaco tomorrow - and are expected to decide to sack Michael Carrick. Executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox will meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to discuss Carrick's future.

It's understood Berrada and Wilcox will recommend Carrick be relieved of his duties. Ratcliffe will have the final say and is expected to consult with fellow owners the Glazers, but it is almost inevitable Carrick will be dismissed.

The meeting in the South of France had been pre-planned to coincide with the international break. But the manager situation is now top of the agenda following United's humiliating start to the season.

Sports.content:
Man Utd would have to pay huge fee to hire Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick's successor

Manchester United's hierarchy are mulling over their next steps with Michael Carrick expected to be sacked on Tuesday, and Mauricio Pochettino is one of the candidates in the frame

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is currently the head coach of the United States (Image: Robin Alam/Getty Images)

Manchester United would have to fork out millions in order to land Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick's successor.

‌



‌



Pochettino has emerged as one of the leading contenders as United draw up a shortlist of options to replace Carrick. Club chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have decided to sack Carrick with United sitting 18th in the Premier League with a dismal eight points from their opening 10 matches.

‌



Former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino is one of the candidates for the job, along with Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte. Berrada and Wilcox are set to meet with INEOS chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe to make a decision during the current international break.

‌



But while Howe, Nagelsmann and Conte are all available, Pochettino's appointment would be more complicated. The 54-year-old is the head coach of the United States, having signed a new deal after this summer's World Cup which runs until 2030.

However, that deal does include a buyout clause which would make a deal possible. Pochettino, who has been considered by United several times in the past, insisted on an exit clause for a high-profile job.

‌



The Athletic reports that his clause stands at around $10million (£7.4m), although many more millions would be required to release Pochettino's coaching staff. It represents a significant expense for United, who already face having to pay Carrick off just 172 days after handing him a two-year contract.

Pochettino is open to talks with United, despite currently being busy preparing for the USA's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti. He has openly courted a return to the Premier League, but has also insisted he is committed to the USA.

If we don’t believe in that process, if we don’t believe in that journey, why (would) we sign four years? Only to be sure that we are going to receive a salary on the end of the month?

Sports.title: Inside Mauricio Pochettino's private meeting he 'set up' with ex-Man Utd boss
Sports.content:
Inside Mauricio Pochettino's private meeting he 'set up' with ex-Man Utd boss

Manchester United are on the verge of sacking Michael Carrick, with Mauricio Pochettino reportedly being lined up as his successor

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino is heavily linked with the Manchester United job (Image: Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino is once again circling the Manchester United hotseat and this time the Old Trafford revolving door might finally swing his way. With Michael Carrick dangling by the barest of threads over the international break, Sunday's chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa felt less like a spirited fightback and more like the frantic final gasp of a doomed tenure.

‌



‌



Sitting 18th in the Premier League table with a miserable solitary win from 10 outings, United look set to hit the reset button. Carrick's P45 hasn't officially landed on his desk just yet, but according to The Athletic, behind closed doors, succession plans are already in overdrive - and Pochettino has sprinted straight to the front of the queue.

‌



Currently in charge of the USA national team, the former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach has long been linked with the Manchester United job. In fact, he once organised a private meeting with Sir Alex Ferguson, fuelling speculation that a move to Old Trafford was imminent.

‌



The pair sat down for lunch at a London restaurant in May 2016, just as speculation over Louis van Gaal's future was reaching fever pitch. United were expected to part company with the Dutchman that summer, while Pochettino had just guided Tottenham through their first genuine Premier League title challenge in years. Naturally, the Argentine's name was being thrown around as a potential successor.

Man Utd set to SACK Michael Carrick after disastrous start to the season READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

When Pochettino was photographed leaving the restaurant alongside his assistant Jesus Perez, the rumour mill went into overdrive. Ferguson, who continued to wield considerable influence at United, was suspected of sounding out the Spurs boss as the club prepared to make their next managerial appointment.

‌



The reality, however, was rather less cloak-and-dagger. The lunch was understood to be a friendly meeting between two men who had been trying to arrange a social get-together for some time. Pochettino had even informed Tottenham of his plans to meet Ferguson, while the fact they chose to do so in broad daylight hardly suggested an elaborate attempt to keep their rendezvous under wraps.

Any lingering fears among Tottenham supporters that their manager was plotting an exit were also eased by developments in the weeks beforehand. Pochettino had already verbally agreed to extend his contract at White Hart Lane and, when his new deal was announced, he was quick to point to Ferguson as an example of what could be achieved with time and stability.

‌



"Sir Alex Ferguson is a very special person. He was given the security to build his legacy at Manchester United," he said. "But I believe we are special too and we can build it here together."

View 3 Images Sir Alex Ferguson and Mauricio Pochettino met for lunch in 2016 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



United, meanwhile, had other ideas. Rather than pursuing Pochettino, the club eventually turned to Jose Mourinho that summer. The board were reportedly reluctant to enter into tortuous negotiations with Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy, who was never likely to make life easy for a club attempting to snatch his prized manager.

It wouldn't be the last time Pochettino's name surfaced in connection with the United job. When Mourinho was dismissed in December 2018, the Argentine was again touted as a leading contender. United instead handed Ole Gunnar Solskjaer the reins on an interim basis, before making the Norwegian's appointment permanent the following March.

‌



Pochettino was back in the conversation when Solskjaer was shown the door in November 2021. By then, the former Tottenham boss was in charge of Paris Saint-Germain and was reportedly keen on a return to the Premier League.

There was, however, a significant stumbling block. United were told they would have to wait until the end of the 2021/22 campaign to prise Pochettino away from the French capital. Instead, they installed Ralf Rangnick as interim manager before eventually settling on Erik ten Hag as their permanent appointment.

‌



View 3 Images Will Mauricio Pochettino finally be taking the reins at Old Trafford? (Image: Getty Images)

The revolving door at Old Trafford provided another potential opening in 2024. Having left Chelsea by mutual consent, Pochettino was once again among the names considered as United assessed Ten Hag's position following a disappointing eighth-place league finish.

‌



This time, though, the club opted to stick with the Dutchman. By the time they eventually dismissed him a few months later, Pochettino had already committed his future to a different project, taking charge of the United States national team.

With Carrick seemingly on borrowed time, Pochettino has once again found himself firmly in the frame for the United job. But for a manager and club whose paths have crossed so many times without ever quite aligning, the timing could prove awkward once again.

‌



Just three months ago, the Argentine signed a new four-year contract as United States head coach, committing himself to the national team until the 2030 World Cup. Any attempt to lure him away would therefore likely require United to negotiate a sizeable compensation package, with the ink barely dry on his new deal.

But if Manchester United are serious about finally landing their long-time managerial target, perhaps this is the moment their paths finally converge. After a decade of near-misses, missed opportunities and tantalising what-ifs, Mauricio Pochettino could yet get his long-awaited chance to take charge at Old Trafford.
