Sports.title: Rui Pinto’s lawyers in talks with UK authorities over deal for Manchester City whistleblower
Sports.content:
Rui Pinto’s lawyers are in talks with British authorities over a potential cooperation agreement under which the Manchester City whistleblower could help to expose serious financial and sporting crime in the UK.

According to information obtained by the Guardian, the Serious Fraud Office has contacted Pinto after it emerged he was willing to assist British authorities with their investigations in exchange for protection.

William Bourdon, Pinto’s lawyer, who has represented whistleblowers such as Edward Snowden and Julian Assange, told the Guardian that contact had been established. “I can confirm that the process is under way,” he said, without providing further details.

If an agreement is reached, the Football Leaks founder could become a significant source of information in investigations into financial crime involving football, law firms and powerful business figures. Between 2015 and 2019, Pinto collected tens of millions of files containing sensitive information. He may be able to assist the SFO in identifying potential tax offences and other irregularities that would otherwise have gone undetected.

The development comes at a significant moment for the 38-year-old Pinto, with his future under Portugal’s witness protection programme uncertain.

Pinto rose to prominence by exposing some of the football industry’s most closely guarded secrets. These included Cristiano Ronaldo’s tax affairs, plans by Europe’s leading clubs to establish a breakaway European Super League and a series of controversial financial arrangements. His revelations triggered investigations and contributed to legal proceedings involving clubs and players across several countries.

More recently, documents collected and leaked by the whistleblower became relevant to the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City, which resulted in the club being found in breach of financial rules.

The information gathered by Pinto is in the possession of French authorities, who sought previously to include him in a witness protection programme. His arrest by Portuguese police in Hungary in January 2019 disrupted those plans, although France has maintained contact with him. Between his arrest in Hungary and his extradition to Portugal, French authorities travelled to Budapest and copied the contents of the electronic devices in his possession.

Pinto was informed on 30 September, just as his name had made headlines again after the City ruling, that he would no longer be protected by the Portuguese authorities after six years under the witness protection programme. Although the authorities maintained there was no threat to his life, he was advised not to express opinions on controversial issues, to avoid crowded places and to limit the time spent with family members.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Pinto was given 10 days’ warning, even though a decision had been taken in July, and the ruling’s implementation was suspended after it was established that he had not been given an opportunity to mount a challenge or appeal. He then appealed and is awaiting a final ruling.

In 2023 Pinto was given a suspended four-year prison sentence in Portugal for attempted extortion and cybercrime offences. He was acquitted in a second case involving similar charges two years later. The public prosecutor’s office and Benfica, one of the clubs hacked by Pinto, appealed against the ruling. A decision from the higher court is awaited.

Supporters regard Pinto as a whistleblower who cast light on corruption, whereas detractors argue that his tactics breached legal standards and moral principles. His disclosures reached far beyond football. Details involving magistrates, legal professionals and public officials were made public and he served as the whistleblower behind Luanda Leaks, which exposed the inner workings of the business empire of Africa’s richest woman, Isabel dos Santos. She denied corruption allegations.

Sports.title: Felix Nmecha denies goal celebrations promote ‘intolerance, discrimination and hate’
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund and Germany midfielder Felix Nmecha has responded to criticism of goal celebrations linked to an evangelical network by saying they’ve been misunderstood and are not meant to promote “intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form”.

Nmecha, a devout Christian, was criticised by the Dortmund official supporters’ group at the weekend for celebrating goals with a gesture signifying the “The King’s Return” campaign linked to Ballers in God (BIG), a network of Christian football players. The German public broadcaster ARD has linked BIG to ultra-conservative positions on issues including homosexuality and transgender identity.

“My celebration is not intended to promote myself or any organisation,” Nmecha wrote in a social media post on Tuesday. “Rather, it is about laying my ‘crown’ before the soon coming King and pointing to Jesus, my hope and strength. My message has never been about promoting intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form.

“As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for everyone, regardless of where they come from, what they believe, or what their worldview may be.”

In a statement, Dortmund official supporters’ group said: “We oppose religious networks that, under the guise of faith, propagate a worldview in which individuals are denigrated or excluded based on their sexual orientation, gender identity, way of life, or personal choices”.

Dortmund said on Sunday that it understood the fans’ concerns and would speak to Nmecha. “For Borussia Dortmund, it is essential to take the concerns and needs of the fanbase seriously and to address them,” read a statement. “Naturally, we also take the current media coverage and the associated questions and discussions very seriously.”

News agency DPA reported that Jürgen Klopp, Germany’s head coach, has already spoken to Nmecha about the issue at the national team camp in Herzogenaurach, Bavaria, before upcoming Nations League games.

Sports.title: Manchester City’s Kerstin Casparij: ‘I love football – but it takes over your life’
Sports.content:
Kerstin Casparij loves football, especially Champions League nights under the lights, but perspective is important too. “I would say football is my most important secondary thing in life, and I’ve found that such a refreshing way of looking at it,” she says before Manchester City’s trip to Milan to face Inter on Tuesday.

“It is so important to me and I love it so much and if I lose I’m going to have a terrible day, but my family’s healthy, my friends are healthy, I am, and I don’t have to worry about anything; I don’t have to worry about getting the food on the table. Being able to see things from that perspective makes it so much easier to stay the person I’ve always been.”

The 26-year-old Dutch full-back has had a phenomenal year, winning a first league title and FA Cup with Manchester City in her fourth season in England. Casparij was integral, having arguably her best season in the Women’s Super League, scoring three times and providing seven assists – the joint-most assists in the league with Aston Villa’s Lynn Wilms.

Key to her growth last season under Andrée Jeglertz was that “now I’m allowed to really play on almost the whole right side”, she says. “And I’m allowed to and trusted with pushing forward and taking risks in the final third.”

Like all team players, Casparij credits her teammates, but her contribution was recognised with a place on the Ballon d’Or shortlist. She finished in 24th place, the fifth-highest defender.

Being able to share these wins with her team outside the team is important too. They “work tirelessly to help me out”, she says. “Especially my partner, who is so invested in my career and has been such an incredible support and helped me out in more ways than I can count. There are so many incredible people around me and I’m just really happy I can give back to them as well, as much as I’m proud of myself for achieving it.”

Casparij’s authenticity, openness and playfulness have made her a fan favourite, not only at City but across the league. Her pun-loaded Instagram captions are as witty and self-critical after a defeat as they are sharp when City win. She is funny, shows fire on the pitch and is not afraid of banter with rivals, and is also a passionate advocate for the causes that matter to her, including as an LGBT Foundation patron and by sharing her experiences growing up with ADHD. Social media is a key tool for connecting.

View image in fullscreen Kerstin Casparij: ‘I’m allowed to and trusted with pushing forward and taking risks in the final third.’ Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

“I always want to be me and I want people that I knew 10 years ago to now speak to me and be able to be like: ‘Oh you haven’t changed a single bit, you’re still the same person.’ I have a lot of friends outside of football and it gives you such a sense of normality because football, the industry, is not normal and we are not necessarily normal.”

The connection with people matters because it cuts through the abnormality. “We’re in the spotlight every three days at times. We’re getting judged on our performance, we’re getting judged on how we do our work, so I kind of need that sense of normality to make sure I don’t take things too seriously and really keep both my feet on the ground.”

Having a partner who isn’t fazed by what comes with being a professional football player and understands the schedule and lifestyle is a big part of that. “I absolutely love football, I love everything about it, but it takes over your life and it’s definitely taken over ours,” she says. “You need a partner that understands that and loves it and is like: ‘Yeah, let’s do this together.’

“I’m so grateful for her and am so appreciative of her. She’s got weekends off but she doesn’t really have weekends off because they all revolve around me. Life revolves around me a lot and I try to make extra effort to make sure she knows it’s about her, too. We’re definitely a two-person team here, but to have her support and know she’s always there, she’s a massive part of my football journey.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That journey has taken her a long way from Heerenveen, for whom she made her debut at 15. Almost two years ago, when Casparij signed a new long-term City contract, she told the Guardian she felt she had unfinished business at the club. She wanted to win, so what did securing the Double in May feel like? “Incredible. It was such a long time coming and I’d been dreaming of that for so long.

“There was a big feeling of relief. We were very determined to win the league and I feel like we remained very calm for very, very long, pretty much up until the end. We just knew what we needed to do to get the job done and we made a big point of having a winning language. As a leadership team we started to talk about ‘when’ we win the league rather than ‘if’ to create an environment that believed and where everyone was going to do everything we could to win.”

View image in fullscreen Kerstin Casparij was 24th on this year’s Ballon d’Or rankings and the fifth-highest defender. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Whether City can retain their title is the big question. They did not play in the Champions League last season and there were questions before this campaign over whether they could juggle the workload. After nine games they are top and unbeaten, two points clear of Chelsea, who drew 1-1 with Everton at the weekend, before their meeting on Saturday at Stamford Bridge. City look as formidable as ever in attack but earned only their second clean sheet in their 5-0 defeat of West Ham on Saturday. In the Champions League, they have three draws from three games as they get reacquainted with the demands of European competition.

Were they aware of the doubts some had in pre-season? “Late last season some were still thinking we were going to bottle it,” Casparij says with a smile. “We see it. I’m not going to say we don’t, because we all follow the media, we all have social media, but it’s not something that gets really discussed very heavily. But it definitely adds fuel to our fire …

“It also allows us, as a team, to keep innovating, to keep thinking: ‘OK, what can we change? What can we improve? Where can we get better? Where do we sometimes need to tweak little things? What does the opponent do?’ And that’s the beauty of it and the fun part because it never gets boring.”

Sports.title: Djed Spence getting rave reviews for Inter Milan as Premier League legend pays huge compliment
Sports.content:
Djed Spence has been hailed for his impressive start in Serie A - prompting Paolo Di Canio to claim he can play 'blindfolded'.

After fitness issues caused him to miss the start of the season, the England international has quickly established himself at Inter Milan following his £30million summer switch from Tottenham.

4 Spence has featured seven times for Inter Milan in all competitions, providing two assists Credit: Getty

Spence secured a move to the Italian giants off the back of an impressive World Cup campaign with England.

He featured in all seven of the Three Lions' matches in North America, including four starts, as they finished third.

And while Spence struggled for fitness following his move to Inter - missing their first five league games - he is now showcasing exactly why the club shelled out for his services.

The full-back completed his third straight 90 minutes on Sunday in a 2-0 victory over Cesc Fabregas' in form Como side.

Spence played a key role in the victory by providing the assist for Pio Esposito's opener with an inch-perfect low cross, as well as fulfilling his defensive responsibilities with a clean sheet.

This was his second assist in as many games - having also done so in Inter's 3-0 Champions League win over Feyenoord last week.

And Spence's impressive displays have quickly been picked up on in Italy, with the defender earning rave reviews.

Spence form hailed

Spence's biggest compliment yet came on Sunday, when Premier League cult hero Paolo Di Canio praised his quality in Serie A.

Reacting to the match on Sky Sports Italy, Di Canio said: "Spence - he plays blindfolded in Italy... he plays with a blindfold on.

"But he was a starter at the World Cup for the world's third-best national team. We're not talking about just anyone... he's got a good left foot, technique."

4 Spence has also been called up for the England squad for the November international break, with it being the first time since the World Cup Credit: Getty

4 Di Canio suggested that Italian football is easy for Spence Credit: Getty

On Spence's assist against Como, the ex-Sunderland boss added: “The ball he puts in is a Premier League assist: a fiercely hit ball - either you score an own goal or my teammate scores.

“But he also has the technical ability to play out from the back.

“Then sometimes he'll switch off because he's a bit like that, but if they can get rid of that flaw, it'll be easier for him to play at wing-back with that athleticism, that quality and that technique."

'No match for Djed Spence'

Di Canio wasn't alone in his praise of Spence - European football expert Andy Brassell also hailed his display against a Como side flying high after an historic 9-1 Champions League win over Lens.

Inter’s win allowed the Italian champions to cement their second-place position in the table and move one point below leaders Lazio.

Appearing on talkSPORT, Brassell said of Como: “They were no match for Djed Spence, it turned out.

4 Spence has impressed both defensively and going forward in his brief time at Inter Milan Credit: Getty

"Inter taught them a lesson. Inter always teach them a lesson. Como have come a really long way, but they cannot beat Inter.

“They went to San Siro. Inter wanted to flex their muscles a bit - they did.

“[It was the] second assist for Spence in successive games. He's getting rave reviews in Italy at the moment since he's got himself fit.

“So he's doing really, really well there. And just underlining that even though Como have come a long way, Inter are the best team in the division.”

After some strong showings for Inter, Spence will now look to take his club form into the international break.

The 26-year-old was named in Thomas Tuchel's 25-man England squad for this week's Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain - which sees him return to the fold after injury forced him to miss the last camp.

Sports.title: Dejan Kulusevski rejected knee transplant and key Zlatan Ibrahimovic advice changed everything in injury hell
Sports.content:
Dejan Kulusevski discussed having a full knee transplant during his nightmare injury recovery - but he turned it down.

Kulusevski spent more than 500 days on the sidelines after suffering a serious knee injury at the end of the 2024/25 season.

4 Kulusevski spent over 500 days recovering from his serious knee injury that could have seen him have a full transplant

He suffered damage to his right patella and the cartilage within it, forcing him down a long road back to fitness that included two failed operations.

But the Tottenham winger incredibly managed to come out the other side of his rehabilitation, returning to action last month.

Kulusevski played his first minutes of competitive football since May 2025 against Coventry City on October 19.

Since then, he has made three more appearances for Spurs off the bench, as he works his way back up to speed.

It was a horrendous, long journey for the 26-year-old, who has received many deserved plaudits for his resilience.

And he has now revealed more details about his recovery, admitting that a knee replacement was a possibility for him at one stage.

Kulusevski rejected full knee transplant

Speaking to Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen, Kulusevski explained: "The answer to why it took so long is that there are people who have never even come back from injuries like this.

"Above all, we should be happy that it was possible to come back. There are many who have stopped playing their sport due to cartilage damage.

"Why it took so long is that we don’t know more. We did what we thought was best and it didn’t work. After that we had to try another operation. Then many people were nervous when they realized that it didn’t seem to work either.

“I spent the whole summer talking to other doctors about having another operation. It would have been a knee transplant.

4 Kulusevski revealed that he turned down the knee transplant in a decision that ended up paying off for him

"I would have exchanged my knee for someone else’s. I said no. If I’m in pain when I play, then I’ll have to play with pain.

"I trained and tried to live like a normal person. I trusted that it would work out. So far I’ve been right."

The Spurs star also revealed that if he has said yes to the transplant, he would have spent potentially another 18 months out.

"Nobody has ever come back from that, it’s 50/50’," he said. "I was like: ‘No, I don’t want to take it’.”

Ibrahimovic advice helped Kulsevski recover

Kulusevski added that Sweden legend Zlatan Ibrahimovic helped him decide what to do after rejected the transplant.

He was advised by the ex-Paris Saint-German, Barcelona and Manchester United striker to go and see a specialist in Serbia about his knee.

4 In the end, advice from Ibrahimovic meant Kulusevski travelled to Serbia where he was boosted by the doctor's commitment Credit: Getty

And he did, explaining: "Zlatan and (Ivan) Perisic wanted me to go there. I went there, and the Serb was important to me.

"He said: ‘Don’t think about other operations, we’re going to do this’. He was so sure of himself that it would work. I needed someone by my side who told me: ‘Dejan, this will work’."

On how he eventually found a solution to his injury, Kulusevski said: "Every day I tried to find out the answer, I couldn’t understand.

"But when we found out, it was complicated and not easy to solve. In the end, I got incredible help from many people involved.

"It’s really not just one person who helped me, I still work with maybe eight people today. There are many people who helped me.

"It was the nervous system, it was more than an injury. A deep, deep expertise from someone who is really good with the body and could resolve traumatised situations that happened to the body (helped) and after that the pain went away.”

4 Kulusevski admitted that he did doubt whether he would be able to play again, but he has incredibly fought back to return to the pitch

Did Kulusevski think he'd never play again?

Kulusevski further discussed the torture of his recovery too, opening up on whether he ever doubted that he could handle it.

"It hurt so much to walk up stairs," he said. "I trained ten hours a day but it didn't work, it didn't matter what I did. Then I started thinking: 'If it's over, it's over'.

"So I had to tell my mother: 'I don't think it's going to work'. To prepare her and the family. But in those days, things changed. And then when things got better, I felt like I could handle it.

The Sweden international continued: "There were many who didn't believe it, many were sceptical. Even at the club.

"But in the end I showed that I was getting better and stronger. And convinced them too.

"Whoever said I wouldn't come back doesn't know me. You could use that (talk) as fuel. But I believed in myself."

Sports.title: Insider gives update on Man City charges case as Sheikh Mansour pumps in £100m
Sports.content:
Insider gives update on Man City charges case as Sheikh Mansour pumps in £100m

We're still no closer to finding out when Manchester City will receive their punishment for their Premier League financial rules breach.

Man City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules in September before launching an immediate appeal.

4 Man City's case and appeal process after their guilty verdict remains 'complicated', as finance expert Borson provides the latest information Credit: Getty

The club are strong in their stance that they are innocent of the accusations and have 'irrefutable evidence' to prove it.

But following the verdict, there have been calls for their trophies from the period where breaches occurred - 2009 to 2018 - to be stripped and for them to be relegated from the top-flight.

Since the news broke of them being guilty on 114 charges though, no sanctions have been handed out to punish them.

And huge questions remain over whether they could end up facing further punishment or if they will be punished at all.

So, with fans wanting answers as soon as possible, what stage is the process at amid City's appeal and expected hearings?

What is the latest on Man City's case?

Football finance expert Stefan Borson told talkSPORT's White and Jordan: "There's a lot of confusion as to the exact stage that we're at.

"I've heard lots of different things, so I don't know whether they've had the sanction hearing or not had it.

"I was told by somebody who should know that there had been no sanction hearing as of last week.

"There's then the question of whether the sanction hearing is published or not.

"City will, I'm sure, try and argue it should've been published or that it shouldn't be binding or we shouldn't have a minus whatever, in the way we did with Everton and Nottingham Forest.

4 Borson thinks there may be an issue within the case that is causing things to be delayed, with the sanction hearing yet to get started Credit: Getty

"We've seen it crystallise with Everton and Nottingham Forest, so the Premier League may well argue that it should crystallise immediately (with Man City)."

When asked whether there's a date that the sanction will be revealed, Borson continued: "There's so many different aspects to what's going on right now, the level of litigation, appeal, other issues...

"The Premier League just brought on a guy, Sir James Eadie KC, who is the No.1 choice for government in these sorts of very technical, public law disputes, or judicial review type things.

"So there's obviously something going on in terms of an issue that requires a non-commercial KC to get involved.

"We just don't know what it is and there's just a number of different things it could be... it could be an appeal to part of the disciplinary section case, or it could be a Rule X arbitration, which is a challenge or an appeal to an appeal...

"It gets very complicated."

4 Amid the ongoing process, City owner Mansour has injected £100m into the club, but Borson isn't reading too much into it Credit: Getty

Mansour pumps £100m into Man City

Amid the ongoing appeal process, Man City have, of course, been continuing to play, albeit while facing some backlash.

Meanwhile, off the pitch, owner Sheikh Mansour has reportedly injected £100m into the City Football Group in a big financial boost to City and the other 11 clubs under the organisation's umbrella.

But Borson is reading too far into the new investment, revealing details on what the money may actually be used for.

"It's support clearly," Borson began. "But, first of all, it's into City Football Group (CFG), which is the parent company.

"Remember, these businesses are not making money and even more so CFG, as CFG has 12 clubs.

"One of them (New York City FC) is building a very big stadium in New York, so not only have they done a £400m development in Manchester, which is the stand, behind that the hotel and retail plaza, they're also building infrastructure in New York, so of course they need cash.

4 The cash injection from Mansour was made into City Football Group rather than just directly for Man City itself Credit: Getty

"The fact that he's putting money into CFG, there's no other option. Either he puts the money in or someone else does."

He added: "All of these clubs that you see raising capital, you see it across the league, these clubs are not generating profit.

"If you're not generating profit, clearly you need cash to pay the bills.

"That is the way these things work and it will continue. City will continue to need cash because there's a high cash burn, not just in Man City, but in the rest of the group."

Sports.title: Man United warned ‘unrealistic’ 100,000-seat stadium project is still a while away
Sports.content:
Man United warned ‘unrealistic’ 100,000-seat stadium project is still a while away

Manchester United’s bold plan to build a 100,000-seater stadium is still a long way off.

That’s the view of football finance expert Stefan Borson, who has cast an expert eye over the club’s cash flow.

4 Club chiefs have targeted 2035 as a completion date for the new stadium Credit: PA

The Red Devils revealed plans to build the biggest sporting arena in the UK just 350 metres away from Old Trafford in time for the 2035 Women’s World Cup, which is being staged in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

The plans to construct a ‘Wembley of the North’ have been estimated to cost around £2billion with wider regeneration of the area also scheduled.

In June, the club spent £63.5million acquiring a 25-acre site to allow the team to continue playing at Old Trafford whilst construction was underway.

But while United chiefs appear confident that the plans will be successfully carried out, Borson has taken a more reserved view on the project.

Speaking on White and Jordan on Tuesday, Borson revealed that the club’s owners, the Glazers, are considering selling the club.

And that could mean that any stadium plans may now fall into the hands of any prospective buyer.

Borson: Man United stadium plans are unlikely

“I’ve said for a while, the level of equity required, i.e. the investment from the shareholders required to even get close to building a project of that scale seems to me unrealistic,” Borson said.

“With the Glazers being happy to now exit, maybe, and INEOS’ own challenges, we've got interest rates going up, not down.

“The inflation risk around the world is still high, so therefore the risk of capital to build a stadium is higher than it’s been probably for the last 15 years.

“So how do they get to the point where they can raise £2-3billion to build a stadium of 100,000?”

4 The Glazers could be set to leave Old Trafford after 21 years of ownership Credit: AFP

Borson then revealed the financial reasons why clubs generally opt against building stadiums that exceed 80,000 spectators.

“There’s a reason why there’s so few 100,000 stadiums in the world, because that last 20,000 seats is extremely expensive to do,” he added.

“Most people build to 70 or 80,000 because the return you get from that incremental 20,000 isn’t there.

“Now United already have 75,000 but obviously it needs development.

“I suspect this will be a project that will be nicely left for the next buyer in a similar way to how it will be left at Chelsea again because of similar drivers about cost.”

United’s revenue streams will also play a key role in the stadium rebuild.

4 Man United continue to underperform under Carrick Credit: Getty

4 United fans made their feelings clear during Sunday's 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa Credit: Getty

Michael Carrick’s side can ill-afford missing out on the riches of the Champions League having made their return to the competition this season.

United sit in a play-off spot in the League Phase table but have been on the receiving end of a defeat against Atletico Madrid and a thumping 4-1 loss at Italian minnows Como.

The Red Devils sit 18th in the Premier League table and require a quick turnaround if they are to be in contention for next season’s Champions League.

Fans were seen holding a banner reading ‘We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners' during Sunday’s 4-4 draw against Aston Villa.

The sentiment shows an ongoing disconnect between the fans and the ownership.

Sports.title: Wrexham star forced to withdraw from international duty in another injury blow
Sports.content:
Wrexham star forced to withdraw from international duty in another injury blow

Wrexham striker Kieffer Moore has withdrawn from the Wales squad for the international break after picking up an injury.

Moore will play no part in his nation's upcoming games against Norway and Portugal this week due to a lower back issue.

2 Moore has withdrawn from the Wales squad after picking up a back issue in another injury blow for Wrexham Credit: Getty

The 34-year-old had been named in Craig Bellamy's squad for the Nations League ties, but he will now remain with Wrexham.

He will receive treatment and undergo rehabilitation with his club rather than travelling to be part of the Dragons' set-up.

Moore has featured in every one of Wrexham's games this seasons so far, scoring five goals in 16 appearances altogether.

The Welshman is Phil Parkinson's side's top scorer, but they will now be concerned that they could be without him.

Wrexham's injury nightmare

Moore was substituted after 77 minutes of their 1-1 draw with Wolves on Saturday, seemingly due to his knock that has now meant he has had to withdraw from the national squad.

Wrexham already have multiple key forwards recovering from injuries, so having another carrying an issue is a huge blow.

Fellow Wales international Nathan Broadhead is expected to remain out until December, while Josh Windass is out too.

Windass hasn't played a Championship game since October 10.

Summer signing Callum O'Hare is also suffering from an ankle problem that has seen him miss the last three games.

On top of that, Sam Smith is out for the entire season after an ACL injury, so Parkinson will be desperate not to lose Moore as well, with the severity of his back problem unknown at the moment.

2 Moore is Wrexham's top scorer this season amid multiple injuries to Parkinson's forward line this term Credit: Getty

Who has replaced Moore in the squad?

MK Dons striker Aaron Collins has taken Moore's place in the Wales squad, receiving his first international call-up.

Collins has scored 17 goals in 16 games in all competitions so far this season, topping the scoring charts in League One.

His 13 league goals see him three clear of any other player.

He could well make his Wales debut on Saturday as they take on Erling Haaland and Norway in Oslo at 5pm UK time.

Bellamy's side then face a Cristiano Ronaldo-less Portugal at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, November 17 at 7:45pm.

Ronaldo retired from international duty last week.

Sports.title: Premier League star receives first international call-up since officially confirming allegiance
Sports.content:
Eli Junior Kroupi has received his first call up Zinedine Zidane's France squad.

The Bournemouth star will replace the injured Marcus Thuram for Les Bleus in the upcoming Nations League fixtures against Italy and Turkey.



2 Kroupi Jr has been called up for Les Bleus senior duty for the first time Credit: Getty

He was given the nod ahead of Everton's in-form striker Thierno Barry after recently making his return from injury.

The news come just two week after the forward pledged his international allegiance to France.

Born in France, his mother is of Portuguese descent whilst his father played for the Ivory Coast.



Kroupi Jr was offered an opportunity to play for Portugal at the 2026 World Cup, but turned it down.

"Junior wanted to represent France, so we respect that," their former head coach Roberto Martinez said.



The 20-year-old has also played at all youth levels from U16 to U21 for France, and is now aiming to represent them at senior level.

Kroupi's plan was always to play for France

"I've always played for the French youth teams," he told DAZN. "I was born in France, I started playing football in France.



"I can't see myself moving to a culture I don't know! The French national team is the goal."

Kroupi Jr will be set to face strong competition for a starting role up front in the long term.

Kylian Mbappe is their all-time record scorer on 67 goals and already won 107 caps at the age of 27.

2 Kroupi Jr has made 39 appearances at youth level for France, but is yet to feature for the senior side Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Ousmane Dembele is also a regular for France, and Hugo Ekitike is also an option despite his long injury lay-off.

However, injuries to Thuram and Ousmane Dembele could see the forward handed his senior debut over the next week.

Zidane also named Rennes star Esteban Lepaul, who netted 21 goals last season, in his first squad last month.

Kroupi Jr has made four appearances for Bournemouth across all competitions so far this season.



He had surgery on a foot injury in the summer, but is slowly returning to full fitness.

Despite his call-up, Kroupi is yet to complete 90 minutes of football this term.

Sports.title: Jason Wilcox escaped infamous England Euro 96 ‘dentist chair’ night out alongside Neville brothers
Sports.content:
Manchester United director of football Jason Wilcox was among four England stars to escape the infamous ‘dentist’s chair.’

Wilcox was named in the squad of players to jet out to Hong Kong for a pre-Euro 96 warm-up tour.



6 Jason Wilcox was included in the provisional squad that travelled to Hong Kong prior to Euro 96 Credit: Getty

6 Terry Venables was met with a might distraction ahead of Euro 96 Credit: Getty

It was there that boss Terry Venables granted his side a night out in Hong Kong to let off some steam ahead of the tournament to be staged in England.

With football almost ready to come home, a night of fun and frolics quickly turned into a huge scandal after players were photographed being tied to a chair and fed copious amounts of alcohol.



Players including Paul Gascoigne, Teddy Sheringham, and Steve Howey took turns leaning back in a reclined chair while bar staff poured tequila and vodka into their mouths at the China Jump Bar.

The images of players wearing soaked in alcohol and sporting ripped shirts caused widespread condemnation ahead of the tournament and remained a talking point for the months following Euro 96.



Recalling that evening in Hong Kong, former England international Phil Neville revealed that senior dressing room figure David Platt, warned the younger players not to attend the bar in anticipation of what was to come.

Among the players that Platt advised not to attend the night out was Neville and his brother Gary, Nick Barmby and a young Wilcox.



Neville’s close call

“We were just kids, I was only 19 at the time,” Neville told The Times. “David Platt made a point of coming to Gary and I, and Nick Barmby and Jason Wilcox, advising us not to go on the night out that was being planned by the more senior players.

“Platty could smell that something was up. ‘It’s not a night for you guys,’” he said.

“Instead we went out for a pizza with Peter Beardsley.

“He often looked after the younger players and I remember his reaction when we told him we were going shopping after dinner to spend the bonus we were due from Manchester United for playing for England.

6 Phil Neville shared his memories of THAT night in Hong Kong Credit: Getty



6 Wilcox was one of England's in-form wingers going into Euro 96 Credit: Getty

“Not only could he not believe how much we were both being paid at the time — just £210 a week — but he was similarly stunned that we then wanted to blow the extra money on some watches for our parents and grandparents. To this day our mum still wears that watch.”

It was a close call for Wilcox who was starring for Blackburn Rovers at the time and one that could have brought about a premature end to his international career.

Wilcox spent nine years at Ewood Park and was part of the 1995 Premier League title winning side.



He went on to make three appearances for England with his first cap coming in a 3-0 win over Hungary in 1996.

But he was not included in England’s final 22-man squad for Euro 96, a decision that Venables described as one of the toughest of his managerial career.

Gazza’s 'dentist's chair' celebration

After netting England’s second goal against Scotland in their Euro 96 group game at Wembley, Gascoigne produced one of the all-time iconic celebrations.

6 Wembley erupted when Gascoigne fired England into a 2-0 lead against Scotland Credit: Getty



6 He was then swamped by teammates as he performed the dentist's chair celebration

Shortly after running away in jubilation, the midfielder laid on the pitch, head up and arms out wide with his mouth open, mimicking that night in Hong Kong.

Alan Shearer, Steve McManaman and Jamie Redknapp joined Gazza in celebration by grabbing a water bottle and squirting its contents into his mouth.

"There were about nine of us who did the dentist's chair in Hong Kong, but obviously, being the person I am, I'm the one who got hammered for it," Gascoigne later said.



"For some reason, in the second game against Scotland, I just said, 'right guys, whoever scores does the Dentist's Chair' and fortunately for me, it was me.

"The lads were clued in and it was good. It's just a shame it was lucozade in that bottle and not gin... I'm only joking!"

Sports.title: Where to watch England v Croatia as Harry Kane prepares to make history
Sports.content:
Where to watch England v Croatia as Harry Kane prepares to make history

Thomas Tuchel's England are preparing to play their final two games of 2026 with Harry Kane set to surpass Peter Shilton's appearance record.

The Three Lions boss named his 25-man squad last Friday and Ballon d'Or winner Kane is set to become the most-capped Three Lions player after he equalled Shilton's appearance record of 125 in October.

4 Kane equalled the record appearances for England last time out against Croatia Credit: Getty

The squad also includes two first-time call-ups with Borussia Dortmund's Jobe Bellingham, and Fulham's Josh King.

King already has experience with the senior squad, having travelled stateside in the summer to be a part of the pre-World Cup training camp in Florida.

Jobe joins his under-21 teammate after impressing for Dortmund this season, and will be alongside his brother Jude for the national team for the first time.

England will be hoping to seal their place in the Nations League quarter-finals next March by finishing either first or second in the group.

Tuchel's side currently sit in second place in Group C and only need to avoid defeat to Slaven Bilic's Croatia to progress in the competition.

Where to watch England v Croatia

The fixture will kick-off at 7:45pm on Thursday November 12 at Wembley Stadium.

It will be shown on free-to-air television and will be live on ITV1, with build-up starting from 7pm.

Fans can listen to live commentary of the match on talkSPORT, with Adrian Durham, Jim Proudfoot and former England captain Stuart Pearce.
