4 Tuchel will hope to end 2026 on a high with England Credit: Getty

England vs Croatia team news

Ezri Konsa will not feature in Thursday’s clash with Croatia at Wembley and will continue to follow his own training programme before hopefully returning prior to the Spain match up on Sunday.

Additionally, Manchester City’s Marc Guehi pulled out of the squad through injury leading to Dan Burn’s late inclusion.

Bournemouth defender James Hill will provide Tuchel with a further defensive option alongside Newcastle captain Burn, Konsa, Jarrad Branthwaite and Jarell Quansah.

The England boss can also call upon Ben White, Lewis Hall, Djed Spence and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Tuchel has revealed he could again split goalkeeping responsibilities between Jordan Pickford and James Trafford for the two fixtures.

While England's No.1 shirt has been largely undisputed since Pickford entered the fold in 2017, the last international break saw himself and Trafford share the minutes.

The Leeds keeper's increased game time for the Three Lions has fueled speculation over a potential changing of the guard in goal.

4 Tuchel is hoping to watch two of his goalkeeping options in action this week Credit: Getty

However, Tuchel has insisted that Pickford remains first-choice for now.

He said: "Pickford is number one, but nothing has changed. The competition is on there as well, like for the outfield players.

"They shared the matches last time. I’m not sure what we will do. There’s an opportunity that we maybe do this again. I have to speak with our goalkeeper coach."

He added: "When do I have a chance to see another goalkeeper, if not in Nations League? If not in high pressure matches?

"So we had James against Spain [a 3-2 defeat]. Because what happens if Jordan Pickford is injured? What happens if he’s not available? So it’s better to test it.

"Jordan knows about this, that we want to use Nations League for exactly that.

"But at the moment, nothing has changed. At the moment, he’s the number one. And he just feels a bit of competition. Which is good for him."

Sports.title: PREM Rugby transfers: Bristol want Alfie Barbeary as Saracens face losing three stars, Sale eye Gloucester scrum-half, Exeter set to tie down international trio... and Eddie Jones reveals 'dream' to switch codes and coach in NRL
Sports.content:
The transfer market for rugby's top No8s is hotting up with Alfie Barbeary, Arthur Green, Bill Mata and Callum Chick all weighing up their next moves.

Barbeary, who only joined Saracens from Bath this summer, has a break clause in his contract in north London and is understood to be on Bristol’s radar.

Pat Lam’s Bears are considering their options as Fijian back-rower Mata reaches the end of his contract. The former Edinburgh man is currently sidelined until the new year with a serious knee injury.

Bath youngster Arthur Green is another back-row forward being courted by clubs throughout the PREM. The 22-year-old’s stock has risen this season and Bristol, Saracens and Northampton are among the clubs interested in signing him. Green, whose father Will was a prop for Wasps, Leinster and England, has been capped at Under-18 and Under-20 level by his country.

Meanwhile, Northampton could lose Chick to France due to budgetary pressures, having already agreed improved contract terms with the likes of England trio Henry Pollock, Tommy Freeman and Archie McParland.

The 29-year-old, who won two England caps in 2021, lifted the PREM Rugby title with Saints last season in his debut campaign in the East Midlands, having left his boyhood club Newcastle the previous summer.

Alfie Barbeary could leave Saracens after just one season, due to a break clause in his contract

Fiji back-rower Bill Mata is approaching the end of his Bristol contract and is currently sidelined until the new year

Callum Chick won two England caps in 2021 but he could be forced to move to France next summer due to budgetary pressures at Northampton Saints

Sale in for Cherries' scrum-half

Sale are exploring a move for Gloucester scrum-half Caolan Englefield to boost their quota of English-qualified players.

Englefield represented England A in a 59-24 win over an Argentina XV last week and Sale coach Alex Sanderson is known to be a keen admirer.

The Manchester club were keen to recruit South African Embrose Papier, but he turned down a move to the PREM and signed a new deal with the Pretoria-based Bulls.

Sale already have New Zealander Xavier Roe signed up for next season, but team-mate Gus Warr is considering a move to Edinburgh that would boost his Test prospects with Scotland. Edinburgh are also in talks with Leicester prop Will Hurd.

Englefield is not the only player reaching the end of his contract at Gloucester. Centre Will Joseph, who could win his second England cap this weekend against Japan, is drawing interest from Saracens, Bath and Newcastle.

Lock Arthur Clark is in negotiations about a new deal but has attracted interest from Harlequins, who need to beef up their front five.

Sale are exploring a move for Gloucester and England A scrum-half Caolan Englefield to boost their quota of English-qualified players

Chiefs lock down three superstars

Exeter Chiefs are closing in on a triple contract extension for star trio Henry Slade, Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Dafydd Jenkins.

The Chiefs have new financial investment from Black Knight, who also own Premier League club Bournemouth, and are keen to lock down their top assets.

England wing Feyi-Waboso and Wales lock Jenkins, both 23, are understood to have already committed their futures to the club – while a new contract has been offered to 24-year-old winger Paul Brown-Bampoe.

Slade has stated his desire to activate an extension clause in his contract, telling Daily Mail Sport: ‘I would have no problem spending my whole career at Exeter. That would be very cool. You never know but I've got a plus one that I'm sure we're going to be talking about fairly soon. I'm in year 16 now and I’ve loved all of it. My family are here, my wife’s family is here, we’ve got babysitters on the doorstep.’

Heavyweight Chiefs centre Zack Wimbush has also been offered a new contract, but the 6ft 6in youngster is weighing up interest from PREM leaders Leicester.

Exeter are looking to tie down England stars Henry Slade (left) and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso (right)

Wales lock Dafydd Jenkins, 23, is also close to committing his future to the Chiefs

Pumas to leave north London

Argentina duo Juan Martin Gonzalez and Lucio Cinti are likely to leave Saracens this summer.

Clashes with Los Pumas' fixture schedule are understood to be a major stalling point in negotiations around new contracts.

Bath back-row Josh Bayliss has been proposed as a replacement for Gonzalez – although the Scotland international is keen to remain at The Rec.

Taine Basham is also eyeing up a move to the PREM but that would likely make the 27-year-old ineligible to represent Wales – he still needs to play eight more times for his country to hit the 25-cap threshold to qualify as an overseas-based player.

Argentina back-rower Juan Martin Gonzalez (right) is likely to leave Saracens

Lucio Cinti (centre) is also set to depart the StoneX Stadium

Eddie eyes NRL

Eddie Jones has revealed his ambitions to coach rugby league in the NRL.

The 66-year-old former England, Australia and Saracens head coach is contracted to Japan until the end of next year's World Cup but has no intentions to step into retirement.

He told Daily Mail Sport he has no desire to take up an advisory role with a PREM club but would love to challenge himself in the alternative code.

‘I’ve done my time in England,’ said Jones. ‘I’ve done Saracens, I’ve done England and that’s it for me. French rugby used to be dominated by foreigners but that’s changed now.

‘What I’d love to coach is NRL. That’s my dream. I was brought up in rugby league, and rugby league in Australia has gone through the roof. It's on a different dimension to union now. It's by far the most glamorous, entertaining game.

‘The risk for rugby is that all the Tongan and Samoan kids could go to rugby league. We could lose two great countries in rugby and that’s a challenge. We need to make our game more entertaining. We don't want to become an old people's game.’

Meanwhile, Japanese hooker Kenji Sato is understood to be on the radar of several PREM clubs.

Eddie Jones has revealed his ambitions to coach rugby league in the NRL

Will Sarries swoop for Sinckler?

The future of exiled England prop Kyle Sinckler remains unresolved.

The 33-year-old has flourished at Toulon since moving to France in 2024 but he is desperate to be in contention for the World Cup.

His services have been offered around the PREM but clubs are struggling to find the budget for his salary demands.

Saracens are understood to be one potential destination for the tighthead, who grew up in south London.

Tier Two talents on PREM radars

Scouts have been casting a curious eye over Nations Cup fixtures in a bid to unearth the next gem.

Tier Two rugby often provides rich pickings for talent, with former Saracens forward Theo McFarland a prime example of a player signed straight from Samoa.

Back-rower Niko Jones, the son of legendary former All Black Michael, and scrum-half AJ Lam, the nephew of Bristol head coach Pat, have both received positive references from the Samoan management.

Samoa scrum-half AJ Lam is tackled against Zimbabwe last week in Wakefield. He has received a positive reference from the Samoan management

Uruguay flanker Manuel Ardao (pictured making a tackle against Spain) is also highly rated

Portuguese full-back Simao Bento, whose team host Samoa in Lisbon this weekend, is on the radar of clubs around Europe and Uruguay flanker Manuel Ardao, who once won five turnovers against Scotland, is also highly regarded. From Tonga, back-rower Sam Tuitupou Jr has been backed to land a major contract.

Zimbabwe forwards Victor Mupunga and Godfrey Muzanargwo and teenage Georgian back Luka Tabatadze are also names that clubs have been told to keep an eye on.

Zimbabwe face Uruguay on Saturday at Ealing Trailfinders' ground, while Tonga travel to Tbilisi to take on Georgia. The Nations Cup regional groups are led by the USA and Georgia, who both have four wins from four.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham says he 'wants to be a gentleman' but admits he doesn't feel 'mature' because 'I can't cook, I can't drive and I rely on my family' in new smouldering photoshoot
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham says he 'wants to be a gentleman' but admits he doesn't feel 'mature' because 'I can't cook, I can't drive and I rely on my family' in new smouldering photoshoot

Real Madrid and England star Jude Bellingham has admitted he doesn't feel 'mature', despite being labelled as such from a young age.

The midfielder, 23, has impressed with his level head and assured public speaking since breaking onto the professional scene at 16 and living under the glare of the public eye in his formative years.

But Bellingham has confessed that his complete attention to detail as a footballer has left deficiencies in other areas of his life, such as cooking or driving.

Speaking to Vogue in an interview accompanying a fashion photoshoot in which he's dressed to fit the 60s and 70s aesthetic he leans into, Bellingham also spoke about his desire to be a role model for the younger generation.

'I feel mature in a football context because I’ve played nearly 400 games, but in a life context I don’t feel that mature now, to be honest,' he told Vogue.

'I can’t cook, I can’t drive… I’m good at what I do, but everything else? Not that great. I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff – chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else.

Jude Bellingham poses for Vogue during a photoshoot displaying his love of 60s fashion

Bellingham admits he isn't mature in some areas of his life - seen here holding up his provisional driving licence

'That’s where I’m at. I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home, I’ve probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. But there’ll be a time and a place for that, I’m sure.'

Bellingham plays with a fierce competitive spirit on the pitch but is aware of his responsibility to behave away from football, adding: 'I’ve always said that, off the pitch, I want to be a gentleman.'

The Real superstar, who is in a relationship with American influencer and model Ashlyn Castro, went on: 'You can’t just behave how you want but then still represent a city or a country every time you wear their shirt, because you are inspiring [someone].

'Whether you like it or not, you are looked up to by the next generation. I prefer to see it as a privilege.'

The photoshoot for the fashion magazine showcased Bellingham's sense of style, which he says is rooted in his admiration for iconic characters from the 60s and 70s such as Elvis Presley, Michael Caine and James Bond movies of the era.

The Vogue cover shows Bellingham in a dark brown suit and coat with wide lapels and a bright orange cardigan, while he appears in a herringbone overcoat and white chino shorts in another.

Another image shows Bellingham holding up his green provisional driving licence.

Bellingham, selected in the England squad for upcoming internationals against Croatia and Spain, is in a rich vein of form.

Bellingham is pictured in a sharp suit and says he is inspired by iconic figures of yesteryear

The cover star feels a responsibility to be a gentleman and positive role model

Under Jose Mourinho's management at the Bernabeu this season, he's scored four goals and provided four assists already in LaLiga, with the Spanish giants three points behind Barcelona in the title race.

He's joined in the England squad by his younger brother, Jobe, and is flying high for the national side now his relationship with Tuchel is on an even keel.

Last Friday, the Three Lions manager said: 'It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place.

'I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable he would not perform on that level.

'In the moment you see he's happy to come into camp, he's happy with the role he has, he's fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach!'

On Jobe being called up from the Under-21s, he added: 'Yeah Jude and I have spoken about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream to play with Jobe for England.

'Jude was always saying: "Watch him, watch him he's good, he can make it". 'I would say: "Yeah we are watching him".

Bellingham poses in more casual attire, pairing a vintage Adidas sweater with pin stripe trousers

'I think he actually watched training very early in my reign. He came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and said it would be nice if one day he was with him.

'He was very kind and very polite and I'm glad to have him in camp. Everyone will compare them and he has to live with this.

'They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. Jobe is more defensive. I think they are also different characters, at least that's what I heard.

'He couldn't stop smiling when I called to tell him the news. He has the same beautiful smile like Jude so it's nice to have him.'

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Jim Ratcliffe makes new 'brutal' cutbacks to ex-players' charity, Nathan Collins and Calvin Bassey among January targets, Luke Shaw eyes Anfield return and why club confiscated two anti-owner banners
Sports.content:
Man United Confidential: Jim Ratcliffe makes new 'brutal' cutbacks to ex-players' charity, Nathan Collins and Calvin Bassey among January targets, Luke Shaw eyes Anfield return and why club confiscated two anti-owner banners

Sir Jim Ratcliffe is known for being ruthless – as Michael Carrick may be about to find out – and it appears as though the Association of Former Manchester United Players has once again paid the price.

Two years ago, Ratcliffe made front-page news at Christmas after it emerged he was cutting a yearly £40,000 donation to the AFMUP charity, which has been helping ex-United players since 1985.

Last week organisers were informed at the last minute that the second of its two annual dinners couldn’t be staged as usual in the Manchester Suite at Old Trafford and would have to move elsewhere.

So while plans were being made for Sir Alex Ferguson’s glittering 40th anniversary bash in the Heritage Suite on Friday night, the AFMUP had to rely on Hotel Football – part-owned by Gary Neville and the Class of ’92 – coming to the rescue to host their event over the road 24 hours earlier. Ferguson, it has to be said, has been a big supporter of the charity over the years.

There are now concerns that AFMUP will never be allowed back to Old Trafford with United understood to be insisting on a total of 400 guests, which is double what the charity can provide.

Previously, the AFMUP gave half of the £40,000 donation back to the club to hire the suite in April and September, raising additional funds through ticket sales and auctions.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left) is known for being ruthless and it appears as though the Association of Former Manchester United Players has once again paid the price

When Neville challenged Ratcliffe over the ‘cruel decision’ to cut the donation in a one-on-one interview in March last year and said the club should consider organising the dinner itself and asking current players to attend, the minority owner replied: ‘Well nobody suggested that, I would have supported that.’

As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada joined Ferguson and former CEO David Gill at the dinner the following month – when Neville, Andy Cole and Jonny Evans were also present – and donated a VIP package for the auction worth £20,000.

Director of football Jason Wilcox then appeared at the next event in September and gave a rare interview on stage. In April of this year, Bryan Robson and Steve Bruce formed a popular double act as the main attraction.

Thursday’s dinner, which had already been moved from September 24 due to a double booking, was a celebration of the life of Duncan Edwards, who would have been 90 on October 1. Former chairman Martin Edwards and Gill were both present along with former goalkeeper Alex Stepney.

The AFMUP’s official filmmaker and publicist John Gubba highlighted the latest setback on his Man Utd The Religion YouTube channel, saying: ‘While the red carpet is being rolled out for Fergie, the club have been brutally abandoning the former players’ association.

‘The latest cutbacks by Sir Jim Ratcliffe have resulted in another kick in the teeth for the AFMUP. Staging their big event at the Theatre of Dreams was always a status that made the former players and their guests feel part of the football club. Being turfed out at short notice leaves a bitter taste.’ You can watch the full video here.

United sources say the club helped to facilitate an alternative venue at Hotel Football due to unavailability in the stadium, and insist that the charity will be welcome back to Old Trafford in future.

Omar’s culture club

Berrada was present at Ferguson’s celebration dinner on Friday in which the United chief executive spoke about the importance of building a culture at Old Trafford.

He was one of 100 invited guests for the event to mark 40 years since Ferguson was appointed as United manager, moving from Aberdeen to replace Ron Atkinson in November 1986.

A number of Ferguson’s old players were present and posed for pictures with him including Michael Carrick, Brian McClair, Edwin van der Sar, Robin van Persie, David May, Wes Brown, Paul Parker, Dion Dublin, Denis Irwin, Jesper Blomqvist, Ryan Giggs, Gary Pallister, Javier Hernandez, Clayton Blackmore, Jonny Evans, John O’Shea, Darren Fletcher, Ronny Johnsen, Lee Martin, Nemanja Vidic and Quinton Fortune.

Ferguson’s former No2 Mike Phelan was also there along with Gill and kit man Albert Morgan.

There were 100 invited guests for the event to mark 40 years since Sir Alex Ferguson (third right) was appointed as United manager in November 1986

Shaw eyes Anfield return

Luke Shaw is targeting a return to action away at Liverpool a week on Sunday, Confidential understands.

The 31-year-old has not featured since October 10 when he played 90 minutes against Tottenham, missing seven games through to the current international break.

That absence badly exposed United's lack of depth at left back, an area the hierarchy failed to address in the transfer window despite a clear need. Diogo Dalot, who was targeted by fans when he came off against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, has played poorly while filling in on his unfavoured side.

With Patrick Dorgu now back in the mix, too, Shaw is hoping to be in contention for the trip to Anfield in what would be a timely boost for a defence that has conceded the joint-most goals in all competitions of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

Defenders on Reds’ radar

Nothing has undermined Carrick's time as United head coach more than the defensive problems that have seen his team concede 15 goals in their last five games.

United chose to delay the overhaul of their defence until next year when they focused on rebuilding the midfield last summer, but it has proved to be a costly misjudgment with Matthijs de Ligt only just returning to action after a year out and a spate of injuries to Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui.

It may force United into the transfer market in January and Confidential understands Brentford centre back Nathan Collins and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey have joined Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton on the list of potential targets.

United also want a striker after failing to offload Joshua Zirkzee and sign cover for Benjamin Sesko in the summer, but a loan deal is more likely.

Brentford's Nathan Collins and Fulham's Nigeria star Calvin Bassey have both joined United's list of centre-back targets

Relegation kit-astrophe

As if the prospect of relegation isn’t nightmarish enough for United after they dropped to 18th place in the table, the cost of going down would be astronomical.

Although parachute payments from the Premier League would cushion the fall in the unlikely event that United are relegated, kit sponsors adidas have the option to scrap their record £900million, 10-year deal which was announced in 2023 but only came into effect last year.

Under the terms of the contract, the German sportswear giant can cancel it if they give the club one year’s notice. Adidas can also halve their annual payment to £45m if United aren’t playing in the Premier League, and hit the club with a £10m annual penalty if they are not in the Champions League.

Banner clampdown

Two banners protesting against United’s owners were confiscated by stewards during Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

One that read ‘Jim Can’t Fix This’ was seized because its connection to Jimmy Savile was deemed to be inappropriate. Another declaring ‘We Don’t Want A New Stadium, We Want New Owners’ was taken down because it was blocking the view of some fans.

Club insiders say protests will always be allowed as long as they remain within the regulations. United kept a close eye on Sunday’s demonstration with a more visible police presence in the Stretford End and stewards asking fans as they entered that section of the stadium which group they were with.

The protest, which once again involved green and gold balloons being released before kick-off, was jointly organised by The Red Army, The 1958, Manchester United Youth Supporters Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds.

However, it seemed like a strange decision to confiscate the banners considering that United were in possession of them for more than 30 hours before kick-off since 10am on Saturday morning.

They are stored in the same place in the Stretford End before every game, so it was odd for United to demand that they be taken down when they could have refused for them to be handed out in the first place.

A banner protesting against United's owners was confiscated during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa

Onana’s word perfect

While goalkeeper Senne Lammens was giving his worst performance in a United shirt against Villa on Sunday, the man he replaced at Old Trafford was faring a little better in Turkey.

Andre Onana kept a clean sheet in Trabzonspor’s win over Alanyaspor as they moved into second place in the Super Lig table behind Galatasaray.

It came three days after a Europa League defeat by Freiburg when Onana couldn’t resist a little light ribbing of English reporters at the game.

Asked by journalists from Daily Mail Sport and the BBC for a quick word, the Cameroon international didn’t disappoint. ‘I don’t speak English, bro,’ Onana said, in perfect English. Classic.

Sports.title: Alisson, 34, reveals he wants to STAY at Liverpool after rolling back the years against Crystal Palace... but is extending the goalkeeper's contract the right call, asks LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker insists he wants to stay at the club after his contract expires at the end of this season.

The Brazilian, now 34, put in a throwback performance in the Reds’ win at Crystal Palace on Sunday with some fine stops to keep his side in the game at 0-0 before the big-money attackers did their job at the other end.

It came after a period where Alisson has been questioned by fans for a string of errors in what is his final contracted year at the club. And the No1 has now opened up on his future for the first time.

Asked if he wants to stay beyond the end of the season, Alisson said: ‘Yes, in my mind. I’m focused on playing every game but in my mind I’m happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations.

‘But my will is to stay. I’m happy here, my family is happy here. I’m still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that’s my thinking on that.’

Alisson later added that his agent has held talks with the club over a new deal.

The 34-year-old keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window

The keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window, which he admits is a decision taken somewhat beyond his will.

He said: ‘It is beneficial (not going), for sure. You have to use it right because you have a lot of time so if you don’t train, if you don’t prepare, time goes really quick and you need to stay sharp.

‘It’s not that I will sit on the couch for a week and then come back training. I still have to work hard but in my mind I can use the time to relax and be more with my family.

‘It’s a little bit against my will. What I always want is to be with the national team but I understand this is what I have at the moment and I will use this time and take the benefit from the rest.’

Should Liverpool continue in Alisson wonderland?

By Lewis Steele

It is tempting to just say ‘yes’ and end this debate there.

Alisson is still the best goalkeeper Liverpool have on their books and, even though he is maybe not as solid as he once was, the 34-year-old remains one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

Last summer, he flirted with the idea of leaving and seriously considered a move to Juventus. Alisson speaks fluent Italian from his time at AS Roma and held talks with the Turin club over a return.

But Liverpool triggered a clause in his deal to extend his stay by a year. With several big names leaving such as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konate and Curtis Jones, the club did not want another experienced head to depart and leave a leadership vacuum.

They have also spent the last three years succession planning for Alisson’s long-term replacement and have signed a number of goalkeepers for more than £60million combined.

Giorgi Mamardashvili is the most obvious in the pecking order. He has had mixed reviews with fans but the Georgian is appreciated more internally than maybe externally. The club believes he has several levels left to step up.

Lucca Brughmans will join from Belgian side Genk after a £28.3million deal was struck. Liverpool genuinely think he is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him.

Liverpool think Lucca Brughmans - who will join them from Belgian side Genk - is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him

They have also signed highly-rated Armin Pecsi and England youth goalkeeper Zach Trinder from Wolves.

Clearly, the post-Alisson future is sorted, with some of them tipped to go far in the game. But are any of them better than Alisson now? No. Will any of them be better next season? No.

Alisson missed 54 games across the previous two seasons with injury and illness, according to Transfermarkt, but his omission from Brazil camps and a specialised pre-season programme mean the keeper seems to have put his issues behind him. Touch wood.

For that reason, a one-year extension makes sense – for both Alisson and 35-year-old captain Virgil van Dijk. The club will have to face up to a future without both of their defensive stalwarts but, for now, they remain the best in class.

Sports.title: Australia DID tamper with the ball during 2017-18 Ashes just before 'Sandpapergate' scandal - and the whole team knew, admits former player Usman Khawaja
Sports.content:
Australia were doctoring the ball against England in the 2017-18 Ashes according to the latest revelations from Usman Khawaja’s whistle-blowing autobiography.

Within the chapter of the newly-released Sabr that covers the explosive claim that all of the Australian team were in on the sandpaper scandal in South Africa eight years ago, Khawaja goes on to reveal that ball tampering was embedded in the dressing room during the 4-0 series win over England that preceded it.

England’s players suspected that Australia had altered the condition of the ball in the third Test at Perth when despite heavy rain, the home attack managed to extract extravagant reverse swing to dismiss Joe Root’s side on the final day.

Reverse swing is most typically generated when the dry nature of the playing square scuffs up one side of the ball and the other is polished vigorously by the players on their trousers, using a combination of that friction and the application of sweat to create a smooth sheen.

However, Khawaja reveals that an attack featuring Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, and Josh Hazlewood plus off-spinner Nathan Lyon had found other ways to get the ball moving off the straight in Adelaide and Perth that winter.

‘On day five, Starcy bowled that unforgettable ball to James Vince off the crack,’ he wrote.

Former Australia star Usman Khawaja claims all of the Australia team knew about the ball-tampering during the 2017-18 Ashes series

‘We were reverse swinging it late on day five. Actually, we were reverse swinging the ball the game before too - except it was much tougher, because it was the pink ball.

‘But we - and I say 'we', because were a team, whether you did the deed or not - had worked out that, if we raised the flaps up on the quarter seam on that ball, it was almost like it had a rudder on it and it'd start reverse swinging.

‘And before you start going at me, calm down. The whole world was doing whatever little they could to try and reverse swing the ball.’

Despite Khawaja’s caveat that such practice was commonplace, under Law 41.3 of the Laws of Cricket, players are strictly prohibited from taking any deliberate action that artificially alters the physical condition of the match ball.

Either prising up, scratching or deteriorating the quarter seam - the secondary seam on the ball that runs at a right angle to the prominent stitched one, and there to secure the leather pieces together - with fingernails, thumbs or foreign objects is illegal and punishable by match officials. A player caught in such an act can face a substantial fine and/or suspension.

If the quarter seam is raised, it can create a tiny flap of leather on the rough side of the ball, which disrupts the air flow on that side, and manufacturing reverse swing that would not occur naturally as a result.

Suspicion was raised in the away dressing room at the famous WACA ground when Australia overcame a three-hour rain delay on day five to pick off England's remaining six wickets for an Ashes-sealing victory that evening.

Only days after Australia’s skulduggery in Cape Town was exposed, leading to lengthy bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, former England captain Alastair Cook revealed the hunch.

David Warner has supported Khawaja's claims, saying they are '100 per cent accurate'

Emphasising the huge differential in lateral movement achieved by the rival bowling attacks the previous winter, Cook said: ‘We did think in Perth, when the outfield was wet after the rain, how had they managed to get the ball reversing?

‘I didn't see anything, (but) we've been pretty good on the ball, managing the ball so that it can reverse swing at certain times. Jimmy (Anderson) is obviously very good at reverse swinging, we got it going a touch at Melbourne either way, but with those drop-in pitches we didn't get it going massively.’

Khawaja’s confirmation of the Australian dressing room culture follows Daily Mail Sport’s exclusive story in the aftermath of the Cape Town sting that David Warner had relayed tampering methods to England players over a drink at the end of the Ashes - an episode Cook personally reflected on in his own autobiography the following year.

It emerged earlier this week that, according to Khawaja, Australia had used sandpaper at Port Elizabeth - in the Test match that preceded the powder keg Newlands contest.

He also states in his book that the entire Australian team were in on the malpractice, not just the trio that were punished - a claim that Warner said was ‘100% accurate.’

However, breaking the silence of the four bowlers who released a statement in 2021 denying prior knowledge of a foreign object being brought onto the field in Cape Town, Starc said his recollection of events had not changed.

‘As far as our statement said, we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field, that’s where I’ll leave it,’ Starc said.

‘We weren’t aware anything was taken on to the field to be tampered with. We saw (the sandpaper) on the big screen in Cape Town.

‘As far as the book is concerned, I haven’t read it. I probably won’t read it. So that’s for Usman to elaborate on. I’ll stick to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time, eight years ago. Clearly, there’s different versions from different people, and I’ll leave it where I left it back then.’

The revisiting of sandpapergate has left a significant proportion of the Australian public demanding another probe, after Warner slammed the original eight years ago as ‘rushed and botched.’

However, Cricket Australia insisted it will not be reopening the investigation, with the organisation’s chief executive Todd Greenberg saying that there was not ‘any compelling reason’ to do so, despite Khawaja’s version of events contradicting previous ones to have made the public domain.

Ex-Australia captain Michael Clarke is leading the calls to revisit the inquiry into a team whose reputation is arguably already irreparably damaged, saying fans have not been able to move on from it.

‘They can't trust what's real. They don't know the truth until this gets reopened and the truth comes out,' Clarke told 2DayFM.

‘Now we've got this opportunity. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to finally tell the truth, and move on.’

While Smith and Warner were suspended for 12 months and lost their rights to leadership upon return and Bancroft - who was caught on camera trying to conceal the sandpaper in his trousers - was for nine months, no other Australian player or coaching staff member was censured.

But Bancroft’s response to being asked, in a 2021 British newspaper interview, if the bowlers’ knew - ‘it’s probably self-explanatory - reopened the festering sore of Australia’s past and triggered the unusual joint statement from Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon.

Now, courtesy of Khawaja’s determination for collective accountability, they face questions regarding their conduct in cricket’s most revered series of them all.

Sports.title: Man United chiefs set for Monaco summit TOMORROW to decide Michael Carrick's fate... with manager taking training today despite facing the sack
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick’s fate as Manchester United head coach is set to be decided on Wednesday when chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

Berrada and Wilcox will make their recommendation to Ratcliffe, with all the indications pointing to Carrick being sacked after United dropped into the relegation zone.

It’s understood that the Old Trafford hierarchy would want to inform Carrick of their decision face to face, so there may not be any confirmation from the club until Thursday.

The 45-year-old turned up for work at Carrington at 7.15am on Tuesday to oversee training with the players who are not away on international duty amid increasing uncertainty over his future.

United sources maintain that a final decision has yet to be made, with the club reluctant to engage in a running commentary over Carrick's position.

The manager's position increasingly precarious after they dropped into the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

It left him with just one win from ten Premier League games this season – United’s worst start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago.

Carrick is taking training as usual this morning - with a cut-down group of players as a number of United's stars have departed on international duty.

Michael Carrick is pictured arriving at Manchester United's training ground at 7.15am

Mauricio Pochettino is the frontrunner to replace Carrick - leaving his role as US head coach

Join the discussion Who do you think is truly to blame for United¿s disastrous season - the manager or the club¿s leadership?

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a new frontrunner to replace Carrick. The Argentine is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.

In the three games since then, Carrick’s side lost at Chelsea, staged a remarkable comeback to beat Roma in the Champions League in midweek and then fought back again to draw with Villa.

Although it’s understood that no final decision has been reached over Carrick’s future and insiders say that speculation over his sacking is premature, the expectation within Old Trafford is that a new man will be in charge for the visit to Anfield a week on Sunday.

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

But this season has unravelled alarmingly for United with his only two wins in 15 games in all competitions coming at home to newly promoted Ipswich and Sabah of Azerbaijan.

Asked after Sunday’s chaotic draw with Villa if he would consider quitting, a defiant Carrick said: ‘That's not going to happen.

‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation and where we are. But we can do something about it. I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it's got to win games.’

Avram Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, co-owners, are pictured at Old Trafford in September

Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their eighth permanent manager or head coach since Ferguson retired 13-and-a-half years ago.

Pochettino was strongly linked with the job when Erik ten Hag was appointed in 2022 and again when the Dutchman was sacked two years later.

The 54-year-old has extensive Premier League experience at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton and was also in charge at Paris Saint-Germain.

Howe was previously seen as the favourite but it’s understood there has been no contact between United and the former Newcastle boss.

It would cost United around £3million in compensation to appoint the 48-year-old under the terms of his departure from St James’s Park in July.

Nagelsmann is available after leaving his role as head coach of the German national team in the summer when they were eliminated from the World Cup following a penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay in the round of 32.

Sports.title: Racing world mourns as promising young jockey dies after suffering horrific fall on her horse during race
Sports.content:
Apprentice jockey Izzy Neale has died in hospital days after she suffered a fall during a weekend race.

Neale, 22, was on board Marnoo when she and another rider fell 400m from the finish line during race six at Warren Racecourse, about 100km from Dubbo, on Sunday.

Racing NSW said she was knocked unconscious and airlifted to Dubbo Hospital, where her family rushed to her bedside.

The sporting authority shared a joint-statement on Tuesday with Ms Neale's family to confirm she had died.

'It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends,' the family said.

'Izzy rode horses before she could walk. Her love of horses was a lifelong passion that, more recently, had grown into a love of racing.

Apprentice jockey Izzy Neale (pictured) has sadly died after suffering a fall during a race

Izzy Neale won her first metropolitan race in July on It's A Tata (both pictured)

'Through organ donation, Izzy will give others the chance of life, bringing some comfort to our family amid this devastating loss.

'We are deeply grateful for the love, kindness and support shown to Izzy and our family by her friends, the racing community and everyone who has been by our side during this heartbreaking time.'

'We would like to thank Racing NSW and the NSW Jockeys Association for their care, compassion and support during this incredibly difficult time.

'We also extend our heartfelt thanks to the medical staff who cared for Izzy with such compassion.

'As we come to terms with our loss, we ask that our family's privacy be respected. Izzy was dearly loved and will forever be in our hearts.'

The Kieran Hazelton-trained Marnoo suffered a near foreleg injury and was later euthanised.

A race meet set to be held at Scone on Monday was postponed following consultation with jockeys and trainers.

Scone is Neale's home track in the NSW Hunter Valley, where she grew up.

The 22-year-old was a promising apprentice jockey having won 88 races

A day before the fall in central-west NSW, Neale was riding at Rosehill's Five Diamonds Day

'The thoughts and heartfelt support of Racing NSW and the entire community are with Izzy, her family, friends and colleagues during this extremely difficult time,' a previous Racing NSW statement read.

The other jockey involved, Diego Montes de Oca, was also taken to Dubbo Hospital with a suspected broken foot.

The incident has rocked the racing world.

'Tough day to be a jockey when things like this happen,' Melbourne Cup winner Robbie Dolan wrote after the accident.

Former jockey Melinda Turner added: 'Praying for a miracle. A terrible day for our industry.'

Just a day earlier, Neale was racing in Sydney at Rosehill's Five Diamonds Day, where she told Sky Racing that she was due to settle on the purchase of her first home this week.

She won 88 races from 699 starts.

Neale recorded her first metropolitan win in July on It's A Tata in the Highway Handicap at Rosehill.

Sports.title: Formula One WILL race in the Middle East as organisers stick with £120m Qatar and Abu Dhabi races despite threat of war
Sports.content:
Formula One WILL race in the Middle East as organisers stick with £120m Qatar and Abu Dhabi races despite threat of war

Formula One will stick to its intended programme that sees the season end in the Middle East, despite the conflict in the region.

The sport's bosses had weighed up whether to divert to Italy – to Imola – after the US and Israel opened attacks on Iran in February.

But F1 chief executive Stefano Domenicali and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem are confident security risks will not prevent them staging the closing races in Qatar on November 29 and the final round in Abu Dhabi on December 6.

Formula One said: 'Imola has been informed they will not be required as a back-up for the end of the season, and we have informed the teams.

'Imola was only an option in the event we didn't go to the Middle East.

'We could not have left Imola waiting indefinitely. Therefore, we have informed them today that we will not require them at the end of the season.'

Lewis Hamilton has been among the supporters of keeping F1's Middle East races on

While there was an attraction to seeing Italian Kimi Antonelli granted a 'lap of honour' in Imola, some 20 miles away from where he was born in Bologna, there is a lot of money tied up in holding races in the Gulf – perhaps £120million between Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

This scheme is yet subject to alteration if hostilities in the area escalate, though the sport's hierarchy is adamantly keen to see the planned races go ahead as scheduled.

Ben Sulayem, an Emirati, and a former champion rally driver, said: 'We are ready for Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

'We are fully prepared and committed to delivering two outstanding grands prix weekends and a spectacular conclusion to the Formula One world championship.

'We look forward to welcoming drivers, teams and fans to two iconic circuits for an unforgettable finish to the season. See you on the grid.'

The Bahrain Grand Prix, delayed from April, was relocated to Malaysia last month after Iranian attacks on the kingdom's US military bases.

Sports.title: Sir Jim Ratcliffe is the real problem at Man Utd - he's put clueless yes-men in charge
Sports.content:
Sir Jim Ratcliffe had all the answers when his investment in Manchester United was confirmed in February 2024. As befits someone from the billionaire class who believes money makes them experts in every industry, Ratcliffe knew why things had gone wrong and what it would take to fix them.

Just take the managers. At the time, Erik ten Hag was clinging on, although it felt inevitable he would be the next out the revolving door as United struggled to alight on the right man in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era.

But for Ratcliffe, this wasn't about the individuals. This was about the environment and the culture around the football club, and that's what needed to change. After making his fortune in petrochemicals, he was just the man to sort out one of the world's biggest sporting institutions as well, despite repeated failures at other football clubs and in cycling and sailing.

Speaking a day after his investment had been fully ratified, Ratcliffe said: "What I think is relevant to the question or the answer is if you look at the 11 years since David Gill and Sir Alex stepped down, there have been a whole series of coaches, some of whom were very good, and none of them have been successful or survived for very long.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"And you can't blame all the coaches. The only conclusion you can draw is the environment in which they were working in didn't work. And Erik has been in that environment. I'm talking about the organisation, the people in the structure, the atmosphere and all that sort of thing in the club, we have to do that bit.

"I'm not really focused on the coach, I'm focused on getting that bit right. It's not for me to judge that anyway. I'm not a football professional."

To put that into context, United had five permanent managers in the 11 years that Ratcliffe is talking about. This week, they will be looking for a fourth in less than three years since he took control of football operations at Old Trafford.

‌



What does that say about the environment at the club now? That Ratcliffe is making United worse, not better. Rather than the local lad riding to the rescue, he has become the problem. He doesn't have the faintest idea how to fix United but is too stubborn to admit it, and instead sees a new 100,000-seater stadium as his legacy.

View 3 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have made a serious of poor decisions (Image: PA)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Part of the issue is that Ratcliffe's desire to surround himself with "best in class" has never materialised. What he has actually done is create a football executive team of yes-men who will tell him what he wants to hear. There is no friction or disagreement here, the kind of dialogue that can drive a club forward.

‌



Dan Ashworth tried to provide that, but Ratcliffe didn't want to know. He was sacked four months after starting in the role of director of football. Ratcliffe called him "one of the top sporting directors in the world" in February 2024, then publicly sacked him straight after a game at Old Trafford in December 2024.

Ratcliffe has since admitted the appointment of Ashworth was an "error" and said the "chemistry" wasn't right. There was some disgruntlement as Ashworth's views when appointing Ruben Amorim as Ten Hag's successor and his approach at the time was seen as cautious, although it is arguable that he was proven right around Amorim.

View 3 Images Ruben Amorim was the last manager to be sacked (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

That is what disagreeing with Ratcliffe gets you, so why would Wilcox or Berrada take the risk? They are evidently part of the problem at United, but the man making the decisions likes them because they're easy to work with, so they're never going to rock the boat.

‌



Since Ratcliffe took over the running of this club, Ten Hag has lasted 31 games, Amorim survived 63 games, and now Michael Carrick looks set to leave after 32 games. That is a staggering failure of leadership and decision-making.

It also tells you everything you need to know about the environment. A succession of head coaches are being let down by those people above them. It should be the end for Wilcox and Berrada, but with Ratcliffe making the decisions, that feels pretty unlikely.

It turns out he doesn't have the answers after all.

Sports.title: Gerwyn Price slammed for sharing post saying there is 'zero evidence' against Russell Brand
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price slammed for sharing post saying there is 'zero evidence' against Russell Brand

Darts player Gerwyn Price has shared a post on his Facebook page which appears to question the prison sentence handed down to Russell Brand after he was convicted of rape and sexual assault

View 2 Images Gerwyn Price shared a controversial post about Russell Brand (Image: Getty Images)

Darts star Gerwyn Price has been criticised for sharing a post on social media which appeared to question the sentence given to rapist Russell Brand.

Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on Monday after being convicted of rape and sexual assault. The former comedian and actor was given nine years for rape, with an additional 18 months, nine months and eight months for three counts of sexual assault.

The 51-year-old was found guilty by a jury at Southwark Crown Court of the charges involving four women between 2004 and 2009. The rape took place this home in London, while the sexual assaults happened at a bar and in the workplace.

Price, the world No.3 darts player, shared a post to his 74,000 followers on Facebook which drew a comparison between Brand's sentence and that of Hamoud Al Soaimi, who was given a two-year suspended sentence for three counts of sexual assault and one assault by penetration of a 13-year-old in 2024.

Russell Brand joke axed from Gavin and Stacey as BBC makes urgent changes to iPlayer READ MORE :

Al Soaimi was 15 when he committed the offences between 2018 and 2019. Price shared the graphic without adding any comment.

After receiving a backlash, Price added in the comments section: "Not saying anyone is innocent just highlighting the two tier justice system we have to deal with".

It is not the first time that the former world champion has voiced his opinion on Brand, having posted about his case when allegations first arose in 2023. The Welshman posted a photo of his TV showing the Channel 4 Dispatches investigation, writing: "speaking up on certain topics, now this".

View 2 Images Russell Brand has been jailed for rape and sexual assault (Image: Shutterstock)

Before being sentenced, the court heard from Brand's victims who spoke of the impact his offending had on them. "Russell Brand has managed to move on," a woman who was sexually assaulted by Brand in 2005 said. "This has had a lasting impact on my life. I recognise this now.

"However, over the years, hearing his voice on television or seeing his image has made me jump. I had a strong adverse reaction hearing his voice." She added: "Russell Brand is a sexual predator who has no remorse... I just hope he is not allowed to hurt any more women."

Article continues below

A statement from the woman Brand was found to have raped was also shared in court. "I felt anxious, humiliated and overwhelmed," she said. "I struggled to sleep and eat, I struggled to cope with my emotions, I had to take time away from my work," she said.

She continued: "I had to live with my parents, I sought help and support... I am living with trauma, something I carry every day. My confidence and self esteem have been badly affected. I no longer trust my instincts."

Sports.title: Nine Man Utd players set to follow Michael Carrick out the door in mass exodus if boss is sacked
Sports.content:
Nine Man Utd players set to follow Michael Carrick out the door in mass exodus if boss is sacked

With Manchester United expected to part ways with Michael Carrick imminently, we're looking at the players who may follow him out the door

View 5 Images Michael Carrick is reportedly close to being sacked by Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Change appears to be afoot at Manchester United, with manager Michael Carrick reportedly on the verge of being sacked. Adjustments, however, may not be limited to the dugout, with several first team stars poised to follow Carrick out the door if and when the axe falls.

‌



‌



United have made a disastrous start to the season and head into the international break languishing 18th in the table after winning just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches. Defensive frailties have been a particular concern, with the Red Devils shipping 15 goals in their last five games in all competitions.

‌



Sunday's chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, despite a late fightback, looks to have been the final straw for Carrick, with the club now seemingly preparing for life without him. But while United begin drawing up a shortlist of potential managerial replacements, they may also need to consider which players might follow him out of the exit door.

‌



As many as nine senior squad members could find themselves either on the chopping block, or eyeing up a hasty getaway in the aftermath of Carrick's expected departure. Here, Mirror Football takes a closer look at all nine players.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Harry Maguire

Harry Maguire's rollercoaster Manchester United tenure appears to be reaching its natural conclusion as he enters the final few months of his contract. While the club hold the option to trigger a one-year extension, exercising it makes little footballing sense given that his form has been questionable for some time.

‌



The former club captain turns 34 in March and has been guilty of several costly lapses during United's latest defensive collapse. A fresh managerial appointment should signal the definitive end of an era, allowing both parties to part ways cleanly in the summer.

Lisandro Martinez

Once revered as United's defensive bedrock, Lisandro Martinez has endured an alarming fall from grace over the past 18 months. Persistent fitness struggles have severely hampered the Argentine's reliability, leaving United's backline constantly reshuffled and chronically exposed.

‌



Martinez is contracted until 2027, and though Old Trafford chiefs retain a one-year extension option, there is no pressing need to trigger it given the defensive cover already on the books. A new manager may well decide that the combative defender's physical peak has passed and look to rebuild the defence elsewhere.

View 5 Images Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire could leave Man Utd in 2027 (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



Mason Mount

Mason Mount's Manchester United move hasn't really worked. Plagued by persistent injury setbacks and underwhelming form, the former Chelsea midfielder now finds himself languishing down the pecking order behind Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo.

With his contract running until 2028, the two upcoming windows represent United's final realistic opportunity to recoup a respectable portion of their initial £55million investment. A clean break would suit all parties, handing Mount the fresh start he desperately needs to revive his stalling career.

‌



Bruno Fernandes

View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes has been linked with an Old Trafford exit for years (Image: Harry Cornish/PPAUK/Shutterstock)

Bruno Fernandes has long been linked with an Old Trafford exit and the club's current nosedive could finally push him toward the departure lounge. His public friction with Michael Carrick has noticeably strained relations with both the hierarchy and sections of the fanbase in recent weeks.

‌



While Carrick's sacking might seem to offer a reprieve, it could instead serve as the ideal cut-off point for a talisman whose on-pitch petulance can cause as many headaches as his goal contributions solve. Contracted until 2027 with a one-year option, United face a major decision over whether to prolong his stay or sanction a lucrative parting of ways.

Marcus Rashford

Marcus Rashford looked destined to leave Manchester during the summer, only remaining at the club after a prospective move to Barcelona collapsed. Bridges were effectively burned when he handed in a transfer request in December 2024 and his underwhelming displays since returning to United done nothing to repair that fractured bond.

‌



The forward's deal expires in 2028, making 2027 the critical juncture for United to command any meaningful transfer fee for their academy graduate. A separation now feels somewhat inevitable, offering Rashford the chance to rebuild his reputation - and his club career - away from the unrelenting Old Trafford spotlight.

View 5 Images Marcus Rashford's Man Utd return hasn't gone to plan (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Joshua Zirkzee

Brought in during the final months of Erik ten Hag's reign, Joshua Zirkzee has continually struggled to convince subsequent managers that he possesses the pedigree to lead United's frontline. The Dutch forward has spent the vast majority of his Old Trafford career confined to the bench, unable to make a lasting impression when handed rare opportunities, with Carrick even using the likes of Cunha and Mbeumo as makeshift No. 9s over Zirkzee.

The 25-year-old cannot afford another campaign playing second - or, in some cases, third - fiddle in a misfiring side when he should be commanding a starting berth. With United in dire need of a ruthless, reliable goalscorer, sanctioning a permanent move away would allow him to kickstart his career elsewhere.

‌



Kobbie Mainoo

Carrick's arrival earlier this year revitalised Kobbie Mainoo's Manchester United career after the young midfielder was frozen out under Ruben Amorim. However, any incoming manager could just as easily decide against building around the academy graduate, placing his rapid development in serious jeopardy once again.

Mainoo cannot risk another prolonged spell on the periphery, especially with several elite European clubs monitoring his situation closely. United chiefs showed an openness to entertaining offers for the England star last year, and they may be tempted to cash in if the next manager prefers a different midfield profile.

‌



View 5 Images Kobbie Mainoo may suffer if Michael Carrick is sacked (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Luke Shaw

Luke Shaw's 12-year stint at Old Trafford is drawing to a close as he approaches the final months of his current contract. Relentless injury setbacks have taken a heavy toll on the England international, leaving him a shadow of the dynamic left back who once dominated the flank.

‌



United desperately need energetic, durable full backs capable of withstanding the physical demands of modern top-flight football week in, week out. Allowing Shaw to leave on a free transfer next summer would clear substantial room on the wage bill and pave the way for a much-needed new addition, such as Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

Tom Heaton

Tom Heaton has been an exemplary squad player and dependable cover over the past six seasons, but his playing days are rapidly winding down. The veteran goalkeeper's contract expires at the end of the season, with no extension option in place to prolong his second stint at the club.

Article continues below

Having turned 40, the former England international is widely expected to call time on his playing career or transition into a full-time coaching capacity. A new managerial regime will inevitably look to modernise the goalkeeping department from top to bottom, making Heaton's exit a straightforward decision.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has let slip what his next job will be after Man Utd sack
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has let slip what his next job will be after Man Utd sack

Michael Carrick's next step after Manchester United has already been revealed

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is facing the sack at Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick could decide to re-enter the punditry world if he ends up getting sacked by Manchester United. The 45-year-old is expected to be dismissed at Old Trafford after overseeing United's worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years.

The Red Devils - who've won just one league game all season - sit 18th in the Premier League table and have failed to improve their results since Carrick received a stay of execution during the last international break.

A lack of progress has left the former England midfielder in a perilous situation, with the Guardian claiming United are 'moving towards' firing their head coach. Should Carrick depart United four months into the season, a swift return to management is not expected of the five-time league winner.

The i Paper reports that sources close to Carrick claim he's settled in the Manchester area and would not look to move in the possible event of his sacking. He spent 12 years of his playing career at United and his two children, daughter Louise and son Jacey, were born during his time at the club.

His inclination to stay is also impacted by Jacey currently starring for Manchester United's U18s. Carrick reportedly had a 'lack of interest' in returning to management after leaving Middlesbrough and some believe that heading into punditry instead of pursuing coaching could be his next job in football.

It wouldn't be an unfamiliar role for Carrick, having worked as a pundit for Prime Video last year following his departure from the Riverside Stadium. He was joined by his former Tottenham team-mate Dimitar Berbatov to provide expert analysis for Spurs' Champions League clash against Villarreal, which the English side won 1-0.

Carrick's exit would see United target their eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013. Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe is a frontrunner for the job and has yet to return to coaching since leaving the Magpies in July.

United States manager Mauricio Pochettino is said to be keen on the role and his contract with the national team includes a release clause should United desire to acquire his services. Ex-Germany and Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann and former Chelsea and Spurs manager Antonio Conte are also in contention for the job.
