Sports.title: F1 scraps back-up plan to race at Imola if Middle East GPs are cancelled – reports | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has committed to holding the final two rounds of the 2026 world championship in the Middle East or not at all.

The series had made contingency arrangements to relocate the final round it Imola in Italy if it decided the risks posed by the war in Iran meant it should not proceed with its races in the Middle East. Multiple reports now claim F1 has told Imola it will not be required to hold a race.

The world championship will resume at Las Vegas in the USA next week. Following that it is due to race at the Losail International Circuit in Qatar and Yas Marina in the United Arab Emirates on the following weekends.

The series cancelled its grands prix in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this year due to the war between Iran and the USA. It later held an event using the ‘Bahrain Grand Prix’ title at Malaysia’s Sepang International Circuit.

The political situation in the Middle East remains uncertain. US president Donald Trump this week suggested he would not escalate its military campaign in the region, but has made similar comments since beginning his war in February, only to subsequently launch further strikes. The US retains a significant military presences in the region and moved more troops there last month.

However Moto GP, which like F1 is owned by Liberty Media, raced in Losail on Sunday. It postponed its Qatar round in April due to the war.

Four bikes were missing from the field as Yamaha did not participate. Most of the series’ riders expressed concerns over visiting the country and asked the championship to provide extra guarantees for their security.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff defended Moto GP’s decision to race in Qatar. He criticised riders who expressed concerns about racing there, saying they “know nothing” about the situation.

Many television broadcasters also opted not to send their staff to the region.

The 2027 F1 season is due to begin in the Middle East with races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia next March. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali told investors last week “the disruption we experienced in the Middle East this year does not change our long-term regional strategy and ongoing partnership with our promoters.”

“This year, we currently remain scheduled to complete our calendar season and at this stage, continue to plan to finish the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi,” he added. “We will continue to monitor the situation. As always, the safety and security of everyone in the sport will remain our first and foremost priority.”

Many other series have cancelled events in the region due to the war in the Middle East. The World Endurance Championship called off its planned rounds in Qatar and Bahrain, replacing them with races in Italy and Spain. The 2027 Dakar Rally, previously held in Saudi Arabia, will take place in Africa. The 2026-27 Asian Le Mans series, which previously raced at Dubai Autodrome and Yas Marina, will take place in Europe under the name ‘Winter Le Mans Series’.

This article will be updated.

Sports.title: No F1 engine manufacturers to get extra upgrades after FIA’s third ADUO evaluation | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA will not to offer any engine manufacturers the chance to perform extra power unit upgrades following its latest Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) evaluation.

Under new rules introduced as part of Formula 1’s 2026 power unit regulations the sport’s governing body controls how often manufacturers can upgrade their internal combustion engines.

The evaluations take place periodically throughout the season. The FIA has completed its third such evaluation and, as was the case during the second, determined no further engine homologation opportunities should be offered.

The third evaluation period concluded after the United States Grand Prix last month. The second followed the Hungarian Grand Prix.

The first evaluation period, which ran from the start of the season to the Canadian Grand Prix, remains the only time any additional upgrade opportunities were awarded. On that occasion Red Bull-Ford were found to have the top-performing power unit.

Audi, Ferrari and Honda’s units were found to be more than 4% less powerful. They were permitted two extra homologation opportunities this year and two more next year. Mercedes were found to be within 2% and 4% of the leading power unit and therefore received one extra upgrade this year and next.

Separately, in May the FIA changed the ADUO rules to allow any manufacturer which was 10% off the leading design to spend more money. The revision was expected to assist Honda following their poor start to the season.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Some have likened F1’s ADUO to the World Endurance Championship’s heavily-criticised Balance of Performance regulations. The FIA’s single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis defended the regulations but indicated they may be revised in coming seasons.

“Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” he said.

“The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1. However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose.

“To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons.”

Sports.title: Russell explains pit exit spin: ‘I took too much risk because I saw a chance to win’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell says he spun in the pit lane exit during the Brazilian Grand Prix because he thought he had a race-winning opportunity.

The Mercedes driver was running third early in the race as the track was drying. He was within 10 seconds of race leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli when he came in to swap his intermediate tyres for slicks on lap 17.

However Russell spun when he reached the pit lane exit. The error cost him around 16 seconds and dropped him behind several of his rivals.

“Obviously it was a bit of an up and down race,” said Russell, who eventually finished fourth. “I’ve no idea what happened on that pit exit, I probably just took too much risk because I was seeing an opportunity to go for the win at that point, but it happened.”

Russell was one of few drivers who only made two pit stops during the race, keeping his set of slick tyres on until the rain returned in the closing stages.

“Ironically, because that happened, I then didn’t pit for another set of slick tyres and it kind of put me back in the same position as I was before the incident,” he acknowledged.

The Mercedes driver set the second-fastest time in qualifying, and believed he could have been quickest had he not aborted his final run under instruction from his race engineer. He said he was satisfied with his performance.

“I’m probably more happy coming away from the weekend because the performance was good,” said Russell, who started seventh following a penalty for replacing his engine. “At this stage I care more about the performance and I care about the result because that’s what’s been my weak point.

“The performance yesterday was great, the performance on the soft tyre was really great today but obviously I did make that mistake. But it probably would have been a different picture if we’d have started P2.”

Sports.title: Reynoso Lists Five Options for Canelo Alvarez in 2027
Sports.content:
Trainer Eddy Reynoso expects Canelo Alvarez to enter the ring two or three times in 2027, eyeing five distinct paths according to The Ring. The lineup features a super middleweight unification, a mandatory defense against Lester Martínez, a light heavyweight clash with Willy Hutchinson, and return bouts against Terence Crawford or Dmitry Bivol.

The Ring notes that no sequence is locked in. Four specific rivals are on the table, while the unification route hinges on which 168-pound titleholder agrees to terms. That gives Canelo two clear avenues for his WBC super middleweight belt: take on Martínez for the mandatory slot, or meet a rival champion to collect more gold.

That list of five narrows down fast once reality enters the room.

WBA champion Jaime Munguía makes zero promotional or competitive sense. Canelo already dropped and thoroughly handled him in 2024, and sharing gym space only solidifies that neither man is looking across the ring at the other. With Munguía struggling to look convincing against fringe opposition like Nikita Zon, nobody is opening their wallet to see that replay.

Osleys Iglesias, the IBF belt-holder at 168, is pure poison for an aging fighter. He is big, heavy-handed, fundamentally disciplined from the Cuban school, and operates out of a sharp southpaw stance. He gives away none of the physical advantages older counterpunchers rely on to slow down the pace. Putting Canelo in with a prime, hard-hitting super middleweight who can control range with a stiff southpaw stick is precisely the kind of voluntary hazard Reynoso routinely steers clear of.

WBC light heavyweight champion Willy Hutchinson represents another completely unnecessary headache up at 175. He brings awkward angles, relentless volume, legitimate reach, and the kind of high-octane engine that drains Canelo’s low-output, single-shot style. Canelo struggled with movement and pace at light heavyweight against Dmitry Bivol in the past, and Hutchinson has the motor to exploit those exact same stamina traps without offering the massive global brand name that justifies taking the beating.

Speaking of Bivol, that ship sailed the moment the cards were read in 2022. Canelo spent years tossing out casual remarks about rematches under impossible conditions, yet never actually pushed to get back in the ring with him. Bivol completely neutralized Canelo’s offense with a disciplined high guard, clean distance control, and piercing combinations. Revisiting that fight would simply be paying to re-watch a masterclass in how to dismantle Canelo’s flat-footed rhythm.

That leaves the two names that actually make sense for the business plan:

Crawford is the cash cow and the safest big-money avenue on the board. Even coming off a defeat, Canelo knows Crawford cannot hurt him with single-shot super middleweight power. Crawford will be 39, coming off a long, comfortable layoff on the heels of his biggest career win, and has shown zero appetite to sit in the pocket and trade heavy leather.

If Turki Alashikh puts up the bankroll, Canelo gets maximum financial reward with zero danger of taking a devastating beatdown. Turki is not blind to entertainment value. He wants explosive, fan-friendly wars. What Crawford and Canelo produced in September was essentially an expensive sparring session dressed up as history. Crawford boxed on his toes, kept his distance, tapped his way through exchanges, and collected the decision.

Even if Netflix reported huge raw viewer counts for the first encounter simply because subscribers could watch at no additional fee, streaming services track engagement drop-offs and social sentiment. Casual viewers complained about the lack of action, and nobody came away demanding a repeat. Shifting a second fight to standard pay-per-view could result in disastrous buy rates, while Netflix or any other platform would have a hard time justifying paying massive purses for another twelve rounds of cautious circling.

Lester Martínez is the exact type of mandatory Reynoso smiles at. He is straightforward, comes forward in predictable lines, lacks elite defensive nuance, and sits right in the pocket where Canelo can time his signature counter hooks without chasing anybody around the ring. It lets Canelo fulfill an obligation, keep a belt polished, and put on an explosive showcase for the cameras without taking real systemic punishment.

The five-man list is great for keeping headlines spinning, but Crawford for the check and Martínez for the routine defense are the only two realistic lanes on that drawing board.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis and Kelly Fight for Three Belts February 27
Sports.content:
Jaron Ennis and Josh Kelly meet for three junior middleweight belts on February 27 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, according to The Ring. The winner leaves the ring holding three world titles, but the route to an undisputed championship leads straight to Sebastian Fundora and Premier Boxing Champions. If Matchroom Boxing tries to lowball him, Fundora has no reason to budge from PBC, leaving the Atlanta winner stuck with three belts and no way to claim the fourth.

Eddie Hearn handled the simple part first. Because Matchroom promotes both Ennis and Kelly, unifying the WBA, WBO, and IBF titles did not require cutting deals with rival promoters or sorting out network broadcast rights. The real struggle starts with pricing the WBC belt away from Al Haymon.

Fundora handled his business in October by stopping Ermal Hadribeaj, dropping his mandatory obligations, and clearing his calendar. With no sanctioning bodies threatening to strip him, Fundora can demand his price on guarantees, pay-per-view percentages, and broadcast rights while risking nothing.

Matchroom keeps talking about a summer date for the undisputed clash, but that schedule is completely unrealistic. Fighting in June or July gives the Atlanta winner barely four months to recover and prepare. That leaves almost no margin to heal bad cuts, rest damaged hands, and jump right into another grueling training camp.

Kelly got sliced to ribbons against Caoimhin Agyarko, while Boots absorbs plenty of clean, heavy shots whenever he trades. If the victor limps out of Atlanta beat up, Fundora has no incentive to accommodate them. He can take a comfortable defense on PBC television, leaving Matchroom to sit on its hands until the end of the year.

The financial picture transforms entirely depending on whose hand gets raised in Atlanta. If Ennis wins, Eddie Hearn gets the all-American clash he covets, a natural pay-per-view headliner for Las Vegas or the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia. If Kelly pulls off the upset, those plans evaporate. Hearn would have to drag the entire event across the Atlantic. Staging an undisputed fight in Newcastle or London guarantees a packed stadium gate, but it creates a massive broadcast problem. It forces the bout into an afternoon slot in the United States, driving down what an American network or streaming platform will pay. Hearn has to build two completely separate business models.

Kelly is a live underdog who can cause real headaches inside the ring. He fights with his hands dangling near his hips, daring opponents to lunge in so he can nail them with lightning-quick counters.

If Boots gets reckless and stalks him in straight lines behind basic one-twos, Kelly has the reflexes to clip him coming in. Ennis needs to turn southpaw and negate that timing, targeting blind spots before the Brit can plant his boots and let his hands go.

Whoever survives Atlanta walks straight into a tactical trap with Fundora. Standard boxing wisdom says you crowd a 6-foot-6 skyscraper to smother his reach, but doing that means marching into a blender. Fundora prefers a dirty, phone-booth war. He digs vicious uppercuts right off his belt line, ripping straight through a tight guard before opponents can spot them coming. Hadribeaj managed to push inside and land heavy left hands, but Fundora just leaned into the fire, tore him apart at close range, and closed the show with a single second left on the clock.

Atlanta crowns a three-belt champion for Eddie Hearn, but Sebastian Fundora controls the real prize. The WBC champion can put his feet up, check out what shape the winner leaves the arena in, and demand a small fortune before he ever considers risking his title.

Sports.title: Conor Benn’s 40 Million Problem: Zuffa’s Make-Or-Break Crossroad
Sports.content:
Chris Mannix estimates Conor Benn will clear upward of $40 million across the Regis Prograis win, his knockout loss to Ryan Garcia, and a third bout. If that figure holds, Zuffa’s next move is simple: decide whether Benn is a long-term commercial asset worth rebuilding, or a depreciating commodity to cash out before the floor gives way.

Cheap preliminary bouts can shave operational overhead, but cost-cutting does not rescue a main event that draws too few buyers to carry elite purses. Denzel Bentley is a clean, in-house booking on paper, yet he brings virtually no promotional leverage outside hardcore circles. If Benn stumbles against a rugged domestic contender, his headliner status evaporates on a Tuesday-level attraction.

“Conor Benn in the last three fights, I would estimate he has made. Well, the last two and then there’s one coming up. He’s going to make north of $40 million. Very few fighters make that in their career,” said Mannix.

A third meeting with Chris Eubank Jr. remains a dependable box-office draw across the UK, but it offers zero forward momentum. Without a world title or fresh bad blood, a trilogy simply taxes the same domestic consumer base a third time. It functions as a lucrative exit strategy rather than a platform to expand Benn’s brand.

Shakur Stevenson provides stateside name recognition, yet the financial and stylistic variables work against Zuffa. Stevenson is a naturally smaller fighter moving up in weight. A Benn win does little to erase the Garcia beatdown, while a calculated twelve-round schooling by Stevenson leaves Zuffa covering two astronomical purses for a clinic that actively turns off casual ticket buyers. That dilemma also complicates distribution, as an American-led Stevenson bout targets a prime U.S. broadcast window, whereas an Eubank card requires a UK primetime slot to secure the gate.

If Zuffa intends to actually rehabilitate Benn, it needs a recognizable, established welterweight willing to stand in the pocket. The play is an opponent who commands respect on the marquee, yet offers the stylistic openings Benn requires to deliver a highlight-reel finish that makes his next event an easy sell.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Gives PBC a Condition for Staying
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is prepared to re-sign with Premier Boxing Champions following his December 5 bout against Michal Cieslak, provided his contract permits regular cross-platform appearances.

In an interview with Chris Mannix, Benavidez revealed he launched his own promotional banner, outlining an aggressive roadmap targeting Jai Opetaia in May followed by Oleksandr Usyk in September. The true worth of any future contractual commitment rests entirely on delivering those marquee bouts without bureaucratic delay.

“As long as we’re able to move freely and fight whoever, whatever network we want to do, then we can stay here,” Benavidez stated. “I want these fights to happen immediately.”

Benavidez gives PBC credit for letting him shop around on other networks. He needs that kind of leeway if he wants major unifications, simply because the money has to come from rival platforms or deep-pocketed outside backers.

Starting his own promotional company lets him push for co-promotional billing, a say on fight dates, and a piece of the TV rights. Still, none of that matters unless the opposing camps and money men sign off. Making a fight with Opetaia is one thing; putting together the numbers for a monster event with Usyk is a totally different ballgame.

Despite turning 29, Benavidez carries the mileage of a thirteen-year professional tenure. Eliminating the harsh cut to 175 pounds undoubtedly preserves his conditioning. Yet his relentless, close-range combinations naturally expose him to heavy return fire from full-sized cruiserweights. A punishing clash with Opetaia in May could result in facial cuts, orthopedic damage, or an abbreviated summer training camp ahead of a proposed September date with Usyk.

With Benavidez, the facial wear is catching up to the odometer. He turned pro at sixteen, but the real mileage is the gym work. His whole identity in camp has always been grueling, high-volume sparring where he plays the hammer, walking guys down and eating clean shots just to deliver five of his own. You can get away with that in your early twenties when the recovery is instant, but that kind of daily collision accumulates on a guy’s face and joints.

The weight shifts do not help either. Spending a decade draining a massive frame down to 168 pounds, ballooning between camps, then cutting to 175, and now suddenly filling out toward 200 changes facial structure dramatically. Once a fighter stops that severe water depletion cycle and carries heavier, solid mass into his late twenties, the baby fat is completely gone, and the facial tissue hardens up fast.

The real giveaway will be the first time he faces genuine adversity at cruiserweight. When guys age overnight on the outside, you watch the legs and the punch reaction. If the feet look heavy early or the reflexes to slip counters are a fraction of a second slower against a puncher like Cieslak or Opetaia, that weathered look in camp ceases to be cosmetic and becomes a fighting reality.

Sports.title: Gene Tunney’s Only Loss Explains His Greatness
Sports.content:
Gene Tunney’s best case for greatness is what he did after Harry Greb handed him his only professional defeat. Greb took Tunney’s American light heavyweight title in 1922 by setting a pace Tunney could barely withstand. Three years and four rematches later, Tunney was landing body shots that forced Greb to hold.

The first fight at Madison Square Garden showed how far Tunney had to go. Greb threw from awkward angles and took control in the late rounds as Tunney tired. Bloodied and exhausted, Tunney stayed upright through the 15th. Two days later, he went to the athletic commission’s office to seek a rematch.

Tunney regained the title by decision in February 1923, though many ringside reporters thought Greb had done enough to win. Tunney won their third meeting that December. Their fourth fight, in September 1924, ended without an official decision. The Cleveland Plain Dealer favored Greb, while The New York Times reported that most ringside writers saw an even fight. More than two years after the first bout, Greb was still giving Tunney trouble.

By their fifth meeting in March 1925, Tunney weighed 181 pounds to Greb’s 168. He used those extra pounds to do damage at close range. The Associated Press reported that Tunney concentrated his attack on the body and cut short Greb’s attempts to rally. Greb, who had poured on punches late in the first fight, spent much of the fifth holding. The weight advantage belongs in the story because Tunney had found a way to make Greb feel it where he had once been most dangerous.

Tunney stopped Tommy Gibbons later that year and took the world heavyweight title from Jack Dempsey by decision in September 1926. Dempsey dropped him in the seventh round of their rematch a year later, then delayed the referee’s count by failing to go promptly to a neutral corner. Tunney rose and made it through the round. In the eighth, he dropped Dempsey on his way to another decision. Tunney stopped Tom Heeney in July 1928 and retired as champion.

The Long Count still invites people to imagine what Dempsey might have done with those extra seconds. The Greb series shows what Tunney did with four more chances against a man who had already beaten him. The first rematch gave him his title back, but the disputed decision left plenty to argue about. By the fifth fight, the clearest evidence was in the way Greb fought. The man who had set the pace over 15 rounds in 1922 was holding to buy himself a few seconds at a time.

Sports.title: Willy Hutchinson Has the Belt and the Style Canelo Hates
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson offers Canelo Alvarez an intriguing path toward an undisputed crown at light heavyweight, along with the precise movement that historically gives Canelo fits. After Hutchinson claimed the vacant WBC belt against Joshua Buatsi, Chris Mannix proposed the pairing, prompting Sergio Mora to wonder about the logic behind it.

Mora highlighted Hutchinson’s slick jab, deceptive rhythm, and southpaw looks, arguing that if Canelo wants to spend twelve rounds chasing an elusive stylist, he might as well target Dmitry Bivol directly.

“It’s the movers, the guys that don’t engage, the tricky guys,” said Mora on Mannix’s YouTube channel, who pointed to Hutchinson’s jab, timing and habit of switching southpaw. If Canelo is prepared to deal with that style, Mora would rather see him fight Dmitry Bivol again.

Mannix’s pitch carries clear tactical purpose. Should Canelo defeat Hutchinson while Bivol retains the remaining straps, their second meeting would crown an undisputed champion. Capturing the WBC strap gives Canelo fresh leverage after dropped rounds in their initial encounter. The cost, however, involves chasing a rangier opponent who rarely plants his feet long enough for return fire.

Against Buatsi, Hutchinson demonstrated his ability to reset aggressive opponents. He scored with his lead hand from distance, slipped away before Buatsi set his base, and tied up on the inside. While Christian Mbilli offered Canelo a stationary target, Hutchinson could force him to spend full minutes fighting into close quarters, only to wrap him up before the Mexican star digs into the ribs.

Stylistically, Hutchinson brings every single attribute that gives Canelo severe problems. Canelo has always struggled against slick, disciplined movers with active lead hands and sharp ring generalship. Floyd Mayweather wrote the blueprint, Dmitry Bivol executed it with physical authority, and Terence Crawford exploited those exact gaps in mobility and lateral footwork.

Hutchinson takes that exact stylistic formula and backs it with genuine light heavyweight size. At 6-foot-1 with a 73-inch reach, he is not an undersized fighter moving up; he is a natural 175-pounder in his physical prime. As he proved against Joshua Buatsi, he can switch stances seamlessly, snap a long jab, control distance, and disengage before an opponent can set their base to load up power shots.

For an aging Canelo whose foot speed has noticeably slowed and who relies heavily on opponents standing in the pocket to trade, chasing Hutchinson around the ring for 12 rounds would be an absolute nightmare. From a risk-versus-reward perspective, it is even worse for Canelo.

Hutchinson possesses world-class talent and now holds a major belt, but he does not carry the mainstream American pay-per-view profile to deliver a massive blockbuster gate. If Canelo wins, critics immediately dismiss it by claiming he merely defeated an opponent without marquee status. If Canelo loses or gets thoroughly outboxed, his aura and marketability take another massive hit against a fighter most casual fans are just learning about.

If Turki Alalshikh put an obscene sum on the table for Willy Hutchinson, Canelo and Eddy Reynoso would probably have a private conversation behind closed doors that sounds very different from what they would say into a microphone.

Their internal calculation would break down into two stages. For starters, Reynoso would likely watch the tape and spot every red flag imaginable. Reynoso is a meticulous matchmaker who protects the Canelo brand with extreme precision. He knows Canelo’s legs are not what they were five years ago, and he knows how much trouble tall, athletic switch-hitters who move laterally cause his fighter. Reynoso’s immediate coaching instinct would be to steer Canelo away from a nightmare style that yields minimal glory.

From there, Canelo’s response would depend entirely on what that number looked like. Canelo has reached the point in his career where he views himself as an enterprise. If the money was merely “great” ($40 million to $50 million), Canelo would casually brush it off. He would tell Turki that Hutchinson brings nothing to the gate, has no real profile in North America, and does not deserve to share the ring with him. He would counter by asking for that same bag to fight someone like Chris Eubank Jr. or another name who actually comes forward to trade.

If Turki offered an absurd, once-in-a-lifetime figure, say, $100 million or more with full guarantees, Reynoso and Canelo would pause. But even then, they would attempt to alter the playing field before signing anything. They would push for a catchweight, demand strict rehydration stipulations, or try to impose terms designed to drain Hutchinson’s mobility and take the spring out of his legs.

If Turki insisted on a straight 175-pound fight with zero compromises, Canelo would almost certainly pass. At this stage of his career, with his financial empire secure, taking a guaranteed boxing lesson against a young, 6-foot-1 mover for any amount of money is not worth watching his aura evaporate in front of the world. Canelo would smile, thank His Excellency, and ask to fight a brawler instead.

Sports.title: Canelo Plans to Renew Turki Deal After March Fight
Sports.content:
Canelo Álvarez plans to renew his deal with Turki Alalshikh after his March fight, trainer Eddy Reynoso says. His decision win over Christian Mbilli may have strengthened the case for another deal, which would keep Saudi backing in play for a Terence Crawford rematch.

“It’s the last one [the fight in March], but we’re going to renew. There are very good plans for Saúl. He already spoke with Turki, and there are good plans to continue his career,” said Reynoso, in comments to La Afición translated and shared by EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai.

What Turki Could Get From Another Deal

Some fans saw the Mbilli win as Canelo’s best performance since he stopped Caleb Plant in 2021. Canelo still fought in bursts, but he had to keep finding clean shots against an unbeaten contender who pressed him for 12 rounds. That gave Alalshikh a fresh performance to judge alongside Canelo’s name and drawing power. Reynoso gave no indication of how much the win figured in their talks.

Crawford offers the biggest commercial reason to renew. The first fight gives the promotion an obvious question to sell. Can Canelo reverse the result? Saudi backing helped make the first fight happen, and a renewed deal would give Canelo a direct route back to the same financier. The boxing problem remains. Crawford could still use his jab and reach to score from outside and make Canelo follow him. Beating Mbilli, who came forward, tells us little about how Canelo would close distance on Crawford.

Hamzah Sheeraz offers a different kind of event at 168 pounds. His British following gives the promotion a second market, and his height and reach give it something to sell beyond Canelo’s name. Sheeraz has less experience at that level, though. Compare that with IBF champion Osleys Iglesias, a dangerous southpaw whose belt gives Canelo a sporting reason to fight him. Sheeraz gives Alalshikh an easier fight to market, especially if the aim is to put on an event that can draw in Britain as well as with Canelo’s audience.

A return to 175 pounds would open up two more fights. Dmitry Bivol already beat Canelo, so a rematch comes with a result to avenge and a clear question about whether Canelo can get past Bivol’s jab and footwork. Artur Beterbiev would be a first-time opponent. The sell there is whether Canelo can hold his ground against a naturally bigger puncher who can force him to work at a pace he would rather set himself. Both fights depend on Canelo being willing to go back up to light heavyweight.

Reynoso named no opponents for an extension and gave no terms. If the deal goes through, Crawford would offer the biggest event, while Sheeraz would give Alalshikh a way to build one around Canelo at 168. Bivol and Beterbiev only enter the picture if Canelo wants another fight at 175.

For Canelo’s camp, Crawford, 39, is the ideal financial play with almost zero physical danger. He is a smaller guy who relied on running, movement, and potshots to nick rounds. He was never going to walk Canelo down or smash him up. There is zero wear and tear on Canelo’s body in that matchup compared to getting in the trenches with a relentless slugger or moving back up to 175.

If Crawford came out on the back foot the first time, a full year sitting on the couch is not going to turn him into a pressure fighter. Ring rust makes guys even more defensive. If he gets pried out of retirement by a massive Saudi check, he will likely double down on the track shoes, look to survive on points from the outside, and avoid any inside trade.

For Reynoso and Canelo, it represents a massive payday without the physical toll. The only hurdle is whether Turki actually wants to cough up another nine-figure purse to finance a fight that already lacked real fireworks.

Sports.title: Alycia Baumgardner Outclasses Turhan, Then Gets Called Out By Caroline Dubois
Sports.content:
On Sunday night, November 8th, at MVPW07, in her lightweight debut, Alycia “The Bomb” Baumgardner put her boxing skills on display as she outclassed Elif Turhan (14-1, 8 KOs) and won the IBF world title.

Baumgardner was elusive; she touched the body, and her power shots were sharp and accurate. Turhan couldn’t find the range to land her right hand, and she failed to make any in-ring adjustments.

In the opening round, Baumgardner set the tone as she fired the jab and followed it up with a three-punch combination. Round two featured back-and-forth action as Baumgardner’s shots were landing and Turhan was missing wildly.

At the 1:05 mark of the third round, Baumgardner landed a big right hand that knocked Turhan off-balance. As the third round was coming to a close, Baumgardner hurt Turhan, but the referee prematurely stepped in to stop the action.

The referee made a significant error when she stopped the action because she thought the ten-second bell was the final bell, which is the one that officially ends the round.

During the first four rounds of the fight, the hard-hitting Turhan was routinely off the mark when she threw her power shots. In the 5th round, Turhan finally experienced success when she was able to land the uppercut.

The second half of the fight featured Baumgardner working off the jab and landing a variety of punches. Baumgardner exposed Turhan as she made it apparent that we were viewing a matchup between a highly skilled boxer and a one-dimensional fighter.

At the conclusion of the 10-round contest, the scorecards reflected the dominance that took place inside of the ring. All three judges scored the bout (100-90) in favor of Baumgardner.

With the victory, Alycia Baumgardner (19-1, 7 KOs) won the IBF title and became a two-division world champion. Following the impressive victory, Baumgardner was confronted by WBC/WBO lightweight champion Caroline Dubois.

After Baumgardner conducted her post-fight interview, Dubois left her ringside seat, grabbed a mic, and addressed Baumgardner. While standing by the ring, Dubois issued a challenge to the new IBF lightweight champion.

“I handle my business; you handled yours. Are we fighting?” Dubois asked. “Are we fighting champ? Are we fighting champ? Are we fighting champ? That’s all you got to say. That’s all you got to say. Why you’re not looking at me champ? Why you’re not looking at me champ? Let’s go. Undisputed.”

Caroline Dubois pulled a bold move based on the fact that she was scheduling a fight for undisputed status while her February 2027 opponent, the WBA lightweight champion Stephanie Han, was sitting one seat away from Dubois at ringside.

During the verbal exchange, Alycia Baumgardner was advising Dubois to focus on her next opponent as opposed to looking ahead to a fight for undisputed. However, if Dubois is successful on February 20th, a Baumgardner vs. Dubois bout would be the 2027 fight of the year for women’s boxing.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse probe 85% complete; evidence points to prosecution – Education Minister
Ghana News.content:
The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, says investigations into the sexual abuse allegations involving female students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) are 85 per cent complete, with evidence gathered so far pointing to a prima facie case for prosecution.

He said the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service was handling the criminal aspects of the case, while a committee established by the government on October 14 was nearing the completion of its investigations.

Mr Iddrisu disclosed this when he addressed Parliament on Tuesday, November 10, after appearing before the joint parliamentary committees on Human Rights, Gender and Education to brief them on developments in the case.

“Mr. Speaker, I'm happy to note and report that the Criminal Investigation Department of the Police Service is dealing with the criminal aspects of it, which has to do with sexual assault against some students at Obuasi Technical,” he told the House.

He added that the committee established on October 14 had made significant progress and that the evidence gathered could support prosecution.

“Mr Speaker, I'm happy to know that a committee we put together on the 14th of October is 85% complete with its investigation, and the weight of evidence suggests that a court would have considered the matter that a prima facie case is established against for purposes of prosecution that we expect to start shortly,” he said.

The Minister's update comes amid growing public concern over allegations of sexual abuse involving the school's headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, and female students.

The allegations gained national attention following a JoyNews investigation by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, titled Inside the Dreaded Headmaster's Bungalow, which detailed claims of sexual harassment, assault and rape involving students.

The investigation reported that complaints had been made to school management and education officials months before the headmaster was interdicted. '

It also cited accounts from students, parents and teachers who said concerns about the alleged abuse had not received adequate attention.

The Ghana Education Service (GES) subsequently interdicted Mr Abdulai on October 14 to facilitate investigations, while the Education Minister referred the criminal aspects of the allegations to the police.

The case has also attracted scrutiny over the handling of earlier complaints. A committee that investigated disturbances at the school in August 2026 reported that the sexual harassment allegations presented to it were not substantiated by the evidence available at the time.

However, that inquiry was separate from the fresh investigations initiated after the JoyNews exposé.

The police have also investigated a rape complaint filed by a student on August 4, 2026, and forwarded the case docket to the Attorney-General for study and advice.

Police clarified that the docket concerned that particular complaint, while other allegations would require separate investigations.

Ghana News.title: Ablakwa expresses Ghana’s interest in nuclear energy cooperation with US
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, has expressed Ghana's interest in exploring opportunities for cooperation with the United States in nuclear energy as the two countries seek to strengthen their bilateral relations.

He made the remarks when the outgoing United States Chargé d’Affaires ad interim to Ghana, Rolf Olson, paid a farewell call on him at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra on Monday, November 9, 2026, at the end of his tour of duty in the country.

Mr Ablakwa acknowledged Mr Olson's contribution to strengthening relations between Ghana and the United States, particularly in the areas of education and security.

He also expressed appreciation to the US government for its support in airlifting Ghanaian Armed Forces personnel and equipment to Jamaica to assist with humanitarian and reconstruction efforts following the devastation caused by Hurricane Melissa.

The Minister reiterated Ghana's commitment to maintaining cordial relations with the United States and deepening cooperation at both bilateral and multilateral levels.

He further assured that the incoming US Consul would receive the same level of support and cooperation extended to Mr Olson during his tenure.

For his part, Mr Olson thanked the Minister, the Ghanaian government and the people of Ghana for the cooperation and hospitality he received throughout his stay.

He reaffirmed the importance of the longstanding partnership between the two countries and expressed confidence in the continued strengthening of their relations.

Ghana News.title: A policy born out of sight, not sympathy: Ghana’s new dawn for persons with disabilities
Ghana News.content:
The launch of the Free Tertiary Education for Persons with Disabilities Initiative by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama has ignited renewed hope and pride among Ghana’s disability community. Beyond promises, this policy marks a visionary step; one that recognizes ability over disability and sets Ghana on course to become a continental model of inclusive development.

A POLICY OF SIGHT: SEEING ABILITY OVER DISABILITY

For many years, the refrain among persons with disabilities in Ghana has been one of hope mixed with uncertainty, hope for recognition, inclusion and empowerment, as well as uncertainty about when that hope would materialize into real systemic change. Today, that narrative is being rewritten.

The announcement by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, during the launch of the Free Tertiary Education for Persons with Disabilities Initiative, at the Accra College of Education on Friday, 24th October, 2025 has rekindled an unprecedented sense of optimism, dignity, and a sense of belonging among the disability community. This bold vision marks a memorable turning point in our nation’s moral and social consciousness; one that views disability not through the lens of sympathy, but through the lens of sight, fairness, and capability.

A VISION ROOTED IN EMPOWERMENT AND EQUITY

What makes this initiative exceptional is not merely its content, but its philosophy. For the first time in Ghana’s policy history, disability inclusion is being pursued not as an act of charity, but as a strategic national development goal.

The initiative recognizes that disability should not prevent a qualified Ghanaian from pursuing a university degree, Higher National Diploma (HND) or diploma. It seeks to make tertiary education more accessible to persons with disabilities who are most often excluded as a result of financial circumstances.

The policy provides for the payment of eligible beneficiary’s academic and residential fees in all public tertiary institutions as part of the support package. From the passage of the Persons with Disabilities Act 2006, Act 715, to the allocation of portions of the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF) to persons living with disabilities, and to the creation of Disability Health and Resource Centres across second-cycle and public tertiary inclusive institutions in Ghana, this is a comprehensive national vision grounded in equity, empowerment, and opportunity.

The President’s directives have sent a clear message: Persons with disabilities are not liabilities to be pitied, but assets to be developed and celebrated. His emphasis on transforming our national mindset “from commiseration to partnership, from exclusion to empowerment, and from antagonism to solidarity” has resonated deeply within the hearts and minds of all Ghanaians who believe in justice and inclusion.

COMPLETING THE CIRCLE OF INCLUSIVITY

In the spirit of compassion, fairness, and nation-building, it is timely to make one heartfelt appeal; to extend the “Free Tertiary Education for PWDs Policy” to graduate persons with disabilities. The pursuit of higher education beyond the undergraduate level is a critical step for persons with disabilities to be fully equipped to contribute at the highest levels of governance, leadership, and national development.

While free tertiary education will open doors to countless young persons with disabilities, many graduates continue to face financial and structural barriers as they pursue postgraduate degrees or professional certifications. By expanding this special intervention to cover graduate-level studies, persons with disabilities will not be left behind in policy, administration, and leadership roles where graduate qualifications are most often a requirement. Furthermore, Ghana will complete the circle of inclusivity His Excellency has so admirably begun.

A further and compelling justification for extending this special initiative to postgraduate education is the employment reality confronting many persons with disabilities after graduation. Currently, too many PWDs who successfully complete tertiary education still struggle to secure employment in spite of their qualifications and capabilities. For some, an undergraduate degree does not provide a sufficient competitive advantage in an increasingly demanding labour market, where advanced qualifications, specialist knowledge, and professional credentials can influence access to meaningful employment and leadership opportunities. Without targeted support to pursue further studies, many capable graduates with disabilities risk remaining unemployed or being excluded from positions for which they could otherwise be well qualified. Extending the policy to cover postgraduate and other relevant graduate-level programmes would therefore help remove a major financial barrier and enable eligible PWDs strengthen their expertise, broaden their career prospects, and compete more effectively for employment. In the long term, this investment could also help position more persons with disabilities to contribute meaningfully to policy formulation, implementation, and evaluation, as well as to public administration, institutional leadership, research, and national development. The policy should not merely help PWDs enter tertiary institutions; it should also help create pathways for them to progress, lead, and participate in shaping the decisions that directly affect their lives and the future of Ghana.

Such a move would not only enhance access but would also position Ghana as a continental leader; a nation where education becomes the ultimate tool of liberation for all citizens, regardless of physical condition. It would demonstrate that our compassion is matched by courage, and our vision by conviction.

A CALL TO COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY

The President has rightfully called upon the private sector, civil society, universities, and the media to join in this noble vision. Disability inclusion cannot be the work of government alone; it must be a shared national mission.

Let us, therefore, as a people, take the bull by the horn and ensure that this transformative policy becomes a living and breathing testament of Ghana’s moral strength and developmental maturity.

In conclusion, this new chapter in Ghana’s disability rights movement reminds us that true progress is not measured by sympathy, but by systems; not by handouts, but by opportunities; and not by rhetoric, but by results.

Indeed, we are witnessing a policy born of sight, not sympathy. A sight that sees beyond physical limitations to the vast potential that lies within every Ghanaian.

And as we move forward together as persons with, and those without disabilities, we reaffirm a shared truth: when inclusion becomes the norm, development becomes unstoppable.

Author Bio

Isaac Ansah is the Ghana Gas Disability Liaison Officer, as well as the Senior Community Relations and CSR Officer for the Community Relations Division of Ghana National Gas Ltd Company, where he advocates for inclusive development and disability empowerment. His work focuses on corporate social responsibility, inclusive education, and livelihood empowerment programmes for persons with disabilities.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t reaffirms commitment to women’s economic empowerment
Ghana News.content:
The government has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening women's economic empowerment through improved access to affordable financing, business development support, export training and expanded market opportunities.

Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang highlighted the establishment of the Women's Development Bank as a major intervention to address the financing challenges confronting women entrepreneurs.

She was speaking at the 5th Ghana Women Entrepreneurship Summit in Accra on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, where she also called for stronger linkages between agriculture and industry to increase women's participation in Ghana's economic transformation.

The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, also outlined government interventions aimed at strengthening women-owned businesses.

In her keynote address, she said more than 1,300 entrepreneurs had benefited from export training and promotional support provided by the Ministry in partnership with TradeMark Africa and other development partners.

She further highlighted efforts to improve access to finance, facilitate product certification, promote value addition and expand market opportunities for Ghanaian businesses under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

The summit also provided a platform for the launch of the Youth Enterprise Launchpad.

Ghana News.title: Hassan Ayariga acknowledges government’s economic gains but questions impact on living standards
Ghana News.content:
Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Dr Hassan Ayariga, has acknowledged improvements in Ghana’s macroeconomic performance under the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government in 2026 but says the gains must translate into better living conditions for ordinary Ghanaians.

In an assessment of the government’s performance ahead of the 2027 Budget presentation, Dr Ayariga cited progress in fiscal consolidation, inflation reduction and revenue mobilisation.

He noted that the Bank of Ghana had reported a decline in the fiscal deficit for the first half of 2026 compared with the corresponding period in 2025, alongside a primary fiscal surplus.

He also acknowledged that inflation had fallen substantially from the high levels recorded in previous years.

However, he cautioned that lower inflation does not necessarily mean prices have fallen or household incomes have improved.

He said the government must demonstrate how economic stabilisation is translating into stronger purchasing power, better wages, employment and business opportunities.

Dr Ayariga also raised concerns about government expenditure, citing Bank of Ghana reporting that total expenditure in the first half of 2026 was approximately 24.9 per cent below its programmed target.

Capital expenditure was also below the programmed level, raising questions about the timely release of funds to ministries, departments and agencies.

He said the shortfall could affect the implementation of programmes in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, agriculture, road construction and water infrastructure.

While cautioning that the expenditure gap does not automatically establish that the Finance Minister personally refused to release funds, he called on the Ministry of Finance to publish a comprehensive report detailing the amounts allocated, released and spent by each ministry during the year.

Dr Ayariga said the 2027 Budget must provide clear answers on funding shortfalls and how the government intends to improve implementation of approved programmes.

He further urged the government to prioritise productive employment, Ghanaian enterprise development, infrastructure, agricultural productivity and public financial accountability.

The APC leader said the success of government should ultimately be measured by improvements in the welfare of citizens, rather than budget announcements and macroeconomic indicators alone.

His assessment, dated November 10, 2026, comes ahead of the government's presentation of the 2027 National Budget to Parliament on Thursday, November 12.

Ghana News.title: Minerals Commission CEO calls for prosecution of Chinese nationals involved in illegal mining
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Isaac Andrews Tandoh, has called for the strict enforcement of Ghana’s mining laws against Chinese nationals and companies involved in illegal mining, saying foreign investors must be held accountable regardless of their nationality.

Speaking at the China-Ghana Mining Cooperation Conference 2026, Mr Tandoh said Ghana’s mining regulations applied equally to all operators and that no foreign national or investor should be shielded from sanctions for breaking the law.

He said a proposed framework agreement between Ghana and China was expected to strengthen cooperation in enforcing mining regulations and prosecuting Chinese nationals found engaging in illegal activities.

“Under the new framework agreement we are doing with the Chinese government, they are supporting us to go ahead and prosecute Chinese who find themselves on the wrong side of the law. They will go through the sanctions, and when they go back, Chinese law will also take care of them,” he said.

The conference brought together stakeholders in Ghana’s mining industry, including the President of the Ghana Chamber of Mines, Ing. Frederick Attakumah, and China’s Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Cong Song.

Mr Tandoh said Ghana remained open to foreign investment in its mineral resources but insisted that all investors must operate within the country’s legal and regulatory framework.

His comments come amid continuing concerns about illegal small-scale mining, popularly known as galamsey, which has contributed to the degradation of water bodies, farmlands and other natural resources.

China’s Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Cong Song, called for a balanced approach to mining cooperation, cautioning against using Africa’s natural resources as instruments of geopolitical rivalry.

He said the continent’s mineral wealth should instead support economic transformation, sustainable development and mutually beneficial international partnerships.

“Africa’s resources should not be used for political rivalry,” he said.

Mr Cong also emphasised the need for mutual respect and cooperation, as well as recognition of African countries’ development priorities in decisions concerning the management and use of their natural resources.

A major highlight of the conference was the unveiling of the China-Ghana Mining Talent Development Centre (CMTDC), an initiative aimed at strengthening technical skills, knowledge exchange and technology transfer in Ghana’s mining industry.

The centre is expected to serve as a training and capacity-building hub for Ghanaian workers and mining professionals, offering opportunities to acquire specialised technical expertise and industry-related skills.

Its proposed programmes are also expected to support the development of local capabilities and contribute to the modernisation of the mining sector.

The initiative forms part of broader efforts to deepen Ghana-China mining cooperation while increasing Ghanaian participation across the mining value chain.

The partnership’s impact, however, will depend on its ability to deliver tangible benefits in areas such as responsible mining, environmental protection, technology transfer and skills development.

Ghana News.title: Patoranking reunites with Olamide for new Lagos-inspired single, ‘Welcome to Lagos’
Ghana News.content:
Nigerian reggae and dancehall star Patoranking has teamed up with rapper Olamide on a new single titled ‘Welcome To Lagos’, celebrating the energy, ambition and cultural influence of Nigeria's commercial capital.

Released on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, through Amari Musiq, the collaboration brings together two prominent Nigerian music acts on a record inspired by the city's vibrant lifestyle, nightlife and cultural identity.

Produced by longtime Patoranking collaborator Ctea, the song combines rolling basslines, syncopated drums and a chant-driven hook, with Patoranking's signature blend of Afrobeats, reggae and dancehall.

Olamide complements the record with a verse that pays homage to Lagos, referencing the city's traditional praise name and celebrating the place both musicians call home.

An official music video directed by UAX was also released alongside the single. The filmmaker previously worked with Patoranking on the visuals for ‘African Soldier’, his collaboration with Jamaican reggae and dancehall star Buju Banton.

‘Welcome To Lagos’ is the fourth single from Patoranking's forthcoming fifth studio album, following earlier releases including ‘No Jonze’, ‘African Soldier’ featuring Buju Banton and ‘Shake That’ featuring Ruger.

The collaboration also comes ahead of Olamide's 13th studio album, Time & Space, scheduled for release on November 16, 2026. It follows his announcement of a headline performance at London's O2 Arena on March 25, 2027.

Patoranking rounds off eventful year with new collaboration

The release comes after a busy year for Patoranking, marked by international performances, award recognition and activities beyond music.

The singer recently completed a summer festival run across the UK and Europe, performing at events including Africa Oye, Summerjam, Sunsplash and Reggae Geel.

In September, he returned to Lagos for a headline performance at TRACE Live, where he celebrated 10 years of his debut album, God Over Everything, originally released in 2016.

That same month, he won Best Male Reggae/Dancehall at the 2026 African Muzik Magazine Awards (AFRIMMA) in Dallas, Texas. His collaboration with Ruger, ‘Shake That’, was also nominated for Best Collaboration.

In October, Patoranking headlined the Nigerian Independence Day Parade in New York and received the Philanthropy Impact Award from the Nigerian Consulate in New York and the Organization for the Advancement of Nigerians (OAN), recognising his philanthropic contributions.

Beyond his music career, the artiste has supported youth development and education through initiatives including the ALU Patoranking Scholarship, which provides fully funded educational opportunities to students across Africa.

A decade of global music success

Born Patrick Nnaemeka Okorie on May 27, 1990, in Ebute Metta, Lagos, Patoranking rose to prominence with his breakout single ‘Girlie O’ and went on to establish an international following through songs such as ‘My Woman, My Everything’ and ‘Abule’.

His discography includes God Over Everything (2016), Wilmer (2019), Three (2020) and World Best (2023).

His 2023 album featured collaborations with international and African acts including Ludacris, Beenie Man, Popcaan, Diamond Platnumz, Victony and Kizz Daniel.

With more than 800 million YouTube views and hundreds of millions of streams reported across digital platforms, Patoranking has built a career that connects Afrobeats, reggae and dancehall audiences across different markets.

‘Welcome To Lagos’ adds another collaboration to his catalogue while bringing together two Nigerian artistes to celebrate the city that has played a significant role in shaping their musical journeys.

The single and its accompanying music video are available across digital music platforms.

Ghana News.title: Policy implementation gap undermining West African trade integration- GSA
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Shippers Authority (GSA) has warned that the gap between regional trade policy commitments and their actual implementation continues to undermine economic integration and cross-border trade in West Africa.

Deputy Chief Executive of the Authority, Silvia Asana Dauda Owu, says businesses operating across the region continue to face multiple checkpoints, cumbersome documentation, inconsistent regulations and unofficial payments, despite commitments by governments to facilitate trade.

She believes these challenges are increasing the cost of doing business and weakening the competitiveness of regional economies.

She made the remarks at the re-launch of Borderless Alliance, a regional platform seeking to strengthen trade facilitation, promote evidence-based advocacy and advance economic integration across West Africa.

“Let us move beyond discussions on regional integration and focus on practical actions. The future of regional trade depends not only what the policies we public, but more importantly, on our commitment to implementing them”, she said.

Acting Executive Director of the Borderless Alliance Secretariat, Efua Eshun, said the Alliance would continue to champion the free movement of goods and people across the region.

The relaunch is expected to reposition the organisation as a stronger platform for engaging governments and other stakeholders on policies and interventions needed to address persistent barriers to regional trade.

As part of the event, stakeholders were also sensitised on the new National Non-Tariff Barriers Reporting and Resolution Platform.

The digital platform is expected to improve the identification, reporting and resolution of non-tariff barriers that impede cross-border trade, including cumbersome administrative procedures and regulatory challenges.

The relaunch was held under the theme, “Pioneering Digital Trade Facilitation and Regional Integration,” highlighting the role of digital solutions in improving trade processes and strengthening regional cooperation.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
