“For a government to exist, it must care for the vulnerable. It must care for the poor and those living with disabilities. If we don’t care for the poor, we are not caring for ourselves,” he said.

He explained that the town hall meetings were designed to provide an opportunity for citizens to communicate their concerns and expectations directly to those seeking political office.

Earlier, during a courtesy visit to the Plateau State Traditional Council in Jos, Mr Obi said Nigeria could not make meaningful progress while citizens continued to live in fear.

He called for competent, committed and compassionate leadership capable of responding effectively to the challenges confronting the country.

“We want a government that has the capacity to do the job. We want a government that has compassion, a government that hears the cries of mothers who have lost their children,” he said.

“We want a government that is committed to the future of Nigeria. Commitment is very important, and that is what we are going to offer Nigerians.”

Responding, the Gbong Gwom Jos, Da Jacob Gyang Buba, appealed to politicians and Nigerians to ensure that political activities did not aggravate the country’s security challenges.

He urged political actors to promote peaceful coexistence and mutual respect among citizens, regardless of their ethnic and religious differences.

“We want to appeal to all politicians and all Nigerians that we should not allow politics to worsen our situation. We already have insecurity, and we must be determined to live with each other in peace and with respect for one another,” he said.

The traditional ruler also prayed for divine guidance in the emergence of a leader capable of governing Nigeria effectively and restoring its greatness.

He urged politicians to conduct their activities peacefully and avoid actions capable of heightening tensions during the electioneering period.

World.title: US House Committee to review Nigeria’s response to attacks on Christians
World.content:
The US House Subcommittee on Africa will hold a congressional hearing on Thursday to review the efforts of the Nigerian government to protect Christians from terrorists in the last year.

The congressional hearing, which will be led by the committee chairman, Chris Smith, a Republican lawmaker, will focus on terrorist operations in Benue and other states in the Middle Belt.

The hearing, titled “One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt,” is expected to examine religious violence and “Christian persecution” in Nigeria.

This comes a week after the US midterm elections, in which Republicans lost badly across the country. Mr Smith, however, retained his seat in the House.

According to a statement issued by Mr Smith’s office, the congressional hearing will assess the operations of radical Islamist groups, including Boko Haram and armed Fulani groups, against Christian communities in the Middle East.

It will also assess the Nigerian government’s efforts to protect vulnerable communities and prosecute perpetrators.

“Chris Smith will chair his fourteenth congressional hearing on the religious persecution of Christians by radical Islamist groups in Nigeria, as well as the Nigerian government’s efforts to mitigate the violence and protect vulnerable communities in the Middle Belt.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The congressional hearing assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities,” the statement read.

The statement also noted that the committee would consider steps the US government could take to ensure that Nigerian authorities address and prevent “systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.”

Mr Chris is one of the lawmakers who pushed the Christian genocide narrative against Nigeria last year amid US President Donald Trump’s antagonism.

Some US lawmakers and members of President Donald Trump’s administration have repeatedly made claims of a Christian genocide in Nigeria despite evidence to the contrary.

In February, Mr Chris also introduced the Nigeria Religious Freedom and Accountability Act to Congress, which seeks to sanction individuals and groups suspected of religious violence.

It sought to impose sanctions on Rabiu Kwankwaso, former Kano governor, alongside Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Miyetti Allah Kautal Hore, and the Fulani-ethnic nomad militias in Nigeria for their alleged ties to extremist groups.

In July, the House passed a bill to withhold all foreign assistance to Nigeria until it can certify that Nigeria is taking effective steps to protect Christians from violence.

The bill is known as the National Security Department of State and Related Programs Appropriations Act for Fiscal Year 2027.

The provision to cut foreign assistance to Nigeria was championed by Riley Moore and other Republican lawmakers.

Although the bill initially restricted US assistance to 50 per cent, Republicans proposed withholding all foreign assistance.

This implies that Nigeria’s access to foreign aid in the 2027 fiscal year depends on Congress’s view of its efforts against violent extremism.

Nigeria’s relationship with the US has improved in recent months, as both countries have set up mechanisms to continue dialogue and cooperation on security and trade.

World.title: Court remands FIJ journalist Daniel Ojukwu over 2023 reports about presidential aide
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Tuesday remanded Daniel Ojukwu, a Foundation for Investigative Journalism (FIJ) reporter, in prison over a series of stories he authored in 2023 about Adejoke Orelope-Adefulire, the senior special assistant on sustainable development goals (SSAP-SDGs) to the president.

The judge, Joyce Abdulmalik,.ordered Mr Ojukwu remanded in the Kuje Correctional Centre until 1 December, implying the journalist will be in detention for the next 21 days.

Ms Abdulmalik issued the order in a 12-count cyberstalking case brought by the Nigerian police against Mr Ojukwu and the FIJ founder, Fisayo Soyombo.

Mr Ojukwu, who had been detained after honouring a police invitation, was produced in court on Tuesday to face the charges dated 19 December 2024.

The prosecutors accused Mr Ojukwu of defaming Mrs Orelope-Adefulire with his report. They also alleged that the report put the official “in fear of death”.

Mr Ojukwu pleaded not guilty to all 12 counts read to him during the proceedings.

The prosecution, led by Kunle Lawal, informed the court that Mr Soyombo was at large and applied for a bench warrant for his arrest. The judge denied the application, stating that Mr. Soyombo had not yet been brought before her to enable her to issue a bench warrant compelling his attendance.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, after Mr Ojukwu entered his plea of not guilty, the prosecution requested that he be remanded in prison,

Opposing the call for Mr Ojukwu’s remand, defence lawyer Atanda Kayode drew the court’s attention to a pending bail application filed on behalf of the defendant.

But the judge said the bail application, filed only on Monday, was not ripe for hearing.

The defence lawyer then requested that Mr Ojukwu be allowed to continue enjoying the prior administrative bail granted him by the police, the terms of which he had never violated.

The judge rejected the request. She said the defendant filed his bail application only on Monday, even though the charges had been served on him long ago.

The judge adjourned the bail application hearing until December and ordered Mr Ojukwu remanded in the Kuje Correctional Centre till then.

Ojukwu’s travails

The remand order came about two years after Mr Ojukwu was abducted by the officers of the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) in May 2024 over FIJ reports regarding Mrs Orelope-Adefulire, a former deputy governor of Lagos State.

He was held in custody for 10 days.

PREMIUM TIMES reported how Mr Ojukwu went missing on 1 May 2024, with his phones switched off and whereabouts unknown to colleagues, family and friends. The following day, FIJ made a missing person report at police stations in the area where he was headed.

Mr Ojukwu’s family and employer would later find out that he was “abducted” by the Intelligence Response Team (IRT) of the Inspector General of Police, and held incommunicado at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Panti in Lagos.

The reporter was later transferred to the Nigerian Police Force National Cybercrime Centre (NPF-NCCC) in Abuja, where he was detained for an additional five days.

Police spokesperson at the time, Muyiwa Adejobi, said the journalist’s arrest was based on a petition written against him, accusing him of violating the Cybercrimes Act, a well-known law that the Nigerian authorities have constantly used to suppress press freedom.

The petition was in relation to a story authored by Mr Ojukwu, revealing how the senior special assistant to then-president Muhammad Buhari on sustainable development goals (SSAP-SDGs), Mrs Orelope-Adefulire, was said to have paid N147 million to a restaurant for the construction of classrooms in Lagos.

Prior to Mr Ojukwu’s abduction, the Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre (NPF-NCCC) invited and grilled the chairperson of FIJ’s Board of Trustees, Bukky Shonibare, in Abuja during which they mentioned the story.

However, the police never invited Mr Ojukwu or any other FIJ staffer except for Ms Shonibare.

The police accused Mr Ojukwu of defaming Mrs Orelope-Adefulire as the senior special assistant on sustainable development goals (SSAP-SDGs) to the president.

He was released on 10 May 2024, after public outcry and human rights pressure. However, the NPF-NCCC has since withheld his passport on the grounds that he would flee the country.

He has appeared before the NPF-NCCC multiple times over this case.

Charges

A certified true copy of the charge sheet obtained by PREMIUM TIMES on Tuesday showed that it was dated 19 September 2024. It relates to four reports published on FIJ’s website between November 2023 and January 2024.

In the first count, the police accused Mr Soyombo and Mr Ojukwu of conspiring to commit cyberstalking, or aiding and abetting the offence, sometime between 2023 and 2024.

Counts two and three concern reports published on 7 November and 3 December 2023. The police alleged that the publications were intended to harass Ms Adefulire and put her in fear of death, violence or bodily harm.

The 7 November report, titled Special Report: 2 Weeks Before End of Buhari’s Tenure, Special Assistant, Adefulire Paid a Restaurant N147.1m to Build Classrooms in Lagos. A Lot Was Amiss, examined a N147.1 million payment by the SDGs office to a restaurant for classroom construction in Lagos.

The second report, published on 3 December and titled How Orelope-Adefulire’s OSSAP-SDGs Paid N47.5m for Shady Contract on Amosun’s Request, questioned a N47.5 million classroom construction contract awarded to Tru3 Nigeria Limited.

FIJ raised questions about the contractor’s status, the alleged failure to mobilise to the project site and the payment for what it described as a vague block of classrooms.

In count four, the police accused the journalists of cyberstalking over a 9 November 2023 report titled Flashback: How EFCC Made Orelope-Adefulire’s SDGs Forfeit N241m Instead of Billions. The publication examined the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission’s forfeiture of N241 million linked to the SDGs office.

Count six concerns a 21 January 2024 report, One Week After OSSAP-SDGs Built Classroom Blocks in Amosun’s District, Solar Panels Stop Working. FIJ reported that solar panels installed at the classroom blocks stopped working a week after installation. The police alleged that the report was intended to harass Ms Adefulire.

The other six counts accuse the journalists of criminal defamation.

In count seven, the police alleged that Mr Soyombo and Mr Ojukwu conspired to defame Ms Adefulire sometime between 2023 and 2024.

Counts eight and nine concern the reports on the N147.1 million payment and the N47.5 million contract, respectively. The police accused the journalists of publishing the reports knowing their contents to be false.

Count ten relates to the report on the EFCC’s forfeiture of N241 million, while counts eleven and twelve concern the N47.5 million contract and the report on the solar panels. In each case, the police alleged that the journalists knowingly published false and defamatory material about Ms Adefulire.

World.title: 2027: All Jigawa former governors with Tinubu, including Sule Lamido – Shettima
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has declared that Jigawa State remains firmly under the control of the All Progressives Congress (APC), stating that all four former governors of the state—including prominent opposition figure Sule Lamido—now back the president.

Speaking on Tuesday during an APC campaign rally in Dutse, the state capital, Mr Shettima expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would secure decisive support from the state in the 2027 presidential election.

The vice president named former governors Ali Sa’ad, Saminu Turaki, Muhammad Badaru, and Sule Lamido among the political heavyweights aligning with the party.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Mr Lamido, who is in the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Nyesom Wike-backed faction, is yet to respond to Mr Shettima’s claim.

“Jigawa State is home to the APC. Every notable politician of consequence is with us,” Mr Shettima stated. “The former governors of Jigawa State—Ali Sa’ad, Ibrahim Saminu Turaki, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, and even Alhaji Sule Lamido—are with us.”

Mr Shettima said President Tinubu is a leader deeply committed to northern Nigeria, pointing to major infrastructure initiatives underway across the region.

He cited the revival and completion of previously abandoned road networks, ongoing rail expansions, and the Greater Dutse Water Project as proof of the administration’s delivery on key campaign promises.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Shettima urged Jigawa residents to turn out en masse to reciprocate the administration’s investments by delivering a landslide victory for President Tinubu and other APC candidates in 2027, noting that the people of the North are historically recognised for rewarding goodwill and loyalty.

World.title: FG provides 80,906 free caesarean sections, reports 22% drop in obstetric emergency deaths
World.content:
The Nigerian government says it has provided 80,906 free caesarean sections under its emergency obstetric care programme, alongside a 22 per cent reduction in deaths from obstetric emergencies in participating health facilities.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, disclosed this on Tuesday at the 2026 Nigeria Health Sector Joint Annual Review (JAR) in Abuja.

Mr Pate said nearly 100,000 free emergency obstetric and newborn healthcare services had been delivered since the programme was announced two years ago.

According to him, the services included 80,906 caesarean sections, approximately 9,100 newborn services and 6,059 repairs for vesicovaginal fistula, a condition that can cause continuous leakage of urine following childbirth injuries.

“Two years after we announced the free emergency obstetric care programme, almost 100,000 services have been delivered,” he said.

“Deaths from obstetric emergencies have fallen by 22 per cent in participating facilities. These are among the highest-risk maternal cases.”

The programme is part of the government’s efforts to reduce preventable maternal and newborn deaths by improving access to emergency healthcare, particularly for women who cannot afford treatment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A caesarean section is a surgical procedure used to deliver a baby through an incision in the abdomen and uterus, typically when healthcare providers determine it’s safer for the mother, baby, or both.

Despite its necessity in many cases, the high cost of a C-section in Nigeria has long been a major barrier, preventing many women from accessing this critical care during childbirth.

Expansion of emergency maternal healthcare

Mr Pate said the government had also strengthened emergency obstetric and newborn healthcare services by providing equipment to more than 300 secondary healthcare facilities and over 500 primary healthcare centres (PHCs).

He explained that the secondary facilities were equipped to provide comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care, while the PHCs were supported to deliver basic emergency services.

“The facilities, staff and referral services must work together if we are to reduce preventable deaths,” he said.

The minister also highlighted progress under the Maternal and Newborn Mortality Reduction Innovation Initiative (MAMII), which targets communities with high maternal and newborn mortality burdens.

He said the initiative had mapped and linked 750,000 pregnant women to functional health facilities.

According to him, emergency transport services operated in 171 of the 172 local government areas covered by MAMII and transported 104,566 women and newborns.

Across the wider referral network, he said 1,053 transport assets and 9,050 community drivers had transported 168,571 patients.

“These arrangements are connecting women and newborns to the care they need,” he said.

Free caesarean sections

In November 2024, PREMIUM TIMES reported that the federal government had announced free caesarean sections for eligible pregnant women as part of efforts to reduce maternal and newborn deaths.

The intervention was initially piloted in August 2024 in four healthcare facilities in Kano and Akwa Ibom states before expanding to other locations.

By April 2025, Mr Pate announced that more than 4,000 women had benefited from free caesarean sections through the programme.

During the same period, the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) disclosed that the intervention had commenced in more than 100 hospitals across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

NHIA explained that eligible women who could not afford the procedure could receive it free of charge after an assessment by the hospital’s social welfare team.

It said beneficiaries were required to provide their National Identification Number, which could be presented before or after admission.

The programme involves federal, state, private and faith-based hospitals, with the NHIA coordinating payments for eligible services.

In September 2026, the government also introduced incentives under MAMII to encourage greater use of maternal and newborn healthcare services and address barriers preventing women from receiving timely care.

Maternal deaths remain a concern

Despite the reported improvements, maternal and newborn deaths remain major public health concerns in Nigeria.

At the review, the National Coordinator of the Sector-Wide Approach Coordination Office, Muntaqa Umar-Sadiq, identified shortages of skilled health workers and gaps in Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (CEmONC) services as challenges affecting healthcare delivery.

“Investments in CEmONC facilities, infrastructure and equipment must be matched with adequate numbers of skilled health workers. We must also modernise our tertiary health institutions,” he said.

Mr Umar-Sadiq stressed the need to improve the deployment and retention of skilled health workers, particularly in facilities providing emergency obstetric and newborn care.

The 2026 Joint Annual Review, held under the theme “Make the Data Count”, brings together federal and state government officials, development partners and other stakeholders to assess progress under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative.

The initiative is being implemented through the Sector-Wide Approach, which seeks to improve coordination, financing and accountability in healthcare delivery.

World.title: 2027: Peter Obi meets Plateau traditional rulers, decries insecurity
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Tuesday visited the Plateau State Traditional Council in Jos, where he expressed concern over insecurity in the state.

Mr Obi, who was received by the Gbong Gwom Jos, Da Jacob Buba, said Plateau State’s security challenges required urgent attention, stressing that meaningful development would remain difficult while citizens continued to live in fear.

The visit was part of his campaign for the 2027 general elections and preceded a town hall meeting in the state.

The former Anambra State Governor said he embarked on the consultations to listen to citizens, understand their challenges and identify practical solutions.

“When you want to serve, you must listen to the people. When we come for campaigns, we only talk, and we don’t listen to the people. We have decided that leadership must be demand-driven,” he said.

Mr Obi recalled his visits to troubled communities in Plateau, including Bokkos, Barkin Ladi and Mangu, describing the security situation as unacceptable.

He said his presidential ambition was driven by the need to address the suffering of Nigerians, particularly victims of violence, displaced persons and families who had lost loved ones.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“If I have one person in an IDP camp, it means we are all in an IDP camp. I am competing because I want to know how we talk to that mother whose child was killed, that husband who lost a wife and that woman who lost a husband. Who is going to listen to their cries?”

He stressed that residents should be able to pursue their livelihoods without fear, saying children must return safely from school, farmers from their farms and traders from the markets.

Mr Obi also expressed concern over poverty, infant mortality and the growing number of out-of-school children, arguing that investments in education, healthcare and agriculture could help address the challenges.

Responding, the Gbong Gwom Jos urged politicians and Nigerians to ensure that political activities did not aggravate the country’s security challenges.

Mr Buba called for peaceful political engagement, mutual respect and coexistence, noting that Plateau and other parts of the country were already grappling with insecurity.

“We want to appeal to all politicians and all Nigerians that we should not allow politics to worsen our situation. We already have insecurity, and we must be determined to live with each other in peace and with respect for one another,” he said.

The traditional ruler also prayed for divine guidance in the emergence of a leader capable of governing Nigeria effectively and restoring its greatness.

He urged politicians to promote peace and avoid actions capable of creating further tension during the 2027 electioneering period.

World.title: 2027: Avoid technicalities, treat electronic evidence rigorously, INEC charges tribunals
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has urged members of the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals to avoid technicalities that defeat substantive justice and to subject electronic evidence to rigorous scrutiny.

He also told them to keep firm control of their courtrooms and let “truth of the ballot prevail”.

According to the commission’s Daily Bulletin of Tuesday, Amupitan spoke on Monday in Abuja while delivering the Commission’s opening remarks at a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the tribunals, held at the Body of Benchers Complex. The Court of Appeal organised the workshop under the theme “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability.”

The INEC chairman said electoral litigation had grown more complex, with disputes now touching on voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results, technological failures and the integrity of digital records.

On the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), he said technology should neither be treated as infallible nor dismissed simply because the evidence is electronic.

Amupitan warned that digital disinformation driven by artificial intelligence, audio cloning and deepfake videos would inevitably spill into the courtrooms. He urged the tribunals to apply strict evidentiary standards under Section 84 of the Evidence Act, saying digital provenance, forensic chain of custody and reliance on certified data from INEC would be vital to stop synthetic fabrications from misleading the courts.

He added that electoral adjudication is evidence-driven, and that allegations of irregularities, non-compliance or result manipulation must be proved with credible and legally admissible evidence.

According to him, the Commission has issued the Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections, 2026, to give clearer operational standards against which claims of non-compliance can be weighed in proceedings.

The INEC chairman told the tribunal members that they carry the democratic aspirations of over 200 million Nigerians once they take their oaths. He described the courtroom as the altar on which public confidence in constitutional governance is preserved, and urged them to let their decisions reflect deep fidelity to the law, uncompromising integrity and the principle that justice must be seen to be done.

Amupitan said Nigeria’s political stability in 2027 would depend not only on how efficiently INEC conducts elections, but also on how courageously, transparently and justly the tribunals settle the disputes that follow.

He described the Election Petition Tribunal as a constitutional valve that releases political pressure and keeps electoral friction from degenerating into civil disruption. A tribunal that acts with procedural speed, evidentiary rigour and absolute impartiality, he said, assures aggrieved parties that a credible platform exists to assess their complaints on merit.

The workshop, he noted, was taking place at a pivotal point in the country’s democratic journey. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on January 16, 2027, followed by the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6, 2027.

Amupitan said the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests on two pillars: impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He added that no institution can secure electoral integrity alone, since credible elections need an impartial electoral management body, responsible political parties, informed citizens, professional security agencies and an independent, effective judiciary.

He commended the Court of Appeal, the National Judicial Institute and the legal experts behind the Second Edition of the Judicial Electoral Manual (JEM), 2026, calling it an indispensable compass for consistency in judicial reasoning. Conflicting decisions on similar facts, he said, create legal uncertainty and erode public confidence.

The INEC chairman stressed that engagement between the Commission and the Judiciary must stay within constitutional limits and must never become a channel for influencing judicial decisions or discussing the merits of pending cases. He assured the Judiciary that INEC respects those boundaries and remains committed to complying with valid judicial decisions.

The event featured the swearing-in of the chairmen and members of the 2027 tribunals, and the unveiling of the Second Edition of the manual by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat M. O. Kekere-Ekun.

The President of the Court of Appeal, Justice M. B. Dongban-Mensem, disclosed that 375 judicial officers had been nominated to serve on the tribunals, made up of 138 returning members with previous tribunal experience and 237 newly nominated members.

She urged the nominees to stay steadfast in judicial independence, resist every form of improper influence and discourage unnecessary adjournments, stressing that speed must never come at the expense of fairness.

World.title: Makinde presents N1.12trn final budget
World.content:
…Allocates 60% to capital expenditure

…Dismisses appointees’ resignations as meaningless

By Adeola Badru

Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Tuesday presented a proposed N1.12 trillion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, describing it as the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, while dismissing the recent resignations of political appointees as inconsequential.

Makinde said the departure of some officials from his administration would not distract his government or affect its commitment to delivering its mandate.

The governor made the remarks while presenting the 2027 Appropriation Bill, valued at N1,115,341,378,359.94, before lawmakers at the Parliament Building, Secretariat, Ibadan.

Speaking against the backdrop of recent resignations by political appointees and other government officials, Makinde said he was keeping count of those who had left but insisted that their decisions were of no significance to his administration.

He also disclosed that one of the female officials who resigned had approached him with what he described as an impossible request, adding that she tendered her resignation after he declined to grant it.

The presentation is particularly significant as the proposed estimates represent the final appropriation bill of Makinde’s administration, which is expected to complete its second term in 2027.

Under the proposal, capital expenditure accounts for N670.03 billion, representing 60.07 per cent of the total budget, while recurrent expenditure stands at N445.31 billion, or 39.93 per cent.

Explaining the allocation, the governor said the proposed spending reflected his administration’s determination to sustain infrastructure development, consolidate existing achievements and strengthen the delivery of essential services across the state.

He said about 60 per cent of every N100 provided for in the budget would go into capital investments, stressing that infrastructure remained central to economic growth and long-term prosperity.

Makinde, however, cautioned that physical infrastructure alone could not guarantee meaningful development without adequate investment in human resources and essential public services.

He said schools needed teachers, hospitals required healthcare professionals, medicines and equipment, while public institutions must be adequately staffed and equipped to function effectively.

According to him, the proposed budget was also informed by consultations with stakeholders and residents across the state’s administrative and political zones, whose concerns and expectations shaped the government’s spending priorities.

The governor also used the occasion to advocate continuity in governance beyond the expiration of his tenure, unveiling what he called the Omituntun 3.0 agenda.

He said the initiative was designed to prevent a reversal of the development trajectory established by his administration over the past seven and a half years after the 2027 governorship election.

Makinde said: “Over the last seven-plus years, we have worked towards sustaining the development trajectory of Oyo State. For the candidates we have recommended for continuity, we refer to this agenda as Omituntun 3.0.

“While political parties may contest elections and some may emerge victorious while others lose, our overriding concern is to ensure that the development of the state does not suffer a setback.

“For the continued development of Oyo State in 2027 and beyond, I will place this agenda before the Governor, while the incoming administration will also be expected to take it forward from where we stop.”

The proposed 2027 budget represents an increase over the original 2026 appropriation of N891.99 billion, which allocated N502.85 billion, representing 56.37 per cent, to capital expenditure and N389.14 billion, or 43.63 per cent, to recurrent spending.

However, following the approval of a N210 billion supplementary budget by the State House of Assembly in September 2026, the state’s total financial provision for the 2026 fiscal year rose to N1.102 trillion.

Meanwhile, Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Adebo Edward Ogundoyin, described the presentation of the 2027 budget as a significant milestone in the state’s democratic and developmental journey, being the final budget cycle of the Makinde administration.

Ogundoyin said the occasion offered an opportunity to consolidate the achievements of the past seven and a half years, sustain ongoing programmes and strengthen the foundation for sustainable growth.

He recalled that the first budget of the Omituntun 2.0 administration was presented before the Assembly on December 5, 2023, describing the latest presentation as another important moment in the relationship between the Executive and Legislative Arms of Government.

The Speaker said the state had witnessed considerable developments in infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and security under the present administration.

He listed investments in road construction and rehabilitation, school infrastructure, healthcare facilities, agricultural development and workers’ welfare as efforts aimed at repositioning the state for sustainable development.

Ogundoyin disclosed that the 10th Assembly, since its inauguration in June 2023, had passed 41 bills into law, processed 146 committee reports and 184 motions, and adopted more than 1,500 resolutions on issues affecting the welfare, security and development of residents.

He said the Assembly had also strengthened participatory lawmaking through public hearings and stakeholder engagements, adding that it had organised 11 major public hearings and stakeholder meetings within the period.

Among the legislative proposals and policy issues considered, he listed the Oyo State Real Properties Protection Bill, Presumptive Tax Bill, Consumer Protection Agency Bill, Oyo State Roads Fund Bill and Single-Use Plastics Prohibition Bill.

He added that the Assembly had engaged stakeholders on market administration, cooperative societies, public safety and the remuneration of political and public office holders.

The Speaker identified the establishment of a Post-Legislative Scrutiny (PLS) Unit in January 2025 as one of the major institutional achievements of the 10th Assembly.

He described the Oyo legislature as the first State House of Assembly in Nigeria to establish a dedicated unit for the exercise.

According to him, the unit had scrutinised the Oyo State Open Rearing and Grazing Regulation Law, 2019, and the Oyo State Security Network Agency Law, 2020, to assess their implementation, identify challenges and recommend improvements.

Ogundoyin said recommendations from the scrutiny of the Open Rearing and Grazing Regulation Law had informed the progress of its amendment bill, which had passed second reading in the Assembly.

He also disclosed that a post-legislative scrutiny inquiry had commenced on the Oyo State Sexual and Gender-Based Response Agency and Referral Law.

On security, the Speaker said the Assembly had organised a security summit that brought together relevant stakeholders to examine the state’s security situation and develop practical responses to emerging challenges.

He maintained that the legislature had continued to discharge its constitutional oversight responsibilities beyond the passage of appropriation bills, with a commitment to transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources.

Ogundoyin assured the governor that the House would subject the proposed 2027 budget to thorough legislative scrutiny, guided by the interests of residents.

He said the estimates should consolidate existing achievements, prioritise the completion of ongoing projects and address critical developmental needs across the state.

The Speaker also appealed to Makinde to address welfare concerns raised by the Parliamentary Staff Association of Nigeria (PASAN), Oyo State Chapter.

The requests, he said, included an upward review of the Consolidated Legislative Salary Structure (CONLESS) to 100 per cent, regularisation of ad-hoc staff appointments and the release of a bus earlier approved for the association.

He said addressing the demands would improve staff welfare, strengthen institutional capacity, enhance productivity and sustain industrial harmony within the Legislative Arm.

On the 2027 general elections, Ogundoyin expressed confidence that residents would support candidates of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), citing what he described as the administration’s record in governance, infrastructure and people-centred policies.

He also expressed optimism that an incoming APM administration would implement the proposed 2027 budget and complete the projects and programmes contained in it.

Earlier, lawmakers representing constituencies across the state commended Makinde’s administration, describing its leadership as visionary, inclusive and people-oriented.

They highlighted what they considered achievements in infrastructure, education, healthcare and residents’ welfare since the administration assumed office in 2019.

The lawmakers particularly praised the administration’s investment in Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), describing the acquisition of sole ownership of the institution by the Oyo State Government as a landmark achievement in the education sector.

Some also commended the governor’s approach to appointments, saying his emphasis on merit had created opportunities for people without established political connections to occupy positions of responsibility.

World.title: IPOB accuses Britain of complicity in Kanu’s rendition
World.content:
By Steve Oko

The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has accused the British government of complicity in the alleged persecution of its detained leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, particularly his abduction in Kenya and extraordinary rendition to Nigeria.

The group also accused Britain of maintaining diplomatic silence over what it described as persistent violations of Kanu’s fundamental rights, despite his British citizenship.

IPOB made the allegations in a statement issued by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Comrade Emma Powerful, following recent interventions by Bishop Godfrey Onah on historical injustices associated with Nigeria’s colonial experience and the treatment of the South-East.

The pro-Biafra group said Britain’s historical involvement in Nigeria’s political and economic affairs had contributed to what it described as structural injustices against Biafra and its people.

It alleged that Britain’s failure to intervene over Kanu’s rendition, its response to calls for his release and what it described as the disregard of previous appellate court decisions reflected a continuation of colonial-era policies that prioritised strategic interests over justice.

IPOB also accused the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) and other Western media organisations of promoting what it described as an anti-Kanu narrative.

It claimed that online searches for Kanu’s name predominantly returned negative reports, alleging that such coverage had contributed to what it called a distorted international perception of his agitation and the circumstances surrounding his prosecution.

The group further alleged that Kanu’s transfer to a prison in Sokoto was politically motivated, claiming it was an attempt by the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government to use his detention as a political bargaining tool to secure support in the North ahead of future elections.

It, however, claimed that the alleged political calculation had backfired and cautioned against using Northern Nigerians as instruments in what it described as divisive political manoeuvring.

On Kanu’s trial, IPOB faulted the characterisation of its leader as someone who hates the North, insisting that his agitation was directed against what it called a corrupt neo-colonial political structure, rather than any ethnic or religious group.

The group specifically challenged a remark attributed to Justice Omotosho that Kanu hated the North with a passion, describing it as a distortion of his broadcasts and political message.

According to IPOB, Kanu’s struggle is against a system it alleges exploits the resources and sacrifices of ordinary Nigerians for the benefit of the political elite.

It maintained that Bishop Onah’s intervention reflected growing recognition of the historical grievances of Biafrans and the need to address the issues underlying the agitation.

The group insisted that what it described as media manipulation and judicial and political manoeuvring would not derail its campaign for the peaceful emancipation of Biafra.

IPOB called on the British government to break its silence and take a more decisive position on Kanu’s case, arguing that its alleged inaction, despite his British citizenship, raised questions about its commitment to protecting the rights of its citizens abroad.

World.title: Carex Rewards Thousands Of Consumers As Everybody Wins Promo Concludes With Grand Finale Live Draw
World.content:
Carex, one of Nigeria’s leading personal hygiene brands, has successfully concluded its nationwide Everybody Wins Promo with a transparent Grand Finale Live Draw, rewarding loyal consumers and reinforcing its commitment to delivering value beyond personal care products.

The campaign, which ran from June 2026 to August 2026, attracted millions of consumers PAN Nigeria and rewarded winners with prizes worth over ₦400,000,000.

The Grand Finale Live Draw, held in Lagos, brought together consumers, media representatives, trade partners, regulatory officials, and other key stakeholders to witness the selection of the campaign’s grand prize winner through a transparent and independently supervised process. The event marked the culmination of months of consumer participation and engagement, further strengthening the connection between the Carex brand and its consumers.

Throughout the promotion, participants had multiple opportunities to win exciting rewards, including instant Recharge Cards, shopping Vouchers, and a brand-new Car. Over 90,000 consumers emerged as winners over the course of the campaign. The grand prize car winner, Faith Stephen from Ijebu Ode, Ogun State, emerged through the live draw process conducted in accordance with all applicable promotional and regulatory requirements.

Speaking at the event, Ifunanya Anwunah, Head of Category – Personal Hygiene, said:

“At Carex, we believe that the consumers who trust our products every day deserve to be appreciated and rewarded. The Everybody Wins Promo was created as a tangible expression of our gratitude for the loyalty and support we continue to receive from Nigerian families.

The overwhelming participation and enthusiasm witnessed throughout this campaign demonstrate the strong connection consumers have with the Carex brand.

The promo was built on a simple promise: giving everyday consumers the opportunity to win meaningful rewards while enjoying the quality, care, and protection they have come to trust from Carex.

As a brand trusted by millions of Nigerians for their personal hygiene and care needs, Carex remains committed to developing initiatives that deepen consumer engagement, reward loyalty, and create memorable experiences for consumers across the country. The successful completion of the Everybody Wins Promo further underscores the brand’s commitment to putting consumers at the heart of everything it does.

ABOUT CAREX

Carex is committed to winning the war against germs through a range of antibacterial products that support the health, hygiene, and wellbeing of consumers. Through innovative products and engaging consumer initiatives, Carex continues to build meaningful connections with families across Nigeria, delivering trusted products that help consumers live healthier and more confident lives.

World.title: ADC-PCC to Tinubu: Where is the electricity you promised Nigerians?
World.content:
President Tinubu

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for his unfulfilled electricity pledge, accusing him of resorting to personal attacks, divisive rhetoric and recycled promises instead of presenting a credible scorecard of his administration.

The Council said Nigerians expected the President to explain what had become of his major campaign promises after nearly three-and-a-half years in office, particularly against the backdrop of worsening insecurity, widespread hunger, rising living costs and massive government borrowings.

In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC said Tinubu’s recent campaign outings in Kaduna, Rivers and Jigawa states offered little beyond verbal attacks on opponents and familiar promises.

Recalling the President’s electricity pledge, the Council challenged him to explain why millions of Nigerians were still struggling with unreliable power supply.

“If I don’t give you electricity, don’t vote for me for a second term,” it quoted Tinubu as saying.

The ADC-PCC described his renewed electricity promises during the Jigawa campaign as an attempt to repackage an old commitment, adding that the President had reportedly invested in alternative power arrangements for his personal comfort.

The Council also questioned the fate of 2,000 tractors reportedly imported from Brazil under the administration’s mechanised farming initiative, alleging that they had yet to make any meaningful impact on agricultural productivity.

It further accused Tinubu of taking credit for projects initiated by his predecessor, late President Muhammadu Buhari, insisting that his administration had little of its own to showcase.

On the state of democracy, the ADC-PCC accused the President of undermining the independence of democratic institutions, alleging undue influence over the National Assembly and attempts to compromise the Judiciary.

It also took issue with Tinubu’s declaration that ‘all is fair in politics’. warning that such a position could encourage political illegality, intimidation, violence and thuggery.

The Council said: “The opposition is increasingly confronted with unconstitutional conduct, judicial rascality, political intimidation and a compromised electoral environment under the APC administration.”

Citing the President’s recent campaign outing in Rivers State, the ADC-PCC questioned his decision to praise and promise to reward a political figure whom it alleged had been illegally removed from office, denied political participation for six months and prevented from seeking re-election.

“Reward him for what?” Ologbondiyan queried, describing the President’s conduct as an affront to constitutional governance and the democratic rights of the people.

The Council accused Tinubu of deploying divisive rhetoric whenever confronted with questions about his administration’s performance, rather than providing verifiable answers to Nigerians.

It maintained that the country needed leadership anchored on accountability, competence, transparency and respect for democratic institutions.

World.title: N210trn not missing from NNPC – Mele Kyari tells Senate
World.content:
FILES: Former NNPC boss Mele Kyari

By Henry Umoru – ABUJA

The immediate past Group Chief Executive Officer, GCEO, of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company, NNPC, Limited, Mele Kyari has appeared before the Senate, refuting alleged unaccounted N210 trillion in the balance sheet of the National oil company as contained in the 2017 to 2023 Audit report.

Kyari who finally appeared before the Senator Ibrahim Dankwabo (PDP, Gombe North) led Senate Committee on Public Accounts said the alleged unaccounted figures arose from accounting entries which have nothing to do with financial loss.

He declared that no such financial infraction happened under him as Chief Executive of NNPCL from 2019 to 2025.

Kyari said, “I wish to confirm that nothing was lost. It is simply not possible that such an amount could have been lost under my care and leadership.

“The matter relates to accounting entries, which have nothing to do with any financial loss.

“They are bookkeeping issues, and I believe the appropriate explanations have been provided in my report.”

The former NNPCL boss who declared that the N5billion allegedly spent on change of name from NNPC to NNPCL , waa untrue as there was no spending like that under his watch, however refuted queries raised in the audit report on registration and incorporation of NNPC Ltd.

He said: “At the time of incorporation, the company was not owned by the Federation in the same manner.

“The Federation was therefore responsible for the payment relating to the incorporation of NNPC.

“However, NNPC made the payment on behalf of the Federation and subsequently charged it to the Federation’s revenue, which was reflected in what we referred to as the former NAPIMS account of NNPC.

“This was simply an accounting entry, involving approximately N2.99 billion. It was a payment made to government institutions responsible for providing the relevant services.

“I have also seen comments suggesting that N5 billion was paid for the naming of the company. That is not correct”.

According to him, NNPCL under him was transformed from loss incurring corporation to a profit making company, adding that prior to his assumption of office as Group Managing Director of NNPC in 2019 , the national oil company had a huge loss of $803billion in 2018 operational year , which gradually turned to o profit making under him from 2019 .

Kyari said, “Mr Chairman, you may be aware from the financial records that the company recorded a loss of about $803billion in 2018.

“I took over in 2019, and we did everything possible to transform the company into a profitable organisation which made it to for the first time in its 44 years of existence, recording sustained profits”

Satisfied with the submissions of Kyari , the Committee through its Chairman, Senator Dankwabo said , responses submitted to the queries shall be thoroughly studied for final decision on the audit report .

Dankwabo said, ” we shall interrogate the figures submitted by the former GMD to know whether to Invite him again or not .

” For now , he has responded to the two issues relating to his leadership of NNPC during the period under review.”

Vanguard News

World.title: ACF crisis deepens as chairman alleges invasion of secretariat
World.content:
— Osuman accuses individuals of breaking into Kaduna headquarters, removing valuables

By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

The leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has taken a fresh turn following allegations by its National Chairman, Maman Mike Osuman, that some individuals forcibly gained access to the organisation’s national secretariat in Kaduna and removed valuables.

In a petition dated November 9, 2026, and addressed to Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State, Osuman accused two individuals of allegedly breaking into the ACF headquarters at No. 11A Sokoto Road, Kaduna, without the authorisation of the recognised leadership.

The petition was also copied to the Inspector-General of Police, the Kaduna State Commissioner of Police and the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) in the state.

According to Osuman, the individuals allegedly gained access to the premises by breaking the gates and office doors, changing the locks and removing valuables and other properties belonging to the organisation.

He further alleged that the operation was carried out without the knowledge or consent of the recognised leadership of the forum and without a search warrant.

Describing the alleged incident as an assault on the institutional integrity of the organisation, Osuman appealed to Governor Sani to intervene to prevent further escalation of the crisis.

“An invasion of this nature not only violates the sanctity of our corporate headquarters but is also a direct assault on the dignity of the entire Northern Region,” he said.

The chairman described the national secretariat as the collective heritage of Northern Nigeria, stressing that its protection was essential to preserving the dignity and integrity of the organisation.

He urged the governor to use his good offices to ensure that the rule of law prevailed and that the forum was protected against actions capable of undermining its stability.

The latest allegation has renewed attention on the protracted leadership crisis within the ACF, particularly the disagreement over control of its national secretariat and the authority to manage the organisation’s affairs.

The dispute has been characterised by competing positions among the forum’s leadership organs over the interpretation of its constitution, leadership structure and the legitimacy of decisions taken by the contending sides.

In one of the major developments, the National Executive Committee (NEC) of the forum reportedly suspended its Board of Trustees (BoT) Chairman, Alhaji Bashir M. Dalhatu, over alleged violations of the organisation’s constitution.

The suspension followed an emergency NEC meeting held in Kaduna in May 2026, amid tensions over access to the ACF headquarters and reports of police restrictions ahead of the meeting.

However, the Board of Trustees subsequently rejected Dalhatu’s purported suspension, describing the decision as illegal and unconstitutional and an attempt to destabilise the northern socio-cultural organisation.

The opposing positions have exposed deep divisions within the forum, with stakeholders holding conflicting views over the interpretation of its constitution and the respective powers of its governing organs.

The latest allegations surrounding the secretariat have further heightened concerns over the prolonged dispute and its implications for the unity and credibility of an organisation established to articulate the collective interests of Northern Nigeria.

World.title: ADC-PCC to Tsoho: Explain why you transferred our case to Lifu
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho, to explain why he transferred a case from Justice Emeka Nwite to Justice Peter Lifu barely 24 hours after receiving the party’s formal protest against the reassignment.

The campaign council said the sequence of events raised serious questions about the handling of the case, particularly as Justice Nwite had already commenced hearing it and had neither recused himself nor ceased to be a serving judge.

It demanded the immediate release of the full judgment, saying the failure to provide an official copy was obstructing the party’s right to challenge the decision at the Court of Appeal.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Phrank Shaibu, on November 10, the ADC-PCC said its lawyers had submitted the legal questions to the appellate court but insisted that Nigerians deserved to know how the case was transferred to Justice Lifu despite the party’s formal objection.

The campaign council disclosed that the plaintiff had sought the transfer from Justice Nwite, citing delays and loss of confidence in obtaining a timely hearing.

However, it said its counsel, in a response dated May 11, 2026, challenged the plaintiff’s account of the adjournments, outlined the circumstances surrounding the delays and described the application as an attempt at forum shopping.

On June 2, the ADC National Secretary, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola, also wrote to Justice Tsoho, asking him to reverse the reassignment and formally protesting the transfer on grounds of the party’s lack of confidence in Justice Lifu’s impartiality.

The following day, the case was assigned to Justice Lifu.

Questioning the decision, Shaibu said: “Justice Tsoho received our protest. Why did he proceed with the transfer? What did he find in the plaintiff’s allegation of delay that outweighed the court record and our protest? Let him publish his reasons. Let Nigerians read them beside the letters.”

The campaign council said the Chief Judge owed Nigerians an explanation for disregarding the protest, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the transfer had created an appearance of possible bias.

It also cited Justice Lifu’s earlier decision in a separate suit, in which he ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to deregister the ADC and four other political parties despite an existing Court of Appeal order staying proceedings.

According to the ADC-PCC, the appellate court subsequently nullified the deregistration judgment, describing Justice Lifu’s decision to proceed with the matter as the ‘highest form of judicial impertinence’ and invoking Supreme Court authority on ‘judicial rascality’.

The council further cited a certified judgment delivered by Justice Musa Liman, who dismissed a challenge to the ADC leadership for lack of merit and locus standi.

It said Justice Liman had held that the internal party dispute was non-justiciable, declared the leadership handover lawful and affirmed INEC’s entitlement to recognise the party’s National Chairman and National Secretary.

The ADC-PCC maintained that the judgment raised important legal questions about the subsequent proceedings before Justice Lifu, which its lawyers had placed before the Court of Appeal.

The campaign council also called on the National Judicial Council (NJC) to investigate the reassignment, the formal protest submitted to the Chief Judge and Justice Lifu’s handling of the earlier deregistration case.

Invoking Nigeria’s political history, it warned judicial officers against decisions capable of deepening political crises, recalling the controversies surrounding the judiciary before the collapse of the First and Second Republics.

Turning its attention to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the ADC-PCC challenged the party to confront its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, on the political field rather than resort to alleged judicial manoeuvres.

“The hallowed chambers of our courts must not be turned into arenas for political combat. Nigerians must see those who would rather fight their opponent through court manoeuvres than meet him at the ballot box.

“Atiku remains our candidate. The law is on his side, not sentiment. We will defend that position before the Court of Appeal and keep the record before Nigerians. Their right to choose their president must never become a bargaining chip in anyone’s struggle for power,” Shaibu added.

World.title: WMO warns of ‘off the charts’ climate extremes as El Niño strengthens
World.content:
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has warned that a very strong El Niño event could intensify global heat and extreme weather into 2027.

Raising concerns about the impact on vulnerable communities, food production and water supplies.

In its latest State of the Climate Update 2026, released on 9 November, the United Nations agency said the world was experiencing a prolonged period of exceptional temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels.



The report found that the past 12 years have each been the warmest on record.

Global average surface temperatures between January and September 2026 reached approximately 1.47°C above the pre-industrial average.

The WMO expects this figure to rise further by the end of the year as El Niño strengthens.



WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said the state of the global climate in 2026 gave new meaning to the phrase “off the charts”.

She warned that hundreds of millions of people had already experienced extreme heat this year, while heatwaves, tropical cyclones and heavy rainfall were increasing the risks facing communities.

Southern Africa faces warmer conditions

The warning is particularly relevant to southern Africa, where the WMO’s seasonal outlook points to warmer-than-normal conditions between November 2026 and January 2027.



The forecast, based on climate models from several international partners, including the South African Weather Service (SAWS), also points to shifts in rainfall patterns across different parts of the world.

For southern Africa, the warmer outlook raises concerns about the potential effects of prolonged heat on water resources, agriculture and communities already vulnerable to extreme weather.

However, the outlook does not mean that every part of the region will experience the same rainfall conditions.



El Niño can bring different impacts to different areas.

Why El Niño is raising concerns

El Niño is a natural climate pattern that develops when sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean become warmer than normal.

The WMO said the current event has been strengthening since August and is expected to reach record strength by December.



The world’s oceans absorb about 90% of the excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases, making ocean warming a major factor in the changing global climate.

The WMO also reported that global sea levels reached their highest point in the satellite record in 2026, while ocean heat continued to rise.

Extreme weather puts lives and livelihoods at risk

The agency warned that El Niño could increase the risks of heatwaves, droughts and heavy rainfall well into 2027.



These conditions could affect food production, worsen water shortages and increase health risks, particularly in communities that depend on rain-fed agriculture.

The WMO also highlighted the human cost of recent extreme weather events.

The WMO said its 2026 update uses data available up to September and does not yet capture the latest impacts of the strengthening El Niño.



Its final State of the Global Climate 2026 report is expected in March 2027

World.title: Does having a degree really give you a better chance of finding a job in South Africa?
World.content:
Does having a degree better your chances of employment in SA? Image: canva

Having a university degree does not guarantee employment in South Africa, but the latest labour market figures show that graduates have a considerably better chance of finding a job than people with lower levels of education.

Statistics South Africa’s (Stats SA) Quarterly Labour Force Survey for the third quarter of 2026 found that graduates recorded an unemployment rate of 11.9%.

This was significantly lower than the national unemployment rate of 33.7%, as well as the rate recorded among people without a matric qualification.



The figures highlight the continued importance of education and formal qualifications in a country where millions of people are struggling to find a job.

Graduates have a much better chance of finding a job

According to Stats SA, the unemployment rate among graduates stood at 11.9% between July and September 2026.

This represented a decrease of 0.6 of a percentage point compared with the previous quarter.

In comparison, people without a matric qualification recorded an unemployment rate of 39.2%, which remained unchanged from the second quarter.

The survey also found that unemployment rates among people with matric and those with less than matric were higher than the national average.

People with other tertiary qualifications, alongside university graduates, recorded unemployment rates below the national figure.



The findings suggest that further education can improve a person’s position in the labour market, although a qualification does not remove the risk of unemployment.

Unemployment increased across all education levels

Despite the advantage recorded by graduates, the latest figures also show that having a qualification does not make South Africans immune to the country’s employment challenges.

Stats SA found that unemployment increased year-on-year across all education levels.

The national unemployment rate rose from 31.9% in the third quarter of 2025 to 33.7% in the same quarter of 2026.

The number of unemployed people also increased by 571 000 over the year, reaching approximately 8.58 million.

The latest figures also show that 16.84 million people were employed in South Africa during the third quarter of 2026.

Although this represented an increase of 101 000 compared with the previous quarter, the number of unemployed people also increased by 97 000.

The broader picture remains challenging, particularly for people entering the labour market for the first time.

Stats SA also recorded a youth unemployment rate of 63.6% among people aged 15 to 24.

Furthermore, 35.7% of young people in this age group were not in employment, education or training.

World.title: Helen Zille’s one-word response to Malema’s lawsuit threat
World.content:
DA federal chairperson Helen Zille has responded with a one-word "No" to Julius Malema's legal demands following his threat to sue her over allegations involving Johannesburg. Image: Facebook/Helen Zille

Democratic Alliance (DA) federal chairperson Helen Zille has refused to back down after Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) leader Julius Malema threatened to sue her over allegations involving the City of Johannesburg.

Zille responded with a single word on a Facebook post on Tuesday, 10 November.

“No.”

She shared the response alongside a letter of demand from Malema’s lawyers, who have given her until Wednesday, 11 November, to retract her statements and apologise publicly.



WHY IS MALEMA THREATENING TO SUE ZILLE?

The dispute stems from an eNCA interview on Sunday, 8 November, during which Zille accused Malema of influencing decisions in Johannesburg while ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba was mayor.

Zille claimed Mashaba relied on the EFF’s support to remain in office and allowed Malema to dictate major decisions.

She alleged that Malema influenced decisions involving City Power and a municipal fleet tender to benefit himself and companies linked to him.



Zille also claimed Mashaba appointed former police deputy national commissioner Shadrack Sibiya to head the city’s anti-corruption unit on Malema’s instructions.

Malema has rejected the allegations as false and defamatory.

MALEMA GIVES ZILLE DEADLINE

In a letter dated 9 November, Malema’s lawyers, England Slabbert Attorneys, demanded that Zille withdraw her statements and issue a public apology.



They want her to publish the apology across her social media platforms and distribute it to media organisations.

The lawyers also demanded that Zille submit the proposed apology for their approval and provide a written undertaking not to repeat the allegations.

They warned that failure to comply by close of business on Wednesday could result in legal proceedings, including a damages claim and an interdict preventing further publication of the statements.



Zille’s one-word response signals that she does not intend to comply with the demands.

The dispute comes as political parties negotiate coalition agreements following the local government elections.

Zille is the DA’s Johannesburg mayoral candidate, while ActionSA has indicated that it is willing to negotiate with the party but will not support her appointment as mayor.

World.title: Maswanganyi sends strong message to Kaizer Chiefs fans
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates midfielder Patrick Maswanganyi has urged Kaizer Chiefs supporters to be patient with the club’s young players.

This comes after Mduduzi Shabalala missed a penalty during Amakhosi‘s 2-1 victory over Siwelele in the Carling Knockout Cup this past weekend.

Speaking to the South African Football Journalists Association (SAFJA), Tito called on supporters to show youngsters more understanding, particularly when they struggle to perform.



“My thing is for the fans to take it easy, especially on young players that are coming in,” said Maswanganyi.

“Sometimes you see Mfundo Vilakazi playing, trying his best and not doing well in the game, and then you see lots of fans speaking badly about a player who is very young for the team that they support.”

Tito wants Chiefs youngsters to shine

Maswanganyi believes young players need time to develop and that negative criticism from supporters does little to help their progress.

“And it’s not really good because that player is someone who still needs to grow. I think there are also senior players in the team who would take it better than the younger players.

“I watched the Kaizer Chiefs [vs Siwelele] and I saw Mdu miss a penalty. And I watched the fans signal for him to go out. Minutes later, he creates another penalty for the team, the team gets back into the game.

“Just imagine if they would have taken him out at that time. Probably they would never have even got a goal. They would have lost the game.”



Tito on Chiefs handling of Shabba

The former Pirates star further pleaded with supporters to encourage young players rather than tear them down when things do not go their way.

“But for me, it’s for the fans to take it easy on the younger players. The more they encourage them, the more they will do for the team. And we need these players to grow better, to improve because these are our future, they’re going to go to the Bafana Bafana team,” Tito said on Chiefs youngsters.

“So we need to protect them, we need to show them love, and we need to appreciate them. Somewhere outside the country, they show lots of love for young players, but in South Africa, it’s very difficult to show love to those players.”

World.title: Have Kaizer Chiefs found their star to help them win the Carling Knockout?
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs seem to have found their perfect defensive pairing with Rushwin Dortley returning to the squad.

Against Siwelele, the two again started alongside each other and guided Chiefs to the last four of the Carling Knockout Cup.

Rushwin gives Kaizer Chiefs quality at the back

“When we play with fresh, we have a left footer so it’s also good for us. Rushwin is good with his head, so he helps us.

“But for me as a coach I prefer to have many options than not have options.

“So, for the moment Miguel is suspended and when he comes back, we’ll have many options in our defence.”



Kaizer Chiefs have often struggled defensively and last season, they had Brandon Petersen to thank. The experienced keeper has looked shaky this campaign and with Dortley returning. the Amakhosi backline has stabilised somewhat.

If they are to win the Carling KO, Dortley will be key.

World.title: eNCA Coalition Builder | Battle for Joburg, who has the numbers?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The City of Johannesburg is the biggest prize in the coalition negotiations, but getting the numbers to govern will require political parties to sit down and work together.

The DA emerged as the largest party in the City of Gold, securing 91 seats in the 270-seat council.

But a majority in the Johannesburg Council needs 136 seats to govern.

This leaves the parties with no other choice but to turn to other political parties for support.

eNCA election analyst Wayne Sussman breaks down the numbers as he explores three possible coalition options.

If the DA chooses to go into coalition with the ANC, which has secured 63 seats, that number combined will add up to a comfortable majority of 154 seats in council.

READ | Pressure mounts on Joburg Water amid ongoing supply disruptions

Another possibility is a partnership between the DA and ActionSA, which secured 43 seats. That number adds up to 134 seats.

But if another party like the IFP, which secured seven seats, agrees it would push the coalition to 141 seats, giving it a viable majority.

The third scenario Sussman plays around with is a coalition that excludes the DA.

He sketches the possibility of the ANC and ActionSA potentially joining with other smaller parties such as the MK Party, Rise Mzansi and the PA.

A multi-party coalition along those lines also has enough seats to get above the magic number of 136.

World.title: Number Of The Day | US$200 Billion | 10 November 2026
World.content:
The World's Most Valuable Technology Is Becoming Its Biggest Security Challenge

Artificial intelligence has turned advanced computer chips into strategic assets. The Nvidia controversy reveals how easily the boundaries between commercial ambition, political power and national security can become blurred.

For decades, the world's most strategically important resources were commonly associated with oil, minerals and industrial infrastructure. Artificial intelligence is changing that calculation. Advanced semiconductors have become essential to economic competitiveness, military capability and technological leadership, placing

the companies that manufacture them at the centre of an increasingly consequential international contest.

Nvidia's extraordinary rise illustrates the scale of this transformation. Its processors power sophisticated AI systems, making the company a critical supplier to technology businesses developing everything from automated services to advanced computing infrastructure. Yet that influence also creates vulnerability. When a company becomes central to an entire technological ecosystem, questions about its leadership, commercial relationships and security arrangements can have consequences extending far beyond its shareholders.

When Commercial Technology Becomes A Strategic Asset

The competition between the United States and China over advanced semiconductors is not simply a disagreement about international trade. Both countries recognise that access to powerful computing infrastructure can influence economic productivity, technological independence and national defence capabilities.

Washington has consequently imposed restrictions on exports of certain advanced chips to China. These measures are intended to limit access to technologies considered strategically sensitive, but they also present an enormous commercial challenge for American manufacturers. China represents a significant potential market, while export controls can restrict the ability of companies to serve customers and expand their businesses.

The disagreement exposes two competing approaches to technological leadership. One argues that allowing international customers to purchase American technology helps preserve US commercial influence and discourages competitors from developing alternatives. The other maintains that providing advanced hardware to geopolitical rivals could accelerate capabilities that eventually challenge American economic and security interests.

Neither argument eliminates the underlying tension. A company may benefit financially from broader market access while its government sees that same access as a strategic vulnerability.

The Complications Of An International Supply Chain

The challenge becomes more complicated when advanced technology moves through international networks of distributors, cloud-computing businesses and data centres. The destination of a physical chip is not necessarily the only consideration. Access to computing power can also be provided through infrastructure located outside the country where its eventual users operate.

This distinction has become relevant to scrutiny surrounding Nvidia's commercial relationships. Reporting has raised allegations about whether companies linked to Singapore-based Megaspeed International helped facilitate access to Nvidia chips by Chinese businesses. These allegations remain subject to investigation and must not be confused with established findings of wrongdoing.

The wider policy question is significant regardless of the outcome. If restrictions focus primarily on where equipment is shipped, regulators must also consider whether access to the technology can be obtained through services or infrastructure elsewhere. Effective controls require an understanding of entire technology supply chains, not merely the initial transaction.

Why Corporate Governance Is Now A Security Issue

The controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has intensified scrutiny of the relationship between corporate leadership and national security. Huang has acknowledged marital infidelity, while allegations that a businesswoman associated with him was involved in Chinese intelligence activity are being investigated.

Nvidia's board has initiated an independent inquiry and has stated that it has no reason to believe company secrets or national-security information were compromised. That distinction matters: the existence of an investigation does not establish that espionage occurred.

Nevertheless, the situation demonstrates why corporate governance cannot be separated from security considerations when a business controls strategically important technology. Effective leadership oversight, conflict-of-interest procedures and independent board scrutiny become essential safeguards for shareholders, employees and customers.

These responsibilities grow more important when the founder of a company is also its public face, principal strategist and most influential representative in government negotiations.

The Financial Cost Of Uncertainty

Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on 9 November 2026, according to Reuters, removing approximately US$190 billion from the company's market capitalisation. The episode of Number of the Day broadcast on 10 November described the loss as US$200 billion.

Such movements show how quickly financial markets can reassess perceived risks. Investors must consider not only potential legal or regulatory consequences, but also leadership continuity, reputational damage and the possibility of restrictions affecting future business opportunities.

A decline in market capitalisation does not mean an equivalent sum has disappeared from the company's bank accounts. It reflects a reduction in the market's valuation of its outstanding shares, driven by changing prices and investor expectations.

The Next Test Of Technological Power

Artificial intelligence is creating opportunities for companies and countries capable of developing sophisticated computing infrastructure. It is also introducing difficult questions about who controls that infrastructure, who can access it and how commercial interests should be balanced against national-security concerns.

Those questions will persist long after any individual investigation concludes. For businesses, policymakers and investors, the central challenge is no longer simply how quickly artificial intelligence can advance. It is whether the institutions governing that advancement can keep pace.

References

· eNCA, Number of the Day, 10 November 2026, featuring Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd.

· Reuters, 9 November 2026: Reporting on Nvidia's market-value decline and the shareholder lawsuit.

· Associated Press, 9 November 2026: Reporting on Nvidia's independent investigation and company response.

· Reuters, 10 November 2026: Reporting on allegations concerning Nvidia chip shipments to China.
