World.title: Peru Court Bars Mayors’ Backdoor Re-Election
World.content:
PERU · ELECTIONS

Peru’s top electoral court has ruled that a former mayor who ran as first councillor (the top council seat on a party’s list) cannot take the mayor’s job again. The National Jury of Elections (JNE), the body that proclaims election winners, said on 6 November 2026 that such candidates will not be proclaimed.

The best-known case is Rafael López Aliaga, Lima’s ex-mayor, who ran as first councillor on his party’s list. The JNE’s president, Roberto Burneo, defended the ruling on Tuesday, 10 November.

What the Court Decided

The ruling is Resolution 4557-2026-JNE, dated Monday, 2 November. LP Derecho, a Peruvian legal news site, hosts the copy of the text linked here.

It rests on Article 194 of Peru’s Constitution, which says mayors cannot be re-elected immediately. Peruvians vote for closed party lists (fixed rankings of candidates), so the first councillor normally steps in when the mayoral candidate drops out, and the court says an ex-mayor cannot use that route.

The court still lets ex-mayors run as councillors. Yessica Clavijo, the JNE’s secretary general, said such a person “no será proclamado ni recibirá las credenciales”, Andina, the state news agency, reported on 6 November.

How Far the Ruling Reaches

The JNE reviewed 427 local proclamations and ordered six councils corrected, Andina reported on 6 November. Six corrections in 427 proclamations is a small share of the first batch.

In each, the next eligible councillor on the list is proclaimed mayor. Caretas, a Peruvian news magazine, reported on 7 November that a second batch of more than 600 cases is being prepared, out of about 1,900 proclamations.

What Burneo Said

El Comercio, a Lima daily, reported on 10 November that Burneo told journalists: “Nunca íbamos a avalar una reelección encubierta”, meaning the court would never endorse a covert re-election. He said no route, including the councillor slot or succession, can lead to an immediate second term.

The Lima Question

Luis Rubio, the mayoral candidate of the conservative Renovación Popular party, withdrew, leaving López Aliaga as first councillor, Caretas reported. The local panel for Lima’s centre makes the final proclamation, and Caretas and El Comercio report that Jeanette Alonzo, second on the list, would then take the job.

The JNE has not announced that outcome. See our earlier report on the credential dispute, the vote count in Lima and our coverage of his lead claim; more is on our Peru hub.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online market where users bet real money on outcomes, López Aliaga trades at about 11% to be Lima’s next mayor, as of 12:29 p.m. ET on Tuesday, 10 November. Two other candidates, Francis Allison and Carlos Bruce, trade at 1.1% each, in a market with about US$797,000 traded.

Prices on Polymarket are real-money bets. These prices are bets, not polls or official results.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The date and wording of Lima’s proclamation are not confirmed. We also do not know whether López Aliaga or his party will challenge the rule, although Andina noted that JNE rulings are final and not open to appeal.

What It Means for Readers

Residents and firms dealing with Lima’s city hall may face a different mayor than the ex-mayor on the list. Watch the proclamation date.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Peru’s electoral court decide?

Former mayors who ran as first councillor cannot be proclaimed mayor for the next term. The next eligible councillor on the list takes the job instead.

Does the ruling cover Lima?

It sets the rule for all councils. Lima’s final proclamation is still pending, and the JNE has not named a new mayor for the capital.

Can ex-mayors still run as councillors?

Yes. Running as councillor stays allowed, but it cannot lead to the mayor’s office.

World.title: At Least 7 Killed in Kenya Road Crew Ambush
World.content:
Trucks and cars on the Nairobi-Nakuru highway, the road the Rironi-Naivasha upgrade is meant to relieve. File photo. (Photo: Njiruh, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0)

Attackers ambushed a road-works party in north-eastern Kenya on Tuesday, killing at least seven people in Mandera County, which borders Somalia. The first police toll was two police reservists and five construction workers, and later reports add an eighth victim.

At least seven killed on Tuesday morning in Hagarso, Mandera County, north-eastern Kenya; later reports say eight.

First police toll: two National Police Reservists (part-time reserve officers) and five civilian construction workers on the Arabiya-Lafey Road.

Suspected Al-Shabaab (Somalia-based militant group) attack; the attackers’ identity and number are not established.

A multi-agency security team is pursuing the attackers; the area was calm afterwards.

As of 10 November 2026, 17:30 GMT

What Happened

The attack came on the morning of Tuesday 10 November 2026 in the Hagarso area of Mandera County, a remote part of Kenya’s north-east. The group was supervising construction work on the Arabiya-Lafey Road, in a county that borders Somalia.

Two of the dead were National Police Reservists, part-time reserve officers who support the regular police. The other five were civilian construction workers.

Who Is Al-Shabaab

Al-Shabaab is a militant group based in Somalia and linked to al-Qaeda. It fights Somalia’s government.

Police have said only that it is suspected in this attack. No claim of responsibility is known.

Farmland and a road in the Rift Valley near Iten, Kenya, 2016. The attack took place in Mandera County, in the country’s north-east. photo. Farmland and homes in the Rift Valley seen from Iten, western Kenya, 2016. Photo: Appleslerp, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

Why It Matters

The road is in a remote county on the Somali border, and the project had been running since April, according to the county police commander. The attack came after months of work on the road.

No official statistic on attacks on road crews was available to us. The wider threat therefore cannot be measured here.

Our Kenya security explainer sets out the wider picture. Our report on Uganda’s troops leaving Somalia covers the neighbouring front.

What Is Not Known

Police have not given a motive, the number or identity of the attackers, any arrests or the victims’ names. The contractor on the road project is also not known, and no claim by Al-Shabaab is known.

Later reports put the toll at eight, adding the driver of the escort vehicle. Police first said seven, and we have no final official toll.

What It Means for You

For US readers, travellers and aid workers, there is no change we can confirm to conditions in Kenya. Check the official US State Department travel advisory for Kenya before any trip.

Anyone with staff or projects in Mandera County should follow guidance from local police and their own security advisers. We have no information on other routes.

What to Watch Next

Watch for police statements on arrests, the attackers’ identity and any claim of responsibility. Confirmation of the victims’ names and of the final toll will also matter.

Watch also whether work on the Arabiya-Lafey Road continues. More reporting is on our Kenya hub.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is suspected of the Mandera attack?

Police say security agencies suspect Al-Shabaab, but the attackers’ identity and number are not established. No claim of responsibility is known.

How many people died in the ambush?

Police first reported seven dead: two National Police Reservists and five construction workers. Later reports add an eighth victim, the escort vehicle’s driver.

Where did the ambush happen?

In the Hagarso area of Mandera County, north-eastern Kenya, a county that borders Somalia. The group was supervising works on the Arabiya-Lafey Road.

World.title: Venezuela Unions Rally for Pay and Vote Date

What the Marchers Demand

The coalition wants pay, year-end bonuses and pensions that keep their buying power, El Nacional reports. It told Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela’s acting president, to pay “aguinaldos, salario y pensión con poder adquisitivo.”

The Pay Gap in Numbers

The legal minimum wage stays at 130 bolívares a month, about US$0.14 at the Central Bank of Venezuela (BCV) official rate of 899.27 bolívares per US$ for 10 November 2026. That is the official rate, not the parallel market rate.

On 30 April Rodríguez announced a “minimum integral income” of US$240 a month and a US$70 monthly pension, as Infobae (30 April) reported. The government did not say how much of the sum is salary, and bonuses do not count for social benefits.

A Bigger Strike Follows on 16 November

Separately, unions of university, health and education workers agreed on 5 November to a 12-hour national stoppage on Monday, 16 November, El Diario (5 November) reported. Gregorio Afonso, president of APUCV, the Central University of Venezuela’s professors’ association, said the government never answered a list of demands delivered on 13 October.

The Government’s Position

None of the reports opened says the government has answered this protest. On 8 October Rodríguez said results of the “mesas de consenso laboral y social,” talks with labour and social groups, would come in November, Bloomberg Línea (8 October) reported.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a crypto-based betting platform, lists a market on whether a Venezuelan presidential election is scheduled by a given date. As of 12:30 ET (17:30 UTC) on 10 November, it priced 0.9% for 30 November, 8.5% for 31 December 2026 and 32.0% for 31 March 2027, with US$677,574 traded.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

No outlet opened gave a turnout figure or a march route, and none reported a government reply to this protest. See also our report on the May wage increase.

What It Means for Readers

Because bonuses do not count for social benefits, as Infobae reported, only a higher base salary would raise severance and pensions. Investors and travellers should watch the 16 November stoppage and the promised November labour announcement.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who called the 10 November protest?

The Coalición Sindical, a group defending workers, retirees and pensioners, called it, with coordinator Carlos Salazar named by Contrapunto. It set 10:00 a.m. at Plaza Caracas.

What is Venezuela’s minimum wage?

The legal minimum wage is 130 bolívares a month, about US$0.14 at the BCV rate of 899.27 per US$ on 10 November 2026. The government pays a US$240 “minimum integral income” mostly through bonuses.

What happens on 16 November?

University, health and education unions plan a 12-hour national stoppage that Monday. They say the government ignored the demands delivered at Miraflores, the presidential palace, on 13 October.

Sources: Central Bank of Venezuela, official rate (10 November 2026); El Nacional (10 November 2026); Contrapunto (9 November 2026); El Diario (5 November 2026); Infobae (30 April 2026); Bloomberg Línea (8 October 2026); Polymarket (10 November 2026).

World.title: Earthquake Off Guatemala Felt in Capital
World.content:
GUATEMALA · EARTHQUAKE

An undersea earthquake shook Guatemala’s Pacific coast at 08:54 local time on Tuesday, 10 November (14:54 UTC). The US Geological Survey (USGS), the American government’s seismology agency, measured it at magnitude 5.6.

Guatemalan and other agencies reported different magnitudes, because each calculates the size its own way. Early accounts mentioned no damage or injuries.

Key Facts When Tuesday, 10 November, at 08:54 local time (14:54 UTC).

Size Agencies range from magnitude 5.2 to 5.8; the reviewed US figure is 5.6.

Where Pacific Ocean, 43 km (27 miles) south of Puerto San José, a port town.

Depth Estimates run from 10 to 35 km below the sea floor.

Damage No damage or injuries appeared in early accounts.

Every agency gave a slightly different number, but the early picture is of a strong shake without reported harm.

What the Agencies Measured

The USGS, in its reviewed solution, recorded moment magnitude 5.6 (a standard measure of energy released) at 35 km depth. Half an hour later, at 15:23 UTC, it logged a magnitude 4.8 aftershock 34 km south of the same town.

INSIVUMEH, Guatemala’s national seismology and volcano institute, put the first shock at a preliminary 5.2 and 30 km deep, according to Infobae, a regional news site, and Prensa Libre, a Guatemalan daily. Publinews, a Guatemalan outlet, reported a second quake at 09:24 local time, magnitude 5.0 and 45 km deep, close to the time of the USGS aftershock.

El Salvador’s environment ministry estimated 5.4, Infobae reported. The Mexican site Quadratín and the Colombian daily El Tiempo reported 5.8 and a 10 km depth, with the 10 km depth attributed to Guatemala’s geological service.

Where It Was Felt

The USGS received 15 reports through its “Did You Feel It?” public survey and gave the quake its lowest, green, alert level for likely damage. Prensa Libre reported that internet users felt it in Chimaltenango, Mixco and Villa Canales.

Guatemala City seen from a distance, with forested hills behind (file photo). Photo: Rene Hernandez / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0).

Infobae said El Salvador felt it lightly to moderately, and El Tiempo reported that some public buildings in Guatemala City were evacuated as a precaution. CONRED, Guatemala’s national disaster agency, urged calm and reminded people of its 119 emergency line, Infobae reported.

What Is Not Known

We could not find a reading from Mexico’s national seismology service, and the reports do not name the source of the 5.8 magnitude. Damage checks may also still be under way.

What It Means for Readers

Visitors and expats in Guatemala should expect possible aftershocks and follow CONRED guidance. Our Antigua guide lists what to check on the ground, and our report on Bolivia’s earthquakes covers a recent quake in the region.

More coverage is in our Guatemala hub, which we update as agencies publish final figures.

Frequently Asked Questions

How strong was the Guatemala earthquake?

The USGS measured magnitude 5.6. Guatemala’s institute reported a preliminary 5.2, and some media reported 5.8.

Was there any damage?

Early accounts reported no damage or injuries. Some public buildings in Guatemala City were evacuated as a precaution.

Where was the epicentre?

The USGS placed it in the Pacific, 43 km south of Puerto San José. Reports citing Guatemala’s geological service said about 70 km south of Sipacate, a Pacific coast town in Escuintla.

Sources: USGS, magnitude 5.6 event, 10 November 2026; USGS, magnitude 4.8 event, 10 November 2026; Infobae, 10 November 2026; Prensa Libre, 10 November 2026; Publinews, 10 November 2026; El Tiempo, 10 November 2026; Quadratín, 10 November 2026.

World.title: Spain Says EU Majority Backs Venezuela Relief
World.content:
VENEZUELA · EU SANCTIONS

José Manuel Albares, Spain’s foreign minister, said on Tuesday, 10 November 2026, that most EU governments now back lifting EU sanctions on Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela’s acting president. He spoke to reporters in Brussels.

The claim is not yet confirmed by the Council of the EU, the body of member governments that adopts sanctions. It matters because the EU would be re-engaging with the Caracas leadership that Washington already deals with directly since US forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January.

Key Facts What Spain’s foreign minister says most EU governments back lifting sanctions on Venezuela’s acting president.

When Tuesday, 10 November 2026, in Brussels.

Sanctions Asset freeze and EU travel ban on Delcy Rodríguez, listed since at least 2018.

Status No Council of the EU decision has been announced; the whole regime runs to 10 January 2027.

Next Spain says EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas is talking to the remaining doubters.

A Spanish proposal to ease EU pressure on Caracas has gathered support, according to Madrid, but nothing is decided.

What Albares Said in Brussels

Albares said it “makes no sense” for Rodríguez to keep the EU restrictive measures, according to EFE, Spain’s national news agency (translated from Spanish). He added that Kallas, the EU’s High Representative for foreign policy, shares Spain’s view.

Kallas is talking to the few countries that still have doubts, EFE reported on 10 November. Albares also said Rodríguez has visited several European countries “with total normality” since February, and that the EU should engage directly, as the United States does.

The Sanctions Already in Force

Rodríguez has been on the EU’s Venezuela sanctions list since at least 2018, and the EU General Court, the bloc’s second-highest court, dismissed her challenge, as reported on 23 July 2021 by European Sanctions, a specialist blog. The EU measures carry an asset freeze and a travel ban for listed people.

On 15 December 2025 the Council renewed the regime for one year, until 10 January 2027, with 69 individuals listed. The Council cited persistent actions undermining democracy and the rule of law, according to its draft decision of 9 December 2025.

How We Got Here

Rodríguez was sworn in as acting president before Venezuela’s National Assembly on Monday, 5 January 2026, after US forces captured Nicolás Maduro on 3 January, the French news agency AFP reported. Spain asked the EU to lift her sanctions in February, after the Assembly passed an amnesty law for political prisoners, EFE said.

On 23 February 2026 Kallas said she would propose lifting the travel ban and asset freeze on Rodríguez, according to EUnews, a Brussels outlet. She also announced a broader discussion of a new approach to Caracas.

For earlier context, see our reports on Spanish court scrutiny of Rodríguez, the offer by opposition leader María Corina Machado to meet her and the new judge in the Maduro case. More is on our Venezuela hub.

The Palacio Federal Legislativo in Caracas, seat of Venezuela’s National Assembly, in 2011 (file photo). Photo: Javiermartinez76 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0).

What Is Not Known

We have not confirmed that a majority of the 27 governments back the move, because Albares gave no count and EFE named no countries. We also found no Council date for a decision, and no public Council statement on Albares’s remarks.

The reports do not name the meeting where he spoke, beyond Brussels. It is also unclear whether the 10 January 2027 renewal would be used to change her listing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Delcy Rodríguez?

She is Venezuela’s acting president. She was sworn in before the National Assembly on 5 January 2026, two days after the United States captured Nicolás Maduro.

Has the EU lifted the sanctions on her?

Not yet. We found no announced decision by the Council of the EU as of 10 November 2026.

When do the EU Venezuela sanctions expire?

The Council renewed them on 15 December 2025 until 10 January 2027. It can change them earlier by a new decision.

Sources: Council of the EU, document 15890/25 (draft renewal decision), 9 December 2025; Council of the EU renewal release, 15 December 2025 (copy on cgc.org.cy); EFE via Infobae, 10 November 2026; El Nacional, 10 November 2026; EUnews, 23 February 2026; AFP via Teletica, 5 January 2026; European Sanctions, 23 July 2021.

World.title: Venezuela Opposition Wants Lawful Court Vote
World.content:
VENEZUELA · POLITICS

Venezuelan opposition politician Delsa Solórzano said on Tuesday, 10 November, that the choice of new Supreme Court magistrates must follow the Constitution. Monitoreamos, a Venezuelan news site, reported her remarks from a radio interview.

It matters because the Supreme Court (the Tribunal Supremo de Justicia, or TSJ) is being renewed seat by seat. It is Venezuela’s highest court.

Key Facts Who Delsa Solórzano, an opposition politician who presides over a political party, spoke on Tuesday, 10 November.

What She asked that choosing Supreme Court magistrates follow the Constitution and guarantee independence.

Vacancies 32 magistrate seats on the Supreme Court are to be filled.

Next The Judicial Nominations Committee is scheduled to interview candidates from 16 to 27 November.

Date The Venezuelan National Assembly is scheduled to receive the shortlist on Friday, 11 December.

An opposition leader wants the court picks to follow the rulebook while the nominating committee works through its list of candidates.

What Solórzano Said

Monitoreamos reported that she spoke on Tuesday, 10 November, on the radio programme A Tiempo on Unión Radio. She said the opposition had been told it would get an independent electoral authority and court: “A nosotros nos han prometido un nuevo Consejo Nacional Electoral y TSJ independientes” (translated: “We have been promised an independent new National Electoral Council and Supreme Court”).

She also ruled out applying for a judicial post, Monitoreamos reported. She said it would be unethical because she presides over a political party.

On 4 September, El Nacional, a Venezuelan news outlet, reported that she had already asked for transparency. She said candidates must meet the constitutional requirements, and that any citizen should be able to challenge a candidate before the National Assembly.

What the Constitution Requires

Article 264 of the Constitution gives magistrates a single 12-year term. Candidates apply to the Judicial Nominations Committee, which, after hearing public opinion, draws up a first shortlist for Citizen Power, a separate branch of the Venezuelan state.

Citizen Power makes a second shortlist, and the National Assembly makes the final choice. Article 264 also lets citizens file reasoned objections against any nominee, and Article 263 sets the entry rules, such as Venezuelan birth and 15 years as a lawyer, law professor or judge.

Caracas, Venezuela’s capital, in a file photo. Photo: Wilfredor / Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

Where the Selection Stands

El Diario, a Venezuelan news outlet, reported that a reform of the court law was published in Official Gazette 7,074 of 15 September. It orders a new 23-member committee of 11 deputies and 12 civil society representatives to start the renewal of all principal and substitute magistrates.

The call for applications ran from Wednesday, 28 October, to Wednesday, 11 November, and covers 32 magistrates, according to Finanzas Digital, a Venezuelan business site. El Diario reported 83 applicants by 29 October, and that an earlier round in May and June was annulled.

A schedule published by El Diario on 24 October sets interviews for Monday, 16 November, to Friday, 27 November. Citizen Power would review names on 8 to 10 December, and the shortlist would reach the Assembly on 11 December.

Earlier Rio Times reports cover the opening of the race for court seats, the expansion of the court to 32 magistrates and a report on a new court by December. They trace how the renewal has moved since September.

What Is Not Known

Only one outlet has so far reported Solórzano’s 10 November interview, and we have not heard the recording. One report gives 11 November as the application deadline and another schedule gives 12 November, and the final applicant count is unpublished.

What It Means for Readers

Investors and companies with Venezuelan disputes or contracts will face whichever court is chosen in December. The outcome will show whether the selection follows the constitutional steps that Solórzano and other critics demand.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Delsa Solórzano?

She is an opposition politician who presides over a political party in Venezuela. She said on 10 November that she will not seek a judicial post.

How many Supreme Court seats are being filled?

The call for applications covers 32 magistrates of the Supreme Court. It also covers other posts, such as the head of the judicial school.

What does the Constitution say about choosing magistrates?

Article 264 sets a single 12-year term and a path through the nominations committee, Citizen Power and the National Assembly. Citizens may object to nominees.

Sources: Constitution of Venezuela, articles 263 to 265, text read 10 November 2026; Monitoreamos, 10 November 2026; El Nacional, 4 September 2026; El Diario, 17 September 2026; El Diario, 24 October 2026; El Diario, 30 October 2026; Finanzas Digital, 27 October 2026.

World.title: Bukele Posts Video of Haiti Gang House Razed
World.content:
EL SALVADOR · HAITI

Key Facts —Who. Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele; 400 Mawozo, a Haitian gang led by Wilson Joseph, nicknamed Lanmò San Jou. Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Haiti story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time. —What. A house linked to the gang leader was destroyed; Bukele posted a video and claimed credit. —Where. Haiti. Reports do not agree on the exact site. —When. Raid reportedly on Sunday 8 November; Bukele posted on Tuesday 10 November 2026. —As of 10 November 2026, 17:00 GMT. No authority has given a casualty toll or damage assessment.

A house tied to one of Haiti’s most feared gang bosses has been destroyed, and El Salvador’s president wants the world to see it. On Tuesday 10 November 2026, Nayib Bukele posted a video and said his promise was kept: the home of gang leader Lanmò San Jou was gone.

The 400 Mawozo gang kidnapped 16 Americans and one Canadian in 2021, so news about it draws attention in the United States. El Salvador has troops inside Haiti, and Bukele has promised to hit the gangs that attacked them.

What We Know

Bukele posted the video on X and other social media with a short message in Spanish. In our translation, it reads: “We kept our promise. We destroyed the house of Lanmò San Jou and the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo gang.”

He added that most people there fled without trying to fight, and called them cowards. Lanmò San Jou is the nickname of Wilson Joseph, who leads 400 Mawozo, a gang that controls areas east of Port-au-Prince.

The operation reportedly took place on Sunday 8 November, carried out by Haitian police with support from Salvadoran soldiers. A Salvadoran government representative confirmed it to The Associated Press, a US news agency.

Reports say Joseph was not at the house and was not captured. The video alone cannot show how much was destroyed or who was affected.

On Friday 6 November, Bukele had answered a user on X, the social network, who shared images of a house attributed to the gang leader. He asked for its exact address and said it would be destroyed.

A market area in Port-au-Prince in a 2015 file photograph taken by Yoni Rubin (CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons).

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Bukele (Haiti) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the 400 Mawozo Gang Matters

In October 2021, 400 Mawozo kidnapped 17 missionaries, 16 Americans and one Canadian, near Port-au-Prince, Haiti’s capital. They belonged to Christian Aid Ministries, a Christian charity based in Ohio.

Five hostages were freed earlier, and the last 12 escaped after about two months. The case drew wide attention in the United States.

El Salvador has sent at least 2,500 personnel to Haiti since October, reports say. Their presence rests on an agreement with the Haitian government, and only some belong to the Gang Suppression Force, a UN-backed multinational mission.

The deployment followed 18 October 2026, when four Salvadoran aviation technicians vanished in an ambush. El Salvador’s government says they are alive, while Joseph has said they are dead, and neither claim is independently confirmed.

What Is Not Known

No authority has given a casualty toll, though unconfirmed reports speak of up to 20 armed men killed. There is no independent damage assessment, and a Haitian outlet withdrew an earlier report on the destruction.

It is unclear who owned the house or how often Joseph used it. Nothing beyond Bukele’s own account shows that any “headquarters” was hit. We have not independently verified where or when the video was filmed.

The fate of the four missing technicians is also unconfirmed. We covered the search in El Salvador’s rescue push.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

The claim will be judged less on a video than on whether gangs lose ground in the coming weeks. No report says how 400 Mawozo has responded, so further violence cannot be ruled out.

Joseph has also asked the UN for mediation, as we covered in Joseph’s letter to the UN. For US readers, the clearest link is the 2021 kidnapping of Americans by this same gang.

A claim is not the same as a confirmed result. We treat Bukele’s account as his own statement until independent information appears.

For background on the gang’s reach, see our report on a Dominican Republic probe tied to 400 Mawozo and our Haiti hub. For now, the clearest facts are a video, a promise and a claim.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Bukele say happened in Haiti?

He said the house of gang leader Lanmò San Jou and the 400 Mawozo headquarters were destroyed. This is his account, and reports differ on what else was hit. No independent report confirms the damage.

Who is Lanmò San Jou?

Lanmò San Jou is the nickname of Wilson Joseph, leader of the Haitian gang 400 Mawozo. Reports say he was not at the house and was not captured.

Why does 400 Mawozo matter to Americans?

The gang kidnapped 17 missionaries, 16 Americans and one Canadian, from an Ohio-based charity in October 2021. Five were freed earlier and twelve escaped after about two months.

Who carried out the raid?

Reports say Haitian police carried it out with Salvadoran military support, reportedly on Sunday 8 November. Bukele posted his video on Tuesday 10 November 2026.

Sources Source: Nayib Bukele’s public posts, 10 November 2026; Christian Aid Ministries statements (2021); Rio Times reporting.
