World.title: Rubio says ‘no need’ to attack Iran as diplomacy gathers pace
World.content:
TEHRAN: Top US diplomat Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that he saw no need to attack Iran again, as diplomatic efforts to end the war gathered steam and Tehran urged Washington to accept its demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Hours after President Donald Trump said he saw “positive momentum” toward resolving the eight-month war, Rubio said the United States’ squeezing of Iran’s economy made further attacks unnecessary.

“The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations,” the secretary of state said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. “That’s what I told our allies here today.”

Iran’s efforts to blockade Hormuz, the major exit route for Gulf energy shipments, have sent oil prices soaring — a major factor in the humbling of Trump’s Republicans in last week’s midterm elections.

Washington has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and in August announced what it called an “economic asphyxiation” campaign aimed at financially strangling Iran, already battered by years of sanctions.

Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called for greater efforts to end the conflict, while warning of the economic damage of an ongoing impasse.

“We need to move beyond the ‘no war, no peace’ stalemate, which is causing deep economic pain for our countries,” he said in Paris.

“We must see an all-out diplomatic effort to end this conflict, prevent a nuclear Iran and the threats it poses around the world, and get the Strait of Hormuz properly reopened.”

Washington has appeared to taper down its threats of renewed strikes after the Republicans’ defeat, and even Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — who launched the war alongside Trump and recently lobbied to “forever eliminate the existential threat of Iran” — appeared to recognize the shifting diplomatic reality.

“In the very near future, we’re going to be confronted by international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the preservation of this terror regime that seeks to annihilate us,” he said on Tuesday.

- ‘Address Iran’s demands’ -

Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table.

Iran’s demands have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing its assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US blockade of its ports.

“The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA news agency.

“The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran’s demands and conditions — which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table.”

Meanwhile, vessels continue to come under attack in and around the strait.

The Emirati state oil company ADNOC said on Tuesday that one of its vessels had “sustained damage following an attack in the UAE’s territorial waters,” while the British maritime agency UKMTO reported a tanker was “struck by an unknown projectile” off the Omani coast.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said that three oil tankers were on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, though it was unclear whether they were referring to the same ships.

- US ‘more flexible’ after midterms -

On Monday, after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House, Trump said that the US was “locked and loaded,” but further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo.”

“We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” he wrote on social media.

Qatar and Pakistan are leading diplomatic efforts to resolve the war, which began with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in late February.

Qatari foreign ministry official Ibrahim Al-Hashmi confirmed there had been progress in the negotiations.

“The mediator is making a persistent and earnest effort to bridge the gaps between the parties’ positions,” he told a regular briefing, adding: “We remain hopeful.”

Iranian political analyst Ali Bigdeli said the outcome of the US elections appeared to have “somewhat reduced Iran’s flexibility, whereas the Americans have become more flexible.”

He noted that the Iranian terms were “demanding and heavy for the United States to accept” but added that “engaging in direct talks” could bear results.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei urged Washington to “surrender” to the Iranian demands.

“The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND,” he posted on X.

World.title: Six held over deadly Turkiye steel blast that killed 17
World.content:
ALIAGA, Turkiye: Six people were arrested overnight after a huge blast at a steel plant near the western city of Izmir killed 17 workers, with grieving families waiting Tuesday to receive their loved ones’ bodies for burial.

Onlookers said Monday’s massive explosion felt like “an earthquake” when it ripped through the HABAS steel factory in Aliaga, a district 60 kilometers (37 miles) north of Izmir known for shipbreaking and heavy industry.

Police have so far detained six people in connection with the incident, with Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar warning “the number could rise.”

The deadly blast at one of Turkiye’s top steel producers also left around a dozen people injured, at least one in critical condition.

Outside the forensic institute in Aliaga, bereaved family members told AFP they had been waiting all night for confirmation that their loved ones had been identified so they could be laid to rest.

“We have been here since yesterday, we’re waiting for the DNA results. Since the bodies are in a condition that makes visual identification impossible, the identification process is carried out through DNA analysis,” said Turgut Dilek, saying his nephew Ozcan Efe was one of the dead.

Meanwhile, there was no word on the fate of a 40-year-old man who set himself alight outside the factory on Monday evening and was taken to hospital with severe injuries, IHA news agency said.

The man had worked for years as a truck driver at the factory, IHA said, without mention of earlier reports that his brother had died in the blast.

Workers’ groups have accused HABAS of a chequered safety record, and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Monday vowed that investigators would get to the bottom of what happened.

Turkiye’s pro-Kurdish DEM party — which said late Monday “not a single party must go unpunished” at the factory — sent a delegation to visit the families and the injured on Tuesday led by its co-chair Tulay Hatimogullari.

Jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, Erdogan’s chief political rival, also demanded accountability.

“Workplace deaths are not fate. The causes of the accident must be fully established, and anyone who was negligent or at fault must be held accountable,” he wrote on X.



Izmir governor Suleyman Elban said the explosion happened during “a boiler replacement operation.”

Speaking to AFP, 52-year-old worker Yasin Cetiner said the crane had dropped a huge container of molten steel.

“The crane rope broke, and as a result, about 120 tons of liquid steel fell onto the furnace ... (which) caused a hydrogen explosion when it came into contact with the water beneath it,” he said.

Contacted by AFP, HABAS declined to respond to any questions.



On Monday, police detained two representatives of a workers’ collective outside Aliaga hospital while trying to make a statement about workplace safety issues, a spokesman told AFP.

Workers’ groups have called a protest in Aliaga on Tuesday, saying: “STOP this hell of exploitation in which dozens of our comrades have died and hundreds were left disabled because of employers’ greed!“

World.title: Iraq, BP discusses increasing oil industry investments
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and officials from British Petroleum (BP) met on Tuesday in London to discuss prospects for a strategic partnership between Iraq and the British firm.

The two sides discussed strategies to increase investments in the energy sector, serve mutual interests, and support the Iraqi economy, according to a statement released by al-Mandalawi’s media office.

The meeting addressed plans to broaden the scope of oil and gas exploration across Iraq, employ modern technologies for development, and create a promising investment climate.

BP is developing four oilfields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, a move that aligns with larger attempts to broaden the base of foreign partners.

The development plan intends to achieve a significant increase in oil and gas output in the next few years.

According to Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, the plan aims to reach an oil production level of 450,000 barrels per day, in addition to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.

The four oilfields—Kirkuk, Bai Hassan, Jambur, and Khabbaz—are key oil assets in northern Iraq and represent an important part of the government’s plans to increase production.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company to develop the oil fields, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

Khudair affirmed that BP is a strategic partner in the oil and gas sectors. He noted that working together as a team will support the project’s implementation and help address any obstacles that may arise during the development phases.

World.title: Iraqi FM participates in Paris Peace Forum
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein has arrived in the French capital to participate in the 9th annual Paris Peace Forum, where he will engage in discussions on key regional and international challenges.

Hussein said in a statement on Tuesday that he will exchange perspectives and explore approaches to de-escalate tensions and advance peace and stability.

The Iraqi foreign minister will present Iraq’s perspective on regional developments, emphasizing the importance of dialogue, diplomacy, and political solutions in addressing crises.

Hussein is expected to meet with international officials and partners to discuss strategies to strengthen cooperation, enhance coordination, and advance shared interests.

According to Hussein, Iraq will remain committed to constructive international efforts to promote regional stability, peace, and sustainable partnerships.

Participating as a featured speaker, Hussein addressed Iraq’s central role in mediating regional conflicts. He confirmed that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi recently conducted an unannounced visit to Tehran.

Al-Zaidi’s secret trip to Iran is part of Baghdad’s active diplomatic bridge to narrow differences, reduce escalating tensions, and work toward ending the ongoing conflict between Iran and the United States.

Hussein stressed that Iraq uses its good connections with the US and strong relationships with Iran to promote peace.

To reduce tension, Hussein had earlier suggested that a regional group of foreign ministers travel to both Washington and Tehran.

During his discussions at the forum, Hussein cautioned world leaders about the dire security and economic consequences of the conflict. He noted that the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz and regional unrest directly harm Iraq’s financial status and threaten worldwide energy, oil, and raw material markets.

World.title: Plane carrying Iran’s football team barred from landing in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq barred on Tuesday a plane carrying Iran’s national football team from landing at Basra International Airport, turning the aircraft back due to strict compliance with US sanctions on Iranian airlines.

The Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority (ICAA) denied landing rights to the flight carrying the Iranian team.

The aircraft successfully altered its course and landed at Abadan Airport in Iran. An official from the Iranian consulate confirmed that the team would continue their journey to Basra by road.

Along with Iraq, Lebanon, and Palestine, the Iranian national team was headed to Basra to participate in a four-nation competition.

Iraq could not risk violating the harsh secondary penalties imposed by Washington, according to an Iraqi civil aviation official.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned earlier that any foreign airports or service providers that assist sanctioned Iranian carriers will be excluded from the US currency system, a step aimed at grounding Iran’s civil fleet worldwide.

After Iraq previously secured a limited humanitarian exemption allowing specific civilian flights from Iran to Najaf, other major Iraqi airports in Basra, Erbil, and Baghdad remain restricted to avoid US financial penalties.

World.title: Excelerate Energy to launch Iraq’s first LNG import terminal in Q2 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is seeing rapid on-site progress, as efforts continue to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq.

Excelerate Energy, the US-based firm implementing the project, anticipates an increase in the pace of work in the upcoming weeks, with construction activities on terminal facilities set to ramp up.

The company aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the military conflict in the region have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026.

The delays forced Excelerate Energy to redirect its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), the Excelerate Acadia, to Jordan for a period of nine months.

To avoid disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed in the region, eliminating the need for such a vessel to transit the strait.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express, according to Attaqa news.

Excelerate Energy indicated that it is attempting to set up the import of LNG from Gulf countries, a remark that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: Iraq, Qatar to lay optical fiber cable linking Singapore to Italy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ooredoo Group’s international connectivity arm, OFN, has partnered with Iraq’s iQ Networks and the Iraqi Telecommunications and Post Company (ITPC) to build a massive terrestrial and subsea digital corridor connecting Asia, the Gulf, and Europe.

Ooredoo is developing a project that includes a 2,000-kilometer subsea system. This system will feature up to 24 fiber pairs and can support a capacity of up to 720 terabits per second.

The project will link seven Gulf and regional markets, which are Qatar, Iraq, Oman, the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait.

This dual-arrangement bridges the subsea Gulf network with an overland path heading north through Iraq toward Turkey and Europe, bypassing traditional maritime chokepoints like the Red Sea.

The fiber-optic connection that will bridge Singapore in East Asia to Italy in southern Europe is expected to be completed by 2027.

The Iraqi Ministry of Communications announced that it signed a deal with Qatar to establish the terrestrial and submarine fiber-optic connection.

World.title: Germany’s Isar Aerospace eyes overtaking Elon Musk’s SpaceX
World.content:
Frankfurt – The head of Germany’s Isar Aerospace voiced hope Tuesday that the company could one day overtake Elon Musk’s SpaceX to become the world’s premier space launch company.

Daniel Metzler, who founded the company with two fellow students in 2018, pointed to a huge backlog of launch orders, helped by European military clients.

“SpaceX was founded in 2002. Back then I was playing with Pokemon cards,” he said. “Looking at what could happen in the next 18 years, I wouldn’t rule out us being further ahead than SpaceX.”

Isar became in September the first privately financed European company to get a rocket into orbit.

Europe is betting that competition between Isar and other players such as Rocket Factory Augsburg will bring down the price of satellite launches.

This would help ensure affordable access to space for sectors ranging from telecommunications to defence, independent of entities such as SpaceX, the sector leader valued at $1.9 trillion (1.7 trillion euros).

Speaking at a conference organised by the SZ newspaper, Metzler said Isar had already come a long way, noting that SpaceX needed four attempts to get into orbit compared to Isar’s two.

Capacity rather than demand was now the big bottleneck, Metzler added.

He said the company was 15-times oversubscribed for 2028 launches as European governments now preferred European providers to put their defence satellites up as opposed to firms overseas.

“There’s 14 customers for every rocket that we have to disappoint,” he said.

“About 18 months ago 85 percent of inquiries were commercial and 15 percent were military, and that ratio has since flipped,” he added.

Isar is working on developing reusable rockets to boost capacity and bring launch costs down, hoping to catch up with SpaceX’s reusable Falcon 9 rocket.

“Already with our next launch, for which we are currently finalising the launch vehicle, we will be taking initial measurements to assess the re-entry of the rocket’s first stage,” he said.

“Over the next three or four flights, we also plan to start flying hardware specifically designed for reusability.”

Asked if Isar could one day be valued at 100 billion euros, Metzler said “people massively underestimate the potential of space”.

“To be honest, I reckon the figure is much higher, but then people would be even more convinced that I’m completely mad.”

World.title: Bulgaria motorway pileup kills 11, dozens injured
World.content:
Sofia – Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU.

Crashes in thick fog snared dozens of vehicles heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas.

An estimated 50 cars and trucks were involved in the accident near the city of Yambol, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency, as government officials rushed to the scene.

Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles.

“The toll at this point is 11 dead and 48 injured,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters.

Radev was meeting EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, who is on a visit to Bulgaria, but the prime minister cancelled his official events scheduled for later Tuesday.

The injured were transported to hospitals in nearby cities. The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams.

Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures.

Victims blame the Balkan nation’s high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system.

– Stricter penalties –

Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed “deepest condolences” to the victims and their families in a post on X.

European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was “deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning”.

A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 — down five percent from the previous year and 27 percent lower than in 2019.

The EU in 2019 introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 percent by 2030.

A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains “one of the world’s safest regions for road travel”, the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target.

The report said that just five of the EU’s 27 countries — including Bulgaria — were on track to meet the target.

However, “despite their progress since 2019, Bulgaria and Romania, alongside Croatia, continue to have the highest fatality rates in the EU when measuring deaths per million inhabitants”, the report said.

In 2023, Bulgaria’s parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs.

The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record.

Bulgaria’s busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts.

But Bulgaria’s status as the EU’s poorest member state also plays a role, with around half of the cars registered more than 20 years old.

World.title: Zelensky holds air defence, energy security talks with Nordic leaders
World.content:
Copenhagen – Denmark on Tuesday hosted security talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Nordic leaders, as Copenhagen announced it was donating $720 million in military aid.

TV images showed Zelensky’s plane landing in Copenhagen and the meetings came as direct Ukraine-Russia talks, under US mediation, began in Abu Dhabi.

Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said his country was planning to donate 4.8 billion kroner ($720 million) in military aid to Ukraine.

Another 150 million kroner would be donated to Ukraine’s energy sector, Rasmussen told reporters.

“I am proud to welcome President Zelensky and the Nordic leaders to Denmark. The Ukrainians’ fight for a free Ukraine and a free Europe continues,” Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said in a statement.

A large police presence could be seen outside the Danish prime minister’s office in Copenhagen, according to an AFP correspondent.

Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and his Norwegian and Finnish counterparts Jonas Gahr Store and Petteri Orpo were also to travel to Copenhagen.

The Nordic countries are key supporters of Ukraine and Zelensky travelled to Oslo at the end of October to meet with American envoys.

After that meeting, Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb had a 90-minute phone call with Russia’s President Vladimir Putin — which Frederiksen slammed and said had not been coordinated with Nordic neighbours.

Stubb said the talk with Putin had been “frank and substantive”.

“Almost five years after the full-scale invasion, the rain of bombs targeting civilians, relief centres, and water and heating plants continues. That is why we must stand firm,” Frederiksen said Tuesday.

Copenhagen police announced that they would increase security for coming days. They have introduced a ban on the use of drones over the capital until November 12.

World.content:
SRINAGAR: Kargil shut down Tuesday and political groups in Leh threatened an agitation after Ladakh announced Dec 4 elections to its eight autonomous hill development councils, rejecting demands to avoid holding the polls during the harsh winter months.

Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) co-chairperson Sajjad Kargili criticised the administration, saying around 25% of Ladakhâs population would be outside the region during the elections. âWhat we are seeing is continuous flow of orders and notifications by UT govt. We are witnessing bureaucracy raj,â he said.

Kundra countered that those who had demanded an end to bureaucratic rule were opposing elections. âThe elected councils will prepare next yearâs budget.





If the elections are delayed, they may lose valuable time in the budget preparation. The timing of the elections is very important,â he said.

World.title: CPCB explains why official AQI is capped at 500 despite private apps showing higher readings
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Central Pollution Control Board on Tuesday defended its air quality monitoring methodology, explaining why official AQI readings are capped at 500 even as private monitoring apps reported levels as high as 1,800 in Delhi after Diwali.

The clarification came amid questions over the wide disparity between government data and readings displayed by private air quality monitoring platforms.

The CPCB said the 500-point ceiling was an intentional feature of the National Air Quality Index (NAQI), consistent with international practices. It explained that readings beyond 500 would not change the health advisory, as all such levels fall under the 'Severe' category.



"The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a tool for effective communication of air quality status to the people in terms that are easy to understand. AQI is an indicative scale designed to convey the likely health implications of prevailing air quality conditions. The AQI category along with the associated health statement is more significant than the corresponding AQI value within that category," the board said in a statement.





The CPCB said the official index uses scientifically validated 24-hour rolling averages to assess sustained exposure to pollutants. Private apps, on the other hand, often capture hourly fluctuations through low-cost sensors, which may show sharp spikes in pollution levels.

According to the board, the NAQI has six categories - 'Good', 'Satisfactory', 'Moderately Polluted', 'Poor', 'Very Poor' and 'Severe' - within a scale of 0 to 500.

It said an AQI reading of 500 or above indicates broadly similar health risks and therefore does not warrant a separate category.

"Beyond this level the AQI remains in the 'Severe' category and extrapolation of the index would not alter the assigned health impact category. The capping at 500 is thus a design feature of the index, as has been evolved in 2015 methodology of NAQI in line with the prevailing international practice including US EPA AQI scale," it added.

CPCB also said private apps could report higher readings during brief pollution spikes but show lower figures when pollution levels subsequently decline.

"It is generally perceived that private apps show higher AQI. This may hold during short peaks, when hourly values rise sharply. However, when concentrations fall, such apps show lower AQI than the NAQI, since the NAQI continues to reflect the exposure of the preceding 24 hours," it said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"This has also been evident in Delhi post Diwali firecrackers bursting event. The NAQI thus provides a consistent and reliable indication of the likely health impacts of sustained exposure to pollutants, which is the scientifically relevant measure for public health advisories," it further said.

The clarification came as social media posts showing screenshots of private air quality apps reporting AQI levels between 1,500 and 1,800 in Delhi on Diwali night, while CPCB's official readings remained below 400.

World.title: Chemical-free crackers: RSS chief extols traditional Diwali practices as severe pollution chokes Delhi

NEW DELHI: Public sector power major NTPC Ltd emerged as the only company to submit applications in the second round of the Rs 37,500 crore coal and lignite gasification incentive scheme.The coal ministry said in a statement on Tuesday that NTPC has proposed to produce urea and methanol dimethyl ether (DME). In the first round, the ministry had received seven applications from five companies, including NTPC, Adani Enterprises, Gallantt Ispat, Shyam Sel and Power, and Talcher Fertilisers.The Union Cabinet had approved the scheme in May to accelerate the development of surface coal and lignite gasification projects in the country. Coal ministry officials said the aim is to encourage wider industry participation, attract investments and accelerate the adoption of coal gasification technologies to achieve the national target of 100 million tonnes of gasification capacity by 2030.With no private sector company participating in the second round, experts said financial incentives need to be complemented with credit guarantees, proven technologies and standardised modular designs to build a pipeline of commercially viable projects.âViability-gap funding alone may not be sufficient. Even commercially sound projects can struggle to secure financing because lenders remain cautious about technology, construction and operating risks, particularly where domestic commercial precedents are limited,â said Atanu Mukherjee, CEO, Dastur Energy, which has been closely involved in coal gasification policy and commercialisation discussions with the coal ministry and Niti Aayog.âOne important step would be to complement existing incentives with a govt-supported partial credit guarantee mechanism. By sharing a defined portion of lenders' risks, while ensuring rigorous project appraisal and adequate sponsor participation, such a framework could improve access to debt, lower financing costs and encourage greater private investment,â he added.Mukherjee also emphasised the need to assimilate proven technologies and adapt them to India's high-ash coal, while standardising modular designs to enable faster and wider commercial implementation.âEach successful project should build operating experience, reduce risks and improve the economics of subsequent investments. Ultimately, the success of Indiaâs coal gasification programme should be measured not simply by the number of applications or projects sanctioned, but by how effectively we create a fleet of commercially successful projects that can attract investment and be replicated at progressively lower costs and risks,â Mukherjee said.Govt on Tuesday also launched the third round of the scheme, providing another opportunity for public and private sector companies to submit proposals for setting up gasification projects.

World.title: COP31 presidency pitches for global 35-by-35 electrification pledge, India may skip signing this informal commitment
World.content:
The world leaders and climate activists will gather in Antalya from November 9 to 20 for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, or COP31.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The UN climate conference (COP31) presidency in Antalya, Turkiye, on Tuesday pitched for â35-by-35â global electrification pledge that aims to raise electricityâs share of the worldâs final energy consumption from about 23 percent today to 35 percent by 2035, asking countries and businesses to join the initiative that will help the world in transitioning away from fossil fuels.Since the global electrification goal is a voluntary initiative of the COP31 presidency as a key headline issue of the current conference, many countries, including India, may not formally join this move being taken outside the formal negotiation process, even as most of them welcomed it in principle.India, which has already taken a big leap towards renewable energy and is gradually moving towards increasing its clean energy footprint, is expected to flag that the voluntary initiatives under the Presidency Action Agenda should remain separate from negotiations and that uniform global targets must respect national circumstances. In India, electricity currently makes up roughly 22 percent of the countryâs total final energy consumption, with the remainder dominated by oil, coal and natural gas.The COP31 global electrification pledge, designed to usher in the âage of electricityâ, will be achieved through electrifying transport, buildings and industry and will support global efforts to enhance energy security, expand energy access and reduce costs and emissions.The â35-by-35â target is based on the International Energy Agency (IEA) and International Renewable Energy Agencyâs (IRENA) analysis of what is needed to keep the world on a pathway consistent with limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.âThe COP31 Presidency is determined to chart a path forward and use the annual UN summit to build momentum. We are bringing everyone together to support each other and build collective momentum. The age of electricity is taking shape â and COP31 will be remembered as the moment we flicked the switch,â said COP31 President Murat Kurum while making the pitch for the â35-by-35â target.India, meanwhile, reaffirmed its commitment to climate multilateralism and the principles of equity and Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), calling for a fair, equitable and ambitious outcome at COP31.Delivering Indiaâs opening statement at COP31, Union environment secretary Narendra Bhooshan reiterated the countryâs commitment to âcontributing its fair share to global climate action while pursuing the development and well-being of its peopleâ.On the critical issue of climate finance, he emphasised that public finance from developed countries remains central to catalysing climate action in developing countries and strengthening adaptation finance flows to address their vulnerabilities.
